articles_hidden.title: PRMT5 licenses AARS1-dependent histone lactylation to amplify microglial glycolytic reprogramming in neuropathic pain
articles_hidden.authors: Honghao Song, Tong Hua, Lei Peng, Xiaoyi Fan, Yutong Yang, Rongrong Fan, Li Cao, Chaofeng Han, Hongbin Yuan
articles_hidden.abstract: Neuropathic pain involves persistent metabolic and transcriptional remodeling in spinal microglia, but the mechanisms linking these processes remain unclear. Time-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing after chronic constriction injury identified increased PRMT5 expression in glycolysis-enriched activated microglia. Microglia-specific Prmt5 deletion or pharmacological inhibition reduced glycolytic remodeling and pain hypersensitivity. Mechanistically, PRMT5 associated with alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1 (AARS1), promoted AARS1-associated symmetric dimethylation and nuclear accumulation, and supported AARS1-dependent H3K18la and H4K12la. Disrupting AARS1 nuclear localization impaired histone lactylation and glycolytic responses. The pathway was validated in primary microglia, spinal microglia, and female mice. Chromatin profiling linked injury-associated histone lactylation to glycolytic gene programs. Finally, biomimetic siPRMT5 nanoparticles preferentially reduced PRMT5 in spinal microglia and alleviated pain hypersensitivity. These findings identify a PRMT5–AARS1–histone lactylation pathway that reinforces microglial glycolytic reprogramming and represents a potential therapeutic target for neuropathic pain.

articles_hidden.title: Contrasting spatial homogeneity in atmospheric ice-nucleating particles from local to synoptic scales
articles_hidden.authors: Ruichen Zhou, Drew Juergensen, Kelton Ayars, Carson Hume, Kevin Barry, Oren Dutton, Gavin McMeeking, Ezra Levin, Anna Hodshire, Leah Gibson, Ethan Emerson, Paul J. DeMott, Jessie M. Creamean, Sonia Kreidenweis, Russell Perkins
articles_hidden.abstract: Ice-nucleating particles (INPs) play a critical role in regulating glaciation and precipitation formation in mixed-phase cloud (containing liquid and ice), yet their spatial variability across different scales remains poorly constrained. In this study, coordinated immersion freezing INP measurements from multiple sites during two campaigns in an urban–rural environment and complex mountainous terrain were used to investigate INP spatial distributions at tens-of-kilometer scales. At these scales, INP concentrations were generally spatially homogeneous during each campaign, indicating that single-site measurements can often represent surrounding areas. Occasional spatial differences were observed at warm activation temperatures (higher than −20 °C), ascribed to variations in heat-labile, likely biological INPs. Extending the analysis to the synoptic scale across multiple campaigns, warm-temperature INPs showed greater site-to-site differences, suggesting stronger influences from local or regional sources. In contrast, INPs active at colder temperatures showed much stronger spatial similarity between two inland continental sites separated by 800 km, revealing a broader regional coherence in this INP population. This was also observed at the coastal site, but only under continental air mass influence; the similarity weakened under marine air masses. These results suggest that cold-temperature INPs may reflect a broader INP background over continents such as that contributed by windblown dust. Our findings provide direct observational constraints on the representativeness of single-site INP measurements, which can help inform the strategy for representing variations in INP populations in atmospheric models.

articles_hidden.title: Precursor-engineered lithiation kinetics enable low-temperature synthesis of Li–Ni–O positive electrode materials
articles_hidden.authors: Chenguang Shi, Junyi Yao, Elliot Brim, Sooyeon Hwang, Xiaowen Zhan, Yaobin Xu, Hongyu Wang, Changlian Wen, Dali Yang, Lu Ma, Sizhan Liu, Hui Zhong, Jianming Bai, Gihan Kwon, Molleigh Preefer, Dennis Nordlund, Jordi Cabana, Ryan M. Richards, Jie Xiao, Feng Lin
articles_hidden.abstract: High-nickel cathodes provide high capacity in lithium-ion batteries; however, their slow lithiation reactions require a prolonged high-temperature hold during synthesis which is directly responsible for high manufacturing cost. Here, we report that the precursor morphology and crystallinity can be engineered to regulate the nucleation and growth of the layered phase at temperatures as low as 575 °C. We use nanosheets of NiO and Ni(OH) 2 with high specific surface areas to maximize the contact area between Li and Ni precursors and to shorten Li + diffusion lengths. Highly crystalline NiO seeds early and uniform layered phase nucleation at low temperatures. Preheating Ni(OH) 2 to NiO at 300 °C maintains the large surface area and yields a higher layered fraction with limited lamellae coarsening. Preheating at 500 °C produces more crystalline NiO seeds that promote the synchronous Ni oxidation and cation ordering upon layered phase formation to deliver higher discharge capacity and better rate capability than conventionally synthesized LiNiO 2 . In contrast, along the hydroxide-based route, in situ generated Li 2 CO 3 disrupts wetting and hampers lithiation, ultimately trapping lithium within a disordered rocksalt intermediate. This work demonstrates that precursor morphology, crystallinity, and processing temperature control lithiation kinetics, providing broad guidance for energy-efficient synthesizing advanced oxide battery cathodes.

articles_hidden.title: Immunometabolic basis of glutamine supplementation as a potential host-directed therapy for tuberculosis
articles_hidden.authors: Qingkui Jiang, Ryan J. Dikdan, Yunping Qiu, Wei Wang, Joseph J. Bulatowicz, Victor C. Agbara, Irwin J. Kurland, Luke Fritzky, Youssef Sabha, Dongfang Liu, Sanjay Tyagi, Selvakumar Subbian, Karl Drlica, Lanbo Shi
articles_hidden.abstract: Undernutrition is the leading risk factor for tuberculosis susceptibility, severity, and poor treatment outcome. Nutritional immunology and immunometabolism frame how nutrient availability and metabolism shape host defense against Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( Mtb ) infection. By integrating targeted metabolomics and transcriptional profiling in a murine tuberculosis model, we defined immunometabolic programs underlying the transition from acute to chronic infection. Immune control of Mtb during acute infection was accompanied by robust activation of immune and metabolic programs, including mTORC1-associated signaling, glutaminolysis, glycolysis, arginine metabolism, and serine one-carbon metabolism, thereby highlighting the importance of amino acid metabolism and mitochondrial function in antimicrobial immunity. In contrast, chronic infection was characterized by reduced immune activation and mTORC1-associated signaling, increased branched-chain amino acid catabolism, and altered amino acid profiles, with leucine and glutamine among the discriminating metabolites. These findings suggest that reduced glutamine availability during chronic infection may increase reliance on leucine oxidative catabolism to sustain mitochondrial metabolism during nutrient stress, potentially limiting leucine availability for mTORC1-associated anabolic metabolism and immune activation. Oral glutamine supplementation restored amino acid homeostasis, including lung leucine abundance, enhanced mTORC1-associated signaling and central metabolic programs, moderately reduced bacterial burden and lung pathology, and mitigated infection-associated wasting. Reanalysis of published human metabolomics datasets further demonstrated reduced circulating glutamine levels during progression to active tuberculosis, supporting conservation of glutamine metabolic dysregulation across host species. Collectively, our findings identify a potential glutamine–leucine metabolic axis linking nutrient availability with immunometabolic competence and provide a mechanistic rationale for evaluating glutamine supplementation as a host-directed strategy for tuberculosis.

articles_hidden.title: Ketamine’s antidepressant mechanisms extend beyond NMDA receptor blockade
articles_hidden.authors: Kenji Hashimoto

articles_hidden.title: Single-cell genomics reveals genome streamlining and functional traits in dominant uncultured marine protists
articles_hidden.authors: David López-Escardó, Aleix Obiol, Guillem Marimon, Xabier López-Alforja, Dolors Vaqué, Irene Forn, Ramiro Logares, Sheree Yau, Òscar Fornas, Manuel Martínez-García, Ramon Massana
articles_hidden.abstract: Marine protists are key players in marine ecosystems, yet a large fraction, particularly among the smallest taxa, belongs to uncultured lineages lacking genomic data, limiting our understanding of their ecology and evolution. Beyond determining their gene repertoires, genomic information is essential to reveal how genomes are organized. Features such as genome size, GC content, and structural gene architecture represent physical constraints that shape evolutionary fitness and adaptability in marine environments. Here, we present a genomic catalog of 147 marine picoplanktonic protist species, greatly expanding the genomic representation of uncultured and ecologically relevant lineages through a single-cell approach. This dataset enables refined phylogenomic placement of previously uncharacterized marine eukaryotes, including abundant marine protistan players as well as a few species belonging to novel or poorly known groups that are crucial for resolving deep questions in eukaryotic evolution. We uncover pronounced genome streamlining in ecologically successful lineages, coupled with extensive, mostly lineage-specific functional adaptations. At a broader scale, we identify functional traits enriched independently across several marine eukaryotic lineages, including genes involved in complex carbohydrate degradation in heterotrophic organisms and the presence of polyketide synthases. Together, these results provide a framework for investigating the genomic drivers and molecular mechanisms behind the ecological success of marine eukaryotic microbes.

articles_hidden.title: A two-dimensional molecular gearbox operated in a crystalline solid
articles_hidden.authors: Hikaru Yamamoto, Rempei Ando, Ayana Sato-Tomita, Masahiro Kuramochi, Motohiro Mizuno, Hiroshi Sekiguchi, Mikhail Tsitsvero, Andrey Lyalin, Tetsuya Taketsugu, Hajime Ito, Mingoo Jin
articles_hidden.abstract: Since the earliest artificial gears, parallel gearbox systems based on intermeshing two-dimensional (2D) networks of multiple gear units have served a fundamental role in macroscale mechanical devices through the correlated mechanical motion of multiple gears. However, the realization of molecular-level 2D gearbox machinery with correlated motion among multiple units remains highly challenging. Here, we report a molecular-level 2D gearbox in a crystal, formed through the supramolecular assembly of an Au(I)-complex rotor with tripodal triptycene and triadamantyl phosphine (Ad 3 P) rotators, connected via an ethynyl–Au(I) unit. Upon heating, the rotators within a 2D hexagonal gear network exhibit 120° site-exchange rotational motion in a correlated manner, as revealed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction (XRD), 2 H solid-state (SS) NMR spectroscopy, and time-resolved variable-temperature XRD measurements. In addition, density functional theory calculations provide insight into the energetic preference for correlated motion within the gear-network. This 2D intermolecular gearbox in the crystalline state represents a supramolecular platform in which the intermolecular gearing motion has a large impact on the bulk crystal, which could provide a bridge between molecular-level mechanical properties and macroscale SS physical functions.

articles_hidden.title: Gammaherpesvirus infection drives genotype-dependent virus-specific T cell responses in the CNS prior to autoimmune neuroinflammation
articles_hidden.authors: Katherine J. Sessions, Emily A. Nelson, Rae-Ling Lee, Courtney M. Waytashek, Senjuti Sengupta, Theresa L. Montgomery, Edward J. Usherwood, Anthony J. Filiano, Dimitry N. Krementsov
articles_hidden.abstract: Infection with the gammaherpesvirus Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) is the strongest environmental risk factor for multiple sclerosis (MS). This risk is driven by poor immune control of viral replication, which is genetically determined. Clonally expanded CD8 T cells are abundant in MS lesions, and some recognize EBV antigens. We previously demonstrated that host genetic variation regulates immune control of the homologous B cell–tropic murine gammaherpesvirus, MHV-68. Here, we investigated how gammaherpesvirus infection and host genotype shape central nervous system (CNS) T cell responses, before and after induction of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE). Chronic infection alone was sufficient to promote a marked accumulation of CX3CR1+KLRG1+ effector CD8 T cells and CX3CR1+KLRG1+ cytotoxic-like T helper cells in the CNS of MHV-68-susceptible C57BL/6 mice. T cells localized to brain border regions and throughout the CNS parenchyma. MHC tetramer analysis demonstrated that CNS-infiltrating T cells were specific for viral antigens, and viral DNA was detectable in CNS-infiltrating leukocytes during early and chronic infection. EAE further amplified cytotoxic T cell accumulation in the CNS of MHV-68-infected C57BL/6 mice. However, CNS T cell infiltration was highly attenuated in genetically divergent wild-derived PWD/PhJ mice, which control MHV-68 more effectively, but not in MHV-68-susceptible 129S1/SvImJ mice. Surprisingly, chronic MHV-68 infection modestly delayed EAE onset in C57BL/6 mice, an effect reversed by B cell depletion. Together with emerging human studies, our results suggest that host genetic variation contributes to poor control of EBV in MS, promoting virus-specific cytotoxic T cell accumulation in the CNS and immune reprogramming both before and during autoimmune neuroinflammation.

articles_hidden.title: Harnessing lattice distortion for point-defect self-healing in multi-principal element alloys
articles_hidden.authors: Bozhao Zhang, Kaihui Xun, Pengfei Guan, Robert O. Ritchie, Jun Ding
articles_hidden.abstract: Multi-principal element alloys are promising structural materials for nuclear, aerospace, and fusion applications, yet their accelerated discovery is limited by the prohibitive cost of evaluating point-defect transport and self-healing behavior across vast compositional spaces. Here, we establish local lattice distortion (LLD), an intrinsic feature of chemically complex alloys, as a predictive and universal descriptor for vacancy–interstitial diffusivity convergence. We develop and validate a high-fidelity machine-learning interatomic potential based on the moment tensor potential formalism for body-centered-cubic Zr–Ti–Nb alloys, enabling accurate large-scale simulations of defect energetics and migration. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal a robust inverse correlation between LLD and the activation energy disparity between vacancies and interstitials. This relationship is further validated in face-centered-cubic V–Co–Ni and Ni–Pd systems, demonstrating transferability across distinct chemistries and crystal structures. LLD-induced narrowing of vacancy–interstitial mobility differences promotes Frenkel pair recombination and defect self-healing. Mechanistically, vacancy diffusion is governed by the energy barrier associated with bond-length compression at the saddle state, together with statistical sampling of low-barrier jumps mediated by oversized atoms. These findings establish lattice distortion as a powerful, physically grounded design lever that links nanoscale disorder to point-defect self-healing, offering a practical pathway for the accelerated discovery of next-generation structural materials for extreme environments.

articles_hidden.title: A zero-one law for one-shot system identification
articles_hidden.authors: Nicolas Boullé, Diana Halikias, Samuel E. Otto, Alex Townsend
articles_hidden.abstract: Can a model be identified from one experiment? We study analytic systems that are linearly parameterized by a combination of prescribed dictionary terms, such as partial differential operators and dynamical systems. For a single input-response pair, recovery is possible exactly when the evaluated dictionary terms are linearly independent. We prove a sharp zero-one law: either no input uniquely determines the coefficients, or almost every random input sampled from a nondegenerate Gaussian measure does. This dichotomy reduces one-shot system identification to a question about degenerate inputs and provides an a posteriori certificate in the noiseless setting. Numerical examples recover dynamical systems, nonlinear partial differential equations, and structured matrix families from single trajectory data, while also detecting when an extra probe is necessary.

articles_hidden.title: The microbial world of male reproduction
articles_hidden.authors: Madangchanok Imchen, Rupinder Kaur, Seth R. Bordenstein
articles_hidden.abstract: The last decade has brought renewed interest to microbial influences on host biology, yet the roles of microbes in host reproductive biology are underappreciated and often defined by a profound maternal bias. This perspective synthesizes emerging evidence across the tree of life to highlight the paternal microbiome as an overlooked driver of fitness, reproductive output, and intergenerational health, impacting epigenetic sculpting of the sperm and embryo, sexual transmission of microbes, and male gamete functions. These contributions indicate that mating can involve interactions between holobionts rather than simply the union of the maternal and paternal genomes. Thus, uniting male reproduction with the growing generalizations of microbial symbiosis guides several conceptual, theoretical, and empirical avenues for research in the life sciences.

articles_hidden.title: Soil contamination and acidification jointly increased cereal cadmium and dietary exposure over four decades
articles_hidden.authors: Qi-Xin Lü, Shuyou Zhang, Lili Niu, Pengjie Hu, Zhi-Xian Tang, Ya-Di Yang, Wangbo Zhang, Yongming Luo, Fang-Jie Zhao, Yijun Yao, Peng Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Cadmium contamination of staple cereals is an important food-safety concern, yet how long-term changes in soil chemistry alter cadmium transfer into food remains poorly resolved. Here we reconstructed changes in cropland topsoil cadmium and pH across China from 1980 to 2020 and quantified their consequences for cereal grain cadmium, dietary exposure, and mitigation potential. National mean topsoil cadmium increased from 0.123 to 0.236 mg kg −1 , while mean cropland pH declined from 6.50 to 6.30 nationally and by about 0.5 units in several southern rice-growing provinces. These coupled changes increased mean grain cadmium from 0.043 to 0.100 mg kg −1 in rice and from 0.017 to 0.032 mg kg −1 in wheat. By 2020, provinces with estimated mean hazard quotients exceeded 1.0 had a combined population of about 138 million. Counterfactual analysis showed that soil cadmium accumulation remained the dominant driver of rising grain cadmium, while acidification substantially amplified soil-to-grain transfer, especially in rice systems. Scenario analysis to 2050 indicated that restoring cropland pH to 6.5 could offset about 44% of the projected increase in rice cadmium even without immediate source control, whereas combining pH restoration with source control reduced mean rice cadmium by about 59% and brought exceedance close to zero. These findings identify soil acidification as an important amplifier of cadmium transfer into staple cereals and highlight targeted cropland pH restoration as a practical near-term strategy for reducing food-chain exposure while longer-term source-control measures take effect.

articles_hidden.title: Beyond blood ammonia: Intestinal ammonia emerges as an early microbial driver of mild cognitive impairment
articles_hidden.authors: Hao Chen, Zhen Wang, Yajun Tang, Yahui Liu, Lihui Kou, Jing Huang, Ke Guo, Zheng Yu
articles_hidden.abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is an early and potentially reversible stage of neurodegenerative disease, yet its initiating pathogenic signal remains unclear. Here, we identify gut microbiota-derived, urease-dependent intestinal ammonia as an early functional contributor to cognitive impairment. Analyses of human MCI-related cohorts revealed increased fecal urease activity and ammonia-related microbial features associated with cognitive performance. Importantly, intestinal ammonia accumulation precedes detectable elevations in blood ammonia, indicating that local intestinal dysregulation occurs before systemic hyperammonemia. Mechanistically, ammonia suppresses colonic SMAD7 and activates JAK2 signaling in the brain, thereby promoting cognitive dysfunction independently of systemic ammonia toxicity. This signaling pattern was further supported in 5xFAD mice. Therapeutically, supplementation with the ammonia-assimilating bacterium Limosilactobacillus mucosae or treatment with the clinically used ammonia-lowering agent L-ornithine-L-aspartate reduces intestinal ammonia levels and ameliorates early cognitive deficits. Together, these findings define an ammonia-SMAD7-JAK2 axis linking gut metabolism to brain function and highlight intestinal ammonia as a promising therapeutic target for early cognitive impairment.

articles_hidden.title: An alternative patterning mechanism for vertebrate tooth complexity
articles_hidden.authors: Daria Razmadze, Juuso Ikola, Ida-Maria Aalto, Nicolas Di-Poï
articles_hidden.abstract: How development reliably generates complex patterns remains a central question in biology. Teeth provide an ideal system for addressing this problem, linking cusp-patterning mechanisms to diversification and the fossil record, yet the developmental basis of multicuspid crown patterning beyond mammals remains unresolved. In mammals, cusp initiation and spacing are controlled by transient epithelial signaling centers called enamel knots (EKs). Here, we combine comparative developmental analyses, 3D morphometrics, mutant perturbation, and Bayesian inverse modeling (BITES; Bayesian Inference for Tooth Emergence Simulation) to examine tooth morphogenesis across six squamate species representing convergent multicuspid dentitions. We find that cusp patterning in these taxa does not rely on a discrete EK-based patterning system. Instead, cusps arise from a broad, persistent cusp signaling field (CSF) that deploys canonical tooth-patterning pathways but lacks the spatial restriction, apoptosis, and discrete secondary EKs (SEKs) characteristic of the mammalian system. Changes in epithelial growth and signaling are associated with disproportionate expansion of this field during tooth development and with the formation of additional cusps. Quantitative variation in field extent and dynamics can generate crown morphologies within and across species, providing a developmental basis for positional heterodonty and repeated gains and losses of multicuspidity in squamates. Our results identify an alternative epithelial patterning architecture for vertebrate cusp formation, in which conserved tooth-patterning signals are deployed through a broad field-based architecture rather than compact signaling centers. Together, these findings revise how tooth developmental complexity is encoded and show how similar complex crown forms can evolve through distinct flexible epithelial patterning mechanisms.

articles_hidden.title: Human sperm mitochondrial DNA retention is associated with reduced fecundability
articles_hidden.authors: Jeffrey M. Mann, Karolina Nowak, Savni Sawant, Ricardo P. Bertolla, J. Richard Pilsner
articles_hidden.abstract: Maternal inheritance of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is thought to depend in part on elimination of paternal mtDNA during spermatogenesis, yet elevated sperm mtDNA copy number (mtDNAcn) is associated with reduced semen quality and longer time-to-pregnancy (TTP). Whether this reflects mtDNA retained within mature sperm or somatic-cell contamination remains unresolved. Here, we used digital PCR and an adapted mtDNA FISH in mature sperm among normospermic men in a prospective preconception pregnancy cohort. We directly visualized mtDNA in the sperm midpiece, and imaging-based mtDNA signal corresponded with bulk sperm mtDNAcn, supporting a sperm-intrinsic origin. Sperm mtDNA retention increased across mtDNAcn groups associated with lower fecundability, reflecting both higher proportion of mtDNA-positive sperm and greater midpiece signal. Substantial cell-to-cell heterogeneity suggests elevated bulk mtDNAcn reflects a distinct subpopulation of mtDNA-retaining sperm. These findings provide direct cellular evidence of mtDNA retention in a subset of mature human sperm and identify mtDNA retention as a sperm phenotype associated with lower fecundability despite normal semen parameters. More broadly, they refine current models of mitochondrial genome elimination during human spermatogenesis and provide cellular context for sperm mtDNAcn as a marker of fecundability.

articles_hidden.title: Pyrethroid insecticide exposure enhances the ability of Helicoverpa armigera to counter host plant defenses through symbiotic bacteria
articles_hidden.authors: Meng Gu, Qiong Yang, Amosi Leonard Mbuji, Jing Yu, Rujing Kang, Lulu Zhang, Yuhao Cai, Laixin Luo, Ary A. Hoffmann, Lei Zhang, Pei Liang
articles_hidden.abstract: Like plant toxins, synthetic insecticides can exert strong selective pressures on pest populations. While responses to both plant toxins and synthetic insecticides can depend on adaptive changes in the nuclear genotype of the pest species, increasing evidence suggests that symbiotic microbes, particularly gut microbes, can also influence these responses. In the cotton bollworm, Helicoverpa armigera , concentrations of the symbiont Corynebacterium glyciniphilum increased in moth strains that were treated with the pyrethroid pesticide lambda-cyhalothrin (LCH), and they were also high in LCH-resistant strains and in populations exposed to 2-Tridecanone (2-TD), a secondary defense compound that is present in the Solanaceae. This increase enhanced the ability of H. armigera to overcome not only the pesticide but also a key defense mechanism in the solanaceous plants. In field populations of H. armigera , the abundance of C. glyciniphilum was lowest in populations feeding on nonsolanaceous plants that were sensitive to LCH. Based on gene knockouts, the underlying reason for the enhanced defensive capability provided by C. glyciniphilum was attributed to two detoxification enzyme genes (a P450 cytochrome and an esterase ) which can metabolize both LCH and 2-TD into nontoxic degradation products. These findings suggest that a common mechanism mediated by a symbiont contributes to the insect’s capacity to develop resistance to both a pesticide and a host plant toxin.

articles_hidden.title: Failure of a tropical upwelling rapidly collapsed Panama’s anchoveta fishery and its exports
articles_hidden.authors: Andrew J. Sellers, Carolina Chong-Montenegro, Amber L. Carter, Anabell J. Cornejo, Natasha A. Hinojosa, Javier Pardo Díaz, Anastasia Quintana, Ramiro Solís, Ana K. Spalding, Aaron O’Dea
articles_hidden.abstract: In 2025 the seasonal upwelling of the Gulf of Panama failed. Net primary production fell by 64% across the Gulf and industrial anchoveta landings dropped to 11% of the average, the lowest since the fishery became fully exploited in 1966. Anchoveta caught per purse-seine set fell to under a third of the normal rate while total catch per set stayed within its normal range. Landed fish carried about half their usual lipid content, and fish oil exports fell by 88% in both volume and value. The effects of one failed season reached international trade within months. Seasonal upwellings like this are common across the tropics yet far less studied than the large eastern boundary systems. The very strong El Niño now under way makes the 2027 season more uncertain.

articles_hidden.title: Targeted metabolic reprogramming of CD8 T cells restores immune regulation in lupus
articles_hidden.authors: Seiya Oba, Morgane H. Humbel, Hyshem H. Lancia, Wei Li, Wenliang Pan, Vasileios C. Kyttaris, Mohammad Rashidian, Reza Abdi, Maria G. Tsokos, George C. Tsokos
articles_hidden.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by pathogenic humoral autoimmunity, yet the mechanisms linking T cell dysfunction to aberrant B cell responses remain poorly defined. Here, we identify a CD8 + T cell–intrinsic metabolic defect that promotes humoral immune dysregulation in lupus. CD8 + T cells from patients with SLE exhibited elevated CD38 expression associated with reduced intracellular NAD + levels, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired cytotoxic capacity. Pharmacologic inhibition of CD38 with the small-molecule inhibitor MK-0159 restored NAD + metabolism and rescued cytotoxic function in human CD8 + T cells ex vivo. To selectively target this pathway in vivo, we developed anti-CD8 antibody-conjugated nanoparticles encapsulating MK-0159. In lupus-prone MRL/ lpr mice, CD8-targeted delivery enhanced granzyme B expression, improved degranulation, reduced plasmablast responses and autoantibody production, immune complex deposition, and renal pathology. Importantly, targeted delivery restored CD8 + T cell function without broad immune perturbation. These findings identify CD38-driven NAD + depletion as a reversible immunometabolic checkpoint limiting CD8 + T cell cytotoxic competence and support a model in which targeted restoration of cytotoxic fitness contributes to the control of humoral autoimmunity in SLE.

articles_hidden.title: Windblown dunes are born in sand at the brink of transport
articles_hidden.authors: M. Colin Marvin, Alex Gleason, Clément Narteau, Olivier Rozier, Mathieu G. A. Lapôtre
articles_hidden.abstract: Windblown dunes are found everywhere in the Solar System where a supply of loose sediment is mobilized by gas flows, from the sluggish winds of Venus to speed-of-sound sublimation flows on comets. Their abundance is nontrivial because dunes only form where grains hop ballistically (“saltate”). This implies that winds across the Solar System reach “goldilocks” speeds that are just right to initiate and maintain saltation of whatever sediment is available despite vast variations in material and fluid properties, and gravity. Based on select observations, it was proposed that dune fields may be characterized by a near-threshold transport state where dune-forming winds minimally exceed the saltation threshold on Earth. Here, we demonstrate that this is indeed the case globally. Next, we show that, unlike riverbeds—which evolve to a similar state through adjustments of channel geometry—dune fields are born in it due to the rapid decrease in wind frequency with increasing wind speed. These results imply that grain sizes in windblown dunes provide a robust record of formative winds, such that corresponding wind speeds can be estimated from aeolian sandstones and dune deposits across planets. The near-threshold state of windblown dunes thus opens a promising line of investigation for paleoenvironmental and paleoclimate reconstructions on Earth and beyond.

articles_hidden.title: Isotope evidence for changing methane sources at high northern latitudes
articles_hidden.authors: Xietiancheng Yu, Bibhasvata Dasgupta, Sylvia Englund Michel, John B. Miller, Xin Lan, Sourish Basu, Shinji Morimoto, Ryo Fujita, Daisuke Goto, Thomas Röckmann
articles_hidden.abstract: The renewed increase of methane (CH 4 ) in the atmosphere since 2007 is an imminent threat to the stability of the climate system and undermines climate policy goals. A reversal in the trend of its carbon isotopic composition ( δ 13 C CH4 ) in the 21st century indicates a fundamental shift in the global CH 4 cycle. Here, we investigate the origin of this δ 13 C CH4 trend by determining isotope source signatures of CH 4 emissions based on high and mid-northern latitude observations. A clear latitude gradient and seasonal cycle of the source signatures reflect the spatially and temporally varying contributions of the different sources, each with distinct signatures. We find a large shift in the source signature after 2007 between −3.6 and −5.1‰ at high northern latitudes, and a moderate change between −0.4 and −0.9‰ at mid-northern latitudes. The decrease in δ 13 C CH4 source signature is likely caused by a shift from thermogenic and pyrogenic to microbial sources, accompanied by a likely decrease in the isotopic signature of the microbial emissions, possibly resulting from climate change. Our results suggest that current inverse models may underestimate the shift between fossil and microbial emissions at high northern latitudes, or that microbial methanogenesis pathways change much more strongly than currently believed. Source changes at high latitudes have a disproportionate contribution to the observed trend in atmospheric δ 13 C CH4 .

articles_hidden.title: Leishmania cytochrome bc1 complex inhibition has potential for shortening leishmaniasis treatment duration
articles_hidden.authors: Advait S. Nagle, Yin H. Lai, Diana Caridha, Colin Deniston, Agnes Vidal-Biggart, Lauren C. Davis, Whitney S. Barnes, Casey J. N. Mathison, Mu-Yun Gao, Fang Liang, Xianzhong Liu, Monique Stinson, Jaime Ballard, Vince Yeh, Jeffrey Smith, Xiaodong Liu, Isabelle Lerario, Donatella Chianelli, Yongping Xie, Celine Be, Todd Groessl, Glenn Federe, Jessica Read, Badry Bursulaya, Michael Shapiro, Shilpi Khare, Ansgar Brock, Ben G. Wen, John R. Walker, Tove Tuntland, Srinivas Honnappa, Srinivasa P. S. Rao, Glen Spraggon, Richard J. Glynne, Valentina Molteni, Frantisek Supek
articles_hidden.abstract: Leishmaniasis affects approximately 1 million people annually with visceral infections resulting in death if left untreated and the cutaneous disease leading to disfiguring skin lesions. Leishmaniasis is caused by the Leishmania spp. parasites and is difficult to treat as existing drugs are far from optimal. Despite increased efforts to identify better drugs for leishmaniasis, there are few new chemical entities that have entered clinical development, thus highlighting the persistent need for such compounds. Here we describe GNF5885, an orally available and parasite-selective inhibitor of Leishmania cytochrome bc1 complex. GNF5885 was derived through phenotypic optimization of buparvaquone. GNF5885 exhibits unparalleled efficacy in vivo and can efficiently clear parasites from mice in models of visceral and cutaneous infections. Furthermore, its ability to clear parasites rapidly with short treatment regimens makes it particularly desirable for treating patients residing in regions endemic to leishmaniasis. Cryo-EM structure of the Leishmania cytochrome bc1 complex with GNF5885 at 2.8 Å resolution revealed that the inhibitor binds in the Qi ubiquinone-binding pocket. Our data provide validation of the Leishmania cytochrome bc1 complex as a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of leishmaniasis and underscore the possibility of developing a short-course oral treatment for this neglected disease. In addition, the availability of the cytochrome bc1 complex costructure with GNF5885 opens an opportunity to rationally design new cytochrome bc1 complex inhibitors suitable for clinical development.

articles_hidden.title: Airborne microbial diversity over Greenlandic and Antarctic plateaus reflects divergent atmospheric connectivity
articles_hidden.authors: Sofía Galbán, Sergi González-Herrero, Marcela Svarc, Pablo Sanz, Ana Justel, Antonio Quesada
articles_hidden.abstract: The polar plateaus are among the most remote environments on Earth. Despite their extreme conditions, these cold deserts on the Greenland and Antarctic Ice Sheets harbor microbial life in snow, ice, and air. However, knowledge of polar airborne microbiomes remains scarce and methodological differences have hindered bipolar comparisons. Here, we present a systematic survey of airborne bacterial and eukaryotic communities across Greenlandic and Antarctic Plateaus, using standardized sampling and genetic techniques, coupled with atmospheric physics and advanced statistical analyses. We found that Antarctic airborne communities are characterized by low diversity and high homogeneity, whereas Greenlandic communities are richer, more variable, and more connected to coastal-marine zones. Our results indicate that atmospheric isolation, together with short-term atmospheric variables, is associated with differences in the microbial biogeography of each Plateau. Compared with Antarctica, the Greenlandic Plateau is more frequently influenced by air masses from outside the plateau over long timescales and exhibits more variable short-term air back-trajectories, reflecting enhanced microbial dispersal and diversity. These findings highlight the potential of polar plateaus as observational platforms for airborne microbial diversity, where sustained and temporally resolved sampling could help assess variations in community composition associated with atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic influence under global change.

articles_hidden.title: Microbially driven iron redox chemistry unlocks phosphorus reservoirs in oxygenated soils
articles_hidden.authors: Liping Fang, Jialin Chi, Yanan Ou, Hui Yin, Kai Liu, Yao Yang, Xiangjun Meng, Wenjun Zhang, Xiaoxia Zhou, Christine V. Putnis, Fengchang Wu, Fangbai Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Biological phosphorus (P) mobilization is generally attributed to proton- and ligand-driven dissolution of mineral P, enzymatic hydrolysis of organic P, and, under anoxic conditions, reductive release of phosphate from Fe(III) minerals. Here, we show that extracellular metabolites released by diverse Gram-positive bacteria sustain Fe(III) reduction under oxic conditions, releasing mineral-associated phosphate. The resulting Fe(II) reacts with O 2 to generate reactive oxygen species that activate organic P. This redox pathway was observed across diverse aerobic bacteria and agricultural soils and increased plant-available P. These findings establish aerobic microbial Fe redox chemistry as a previously overlooked route for returning otherwise inaccessible P to bioavailable pools, with implications for reactivating legacy P in agricultural soils.

articles_hidden.title: Evidence for patterns of colonization risk in the nationwide hospitalized patient network in France
articles_hidden.authors: Shrichand Bhuria, Lucille Calmon, Madhav Chaturvedi, Laura Temime, André Karch, Tjibbe Donker, Vittoria Colizza, Pascal Crépey
articles_hidden.abstract: Patient movement within and between hospitals creates a complex hospital network that facilitates the spread of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria and contributes to healthcare-associated infections. Yet most national-scale studies infer spread from aggregated hospital-to-hospital patient sharing, leaving patient-to-patient contact pathways and the role of routine patient mobility in shaping colonization risk poorly characterized. Using France’s 2023–2024 national hospital-discharge data, we reconstructed a temporal patient-based network of 10.4 million patients across 1,408 acute-care hospitals, comprising 326.6 million overnight ward colocation interactions. We simulated colonization over 365 d on the observed day-by-day temporal network using a stochastic susceptible–colonized–susceptible model, with a mean colonization duration of 180 d. We used national carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) surveillance data to calibrate differences in transmission risk across clinical settings. Across 2,000 simulations initiated on randomly selected dates in 2023, we calculated patient-level colonization probabilities and summarized risk across patients’ residential areas, wards, and hospitals. We further assessed hospital-level consistency between simulated risk and recorded CPE occurrence. Simulated risk was highly heterogeneous across patients and care settings. When mapped by place of residence, hospital-associated colonization risk showed strong spatial clustering in both urban and rural areas. Multivariable regression analyses identified patient- and hospital-level characteristics associated with heterogeneity in simulated colonization risk. Sensitivity analyses varying initial seeding and colonization duration showed that relative risk patterns remained highly stable. This nationwide framework shows how patient mobility and ward colocation patterns can reveal patterns of hospital-associated colonization risk and could support pathogen-specific surveillance and intervention evaluation.

articles_hidden.title: Compound heterozygosity for I692del and V726A variants in MEFV leads to severe autoinflammation and elevated interleukin-18 (CHIVE-18)
articles_hidden.authors: Deborah L. Stone, Sophie Georgin-Lavialle, Ezgi Deniz Batu, Scott W. Canna, Mary Maclean, Kumi Izawa, Carl Esperanzate, Sabrina Helmold Hait, Jiro Kitaura, Ines Elhani, Hongying Wang, Oskar Schnappauf, Kazushi Izawa, Eitaro Hiejima, Jennifer Stoddard, Julie E. Niemela, Sergio D. Rosenzweig, Tina Romeo, Guilaine Boursier, Helen L. Leavis, Aurélia Carbasse, Juan I. Aróstegui, Ali Sobh, Norhan Ragab, Heba Gadelrab, L. Nandini Moorthy, Veronique Hentgen, Laure Calas, Anna Mensa-Vilaró, Pilar Llobet-Agulló, Estibaliz Lazaro, Lars T. van der Veken, Manon M. H. Huibers, Laurence Cuisset, Dorota Rowczenio, Massimo Gadina, Amanda K. Ombrello, Jae Jin Chae, Yasmine El Chazli, Walaa Shoman, Daniel L. Kastner, Ivona Aksentijevich
articles_hidden.abstract: We describe a severe MEFV -associated autoinflammatory disease, distinct from familial Mediterranean fever (FMF), and designate it CHIVE-18 syndrome (Compound Heterozygosity for I692del and V726A MEFV variants and Elevated IL-18). We present the clinical features and inflammatory signatures of 44 CHIVE-18 patients and 9 other patients with two MEFV variants including I692del. Clinical findings in CHIVE-18 patients often include transfusion-dependent anemia, arthritis, organomegaly, inflammatory bowel disease, failure to thrive, and less frequently cytokine storm, Amyloid A (AA) amyloidosis, and neutrophilic dermatoses. Serum total and free IL-18 levels in CHIVE-18 patients were markedly elevated compared to those of healthy controls, classical FMF patients, and compound heterozygotes for I692del and a pathogenic MEFV variant other than V726A and were comparable to the previously described levels of patients with pyogenic arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, and acne syndrome. Cultured U937 cells expressing the V726A/I692del double mutant exhibited significantly increased release of IL-1β, IL-18, and lactate dehydrogenase compared to the other FMF-associated mutants. Patients’ myeloid cells showed enhanced STAT1 phosphorylation after stimulation with IFNγ. Despite having undetectable serum IL-1β, a previously reported CHIVE-18 patient with autoimmune hepatitis had in situ staining of a liver biopsy that showed high expression of IL-1β, TNFα, and IL-18, which localized to CD68+ tissue macrophages. CHIVE-18 patients usually require an IL-1 inhibitor and sometimes combination therapy with another biologic to control disease activity. In summary, CHIVE-18 is a distinct, severe disease that expands the spectrum of MEFV -associated autoinflammatory disorders and highlights genotype/phenotype complexity in compound heterozygous disorders.

articles.title: Rebuilding science’s social contract with the public
articles.abstract: Much has been written about how the social contract between science and society in the United States is in crisis. According to its terms, research will yield broad economic, health, and security benefits to the very public that funds it. But this relationship depends on public trust in science, its systems, and the scientists themselves, and therein lies the problem. Beyond making discoveries and publishing results, scientists shape their own culture, and that is where some changes may be the key to rebuilding public trust.

articles_hidden.title: AI-based digital pathology defines spatial border ecosystems in triple-negative breast cancer
articles_hidden.authors: Hang Zhang, Fan Yang, Pu Tian, Han Wang, Ying Xu, Xiao-Hui Zhu, Xue-Pei Li, Shen Zhao, Yi-Zhou Jiang, Yi Xiao, Zhi-Ming Shao
articles_hidden.abstract: The invasive tumor border in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is currently poorly understood. We integrated digital pathology and spatial multi-omics to define border ecosystems in TNBC. AI-based digital pathology identified five border ecosystems, three associated with prognosis. Spatial multi-omics analyses further resolved the spatial niche, molecular mechanisms and clinical relevance of these ecosystems. Immune-infiltrated borders contain a triadic immune niche associated with favorable prognosis and immunotherapy sensitivity. Tumor–stroma borders harbor a MIF + fibroblast exclusion niche that blocks immune infiltration and suppresses T cells function, predicting poor prognosis. Tumor–adipose borders, featured an FLT1 + endothelial niche, promote hypoxia, vascular leakage, and tumor dissemination. Targeting this niche inhibits tumor progression. Collectively, these findings establish a spatial resource that might enable border-directed therapeutic strategies in TNBC.

articles_hidden.title: Millisecond-scale imaging of fragmented earthquake rupture by near-source fiber-optic sensing
articles_hidden.authors: Sangwoo Han, YoungHee Kim, Jaewoo Kim, Avinash Nayak, Fu Yin, Jonathan Ajo-Franklin
articles_hidden.abstract: Small earthquakes [i.e., those of magnitude ( M ) <3] are commonly modeled as simple circular ruptures, leaving the fine-scale spatial attributes of rupture dynamics unresolved. We used near-source distributed acoustic sensing to image the millisecond-scale rupture of an M 2 earthquake within a swarm sequence in California’s Brawley Seismic Zone. Inverting fiber-derived apparent source time functions revealed two distinct rupture episodes separated by 42 milliseconds, reflecting rupture arrest followed by dynamic renucleation. Analysis of a 3-hour sequence showed adjacent, largely nonoverlapping fault patches activated in succession, forming complementary slip partitioning. These fragmented failure patterns within the M 2 rupture and its sequence limited rupture growth, consistent with the absence of a dominant mainshock. Microearthquakes, which are now accessible by fiber-optic sensing, provide direct constraints on fault mechanics across scales bridging laboratory experiments and large earthquakes.

articles_hidden.title: An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs
articles_hidden.authors: Alexandre Webster, Halima Yusuf, Nina Schweizer, Chloe Charalambous, Eike Urs Mönnich, Heike Eckel, Rüdiger Moltrecht, Martyn Blayney, Kay Elder, Claus Sibold, Andreas Tandler-Schneider, Melina Schuh
articles_hidden.abstract: In humans, female fertility declines rapidly from approximately 35 years onward owing to a steep increase in eggs in which chromosomes have split prematurely or that harbor an incorrect number of chromosomes (aneuploid eggs). A leading cause of age-related aneuploidy in eggs is the premature separation of sister chromatids (PSSC), which is caused by a loss of cohesin from chromosomes. In this study, we created an artificial cohesion system that reduces PSSC in aged mouse eggs. We further engineered a separase-cleavable sequence into the system, allowing for its scheduled deactivation during anaphase. We demonstrated that the artificial cohesion system could be adapted to tether human chromosomes, providing a proof of principle for the future development of approaches to reduce PSSC in eggs from women of advanced reproductive age.

articles_hidden.title: Binding kinetics enable tumor-selective MAPK and growth suppression by a Type 1 RAF inhibitor
articles_hidden.authors: Mathieu Desaunay, Tara L. Peters, Evangelia Matenoglou, Beau Baars, Bijaya Gaire, Ana Orive-Ramos, Li Ren, Joseph P. Lyssikatos, Michael R. Burkard, Dalton Dacus, Matthew J. Sale, Stuart A. Aaronson, Frank McCormick, Evripidis Gavathiotis, Stefan D. Gross, Poulikos I. Poulikakos
articles_hidden.abstract: Targeting the RAS/MAPK pathway has long been constrained by dose-limiting toxicity in normal tissues at doses required for durable tumor control. Although Type 1.5 RAF inhibitors improved selectivity in BRAF(V600X)-monomer tumors, a comparable strategy for RAF dimer-driven cancers, including those with RAS mutations, has been lacking. We describe ELV-3111, a potent Type 1 RAF inhibitor that inhibits RAF dimers and exploits binding kinetics for tumor selectivity. ELV-3111 primes RAF in normal tissues, and its rapid dissociation during drug clearance generates drug-free RAF dimers that paradoxically activate MAPK signaling. RAS-mutant tumors are spared, where RAF is already primed. Combined with a MEK inhibitor, ELV-3111 restored normal tissue signaling while deepening tumor pathway inhibition, producing regressions across RAS- and BRAF-mutant experimental models. Thus, inhibitor dissociation kinetics provide a generalizable source of therapeutic index.

articles_hidden.title: Mechanisms of nucleosome disruption shape epigenetic inheritance pathway choice
articles_hidden.authors: Oliver Willhoft, Milos A. Cvetkovic, Fernando R. Rosas Bringas, Dolores Jurado-Santiago, Robert Ciaran Mackenzie Frater, Kimberly Quililan, Thomas Pühringer, Daniel Ramirez Montero, Zhuo Angel Chen, Juri Rappsilber, Frank Uhlmann, Anja Groth, John F. X. Diffley, Rodrigo Bermejo, Alessandro Costa
articles_hidden.abstract: Maintaining cell identity requires duplicating the genome and epigenome during S phase. As DNA is copied, histones extracted from parental nucleosomes are transferred to nascent strands, which preserves the position of epigenetic marks. How the replisome coordinates these processes is unclear. Using reconstitution with purified yeast proteins, kinetic measurements, structural biology, mass spectrometry and genomics, we examined nucleosome-replisome encounter and histone transfer. Parental nucleosomes can be unwrapped ahead of the fork by the MCM helicase, aided by FACT and Ctf4, or by Tof1. Nucleosomal DNA unwrapping by MCM creates a FACT binding site, helping strip histones off DNA. Ctf4 enhances FACT-stimulated histone extraction, retains parental histones and hands them to Tof1, en route to lagging-strand redeposition. Thus, extraction via Ctf4 commits histones to lagging-strand transfer.

articles_hidden.title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 M w 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake
articles_hidden.authors: Haipeng Luo, Fengzhou Tan, Zhangfeng Ma, Kejie Chen, Jian Zhang, Xin Wang, Shiqing Xu, Matías Carvajal, Hang Xu, Sang-Ho Yun, Ling Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: Rough fault segments typically terminate giant earthquakes but are rarely reported to foster them. However, rupture characteristics of the 2025 moment magnitude ( M w ) 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake are consistent with initiation in a rough zone. Its early rupture was sluggish, lasting ~50 seconds with limited slip but strong, scattered high-frequency radiation. Rupture then propagated southward into a smoother segment, producing >20 meters slip with less intense high-frequency radiation. Using also the rupture characteristics of four M w 7+ foreshocks and aftershocks, we reveal variably sized seismic patches within the rough zone. We interpret these behaviors as manifestations of stress or frictional heterogeneities on the rough segment that favor localized failures yet can foster a giant rupture when spatially connected to a smooth, locked neighboring segment, a scenario previously underrecognized and meriting consideration in seismic hazard assessments.

articles_hidden.title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
articles_hidden.authors: Yongqiang Zhang, Xian Wang, Jun Xia, Congcong Li, Xiaojie Li, Zhenwu Xu, Jing Tian, Gang Zhao, Yuxuan Xie, Xuanze Zhang, Ning Ma, Haoshan Wei, Qi Huang, Longhao Wang, Pedro L. B. Chaffe, Georgia Destouni, Francis H. S. Chiew, Alexandra M. Murray, Xing Yuan, Edwin H. Sutanudjaja, James McPhee, Sulagna Mishra, Murugesu Sivapalan, Günter Blöschl
articles_hidden.abstract: Global warming is expected to accelerate the hydrological cycle, yet its impact on terrestrial water availability is uncertain. Using assimilated streamflow observations from 150 major basins and satellite data for over 1.2 million water bodies, we show a global-scale synchronized decline of streamflow and surface water storage during the 2023–2024 record-warm period, the largest reduction since 1991. South America accounted for 70.4 ± 4.2% of the global streamflow decline. This abrupt depletion was driven by compound ocean–atmosphere forcing, in which concurrent El Niño and tropical North Atlantic warming triggered large-scale atmospheric subsidence, moisture divergence, and amplified drought. These findings reveal that extreme warming can induce abrupt water losses even in humid regions, underscoring a critical vulnerability of global hydrology and water security.

articles_hidden.title: Integrating established and emerging tools to assess wildlife condition from the ground, up
articles_hidden.authors: Michelle R. Shero, David W. Johnston, Amy L. Kirkham, Jennifer M. Burns, Caroline L. Rzucidlo, Daniel P. Costa, K.C. Bierlich
articles_hidden.abstract: Metabolic energy links individual physiology to population-level dynamics, making wildlife body condition a cornerstone of conservation science. Emerging technologies, including unoccupied aircraft systems, make remote assessment of animal condition possible at unprecedented scales, and physiologically grounded validation is essential for strong inference. Here we examine the strengths and challenges of traditional and remote methods, using a comparative perspective that emphasizes both lipid and lean mass dynamics in evaluating wildlife health. We provide a framework that integrates complementary approaches to assess wildlife condition across diverse systems, matching emerging methods with the required physiological resolution, species characteristics, and temporal and spatial scales, while enhancing research ethics. Expanding capacity to track wildlife energetics from individuals to populations requires novel approaches and is vital for conservation in a changing world.

articles_hidden.title: Priming of AGO2 by type I interferons balances inflammation and antiviral immunity
articles_hidden.authors: Yujie Ren, Xiao-Xu Zhu, Yaxin Wang, An Wang, Bowen Zhang, Jing Lou, Cheng Zhu, Dawei Jiang, Xiaobei Xiong, Xi Zhou
articles_hidden.abstract: Argonaute-2 (AGO2)–mediated RNA silencing contributes to antiviral defenses in plants and insects and may contribute to mammalian immunity, too. However, it is unknown whether AGO2 is modified upon infection or inflammation in mammals. We identified that the ubiquitin ligase RING-finger protein 126 (RNF126) interacts with and ubiquitinates AGO2 to enhance its small interfering RNA or microRNA loading. Using data from cells in vitro and mouse tissues, we propose that RNF126 is induced by type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling and promotes the ability of AGO2 to silence proinflammatory genes and inhibit viral replication. Lipid nanoparticle delivery of RNF126 mRNA to mice inhibited inflammation and viral replication. These findings identify cross-talk of IFN-based immune signaling and AGO2-mediated RNA silencing and suggest that the RNF126-AGO2 axis helps to balance inflammatory and antiviral immune protection.

articles_hidden.title: Counter-ion confinement reverses ion selectivity in subnanometer channels
articles_hidden.authors: Fangmeng Sheng, Liang Ge, Bin Wu, Xingya Li, Tongwen Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: Ion transport in nano- and subnanometer channels is central to processes such as ion separation, energy conversion and storage, and nanofluidics. Conventionally, positively charged nanochannels favor anion transport and vice versa. We report that cationic covalent organic framework membranes with sub–one-nanometer channels exhibit selective cation transport. This reversal in selectivity arises from a counter-ion confinement effect, which inverts the electrostatic environment inside the channel wall and creates a secondary confinement region. The counter-ion confinement mechanism concomitantly suppresses coexisting ion competition in mixed-salt systems, enabling membranes to retain high selectivity under practical separation conditions. Our findings provide a design strategy for creating adaptive and highly selective membranes for precise ion transport and separation.

articles_hidden.title: A tryptophan cation radical determines radical transfer kinetics and catalytic rate in a ribonucleotide reductase
articles_hidden.authors: Nejc Nagelj, Chang Cui, Kenichi Yokoyama, JoAnne Stubbe, Daniel G. Nocera
articles_hidden.abstract: Ribonucleotide reductase (RNR) is the sole enzyme responsible for de novo deoxynucleotide synthesis for DNA replication and repair. In the Escherichia coli class Ia RNR, a radical must traverse 32 angstroms along a pathway composed of amino acids spanning β and α subunits to complete each turnover. By incorporating unnatural amino acids to alter reduction potentials of pathway tyrosine residues, we (i) perturb the rates of radical transfer and show that they match the rates of deoxynucleotide production and (ii) directly observe a tryptophan cation radical (W 48 + •) as a kinetically competent pathway intermediate. Together, these results establish that radical transfer through W 48 in α 2 β 2 is the rate-limiting process, which controls the enzymatic activity of E. coli RNR.

articles_hidden.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal’s assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing’s most important challenges.

articles_hidden.title: Nutritional interventions’ impacts on human milk: Three trials in low-resource settings
articles_hidden.authors: Trenton Dailey-Chwalibóg, Andrew Mertens, Kelsey Fehr, Chi-Hung Shu, April Jauhal, Melissa B. Manus, Lishi Deng, Laeticia Celine Toe, Ameer Muhammad, Aneela Pasha, Yasir Shafiq, Naveed Iqbal, Waqasuddin Khan, Muhammad Imran Nisar, Jo-Anna B. Baxter, Megan R. Beggs, Niveda Sundararaman, Jennifer E. Van Eyk, Lars Bode, Alan Hubbard, Kim A. Lagerborg, Mohit Jain, Daniela Hampel, Setareh Shahab-Ferdows, Lindsay H. Allen, Carl Lachat, Mark D. DeBoer, Fyezah Jehan, Nima Aghaeepour, Liat Shenhav, Joann M. McDermid, Meghan B. Azad
articles_hidden.abstract: Human milk (HM) composition is variable to support changing infant needs and is influenced by maternal diet and health. We harmonized HM data from three randomized trials in Burkina Faso (MISAME-III), Pakistan (Mumta-LW), and Tanzania (ELICIT) within the International Milk Composition (IMiC) Consortium to test how maternal nutrition affects HM composition. Balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplements or nicotinamide given to lactating mothers increased milk B vitamins, whereas macronutrients, oligosaccharides, bioactive proteins, and microbiome composition were physiologically buffered. Metabolomic and proteomic analyses revealed shifts in vitamin-related metabolites, triglyceride profiles, and intracellular protein representation. In a MISAME-III subset, maternal and infant blood showed concordant changes. Postnatal BEP improved infant growth only in the more undernourished cohort. Improved milk micronutrient quality across settings supports extending maternal supplementation into lactation.

articles_hidden.title: A fast radio burst at redshift 2, three billion years after the Big Bang
articles_hidden.authors: Manisha Caleb, Themiya Nanayakkara, Benjamin W. Stappers, Inés Pastor-Marazuela, Ilya S. Khrykin, Karl Glazebrook, Nicolas Tejos, J. Martin, Anya Nugent, Kavya Shaji, Jun Tian
articles_hidden.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients from extragalactic sources. Their frequency and polarization properties are affected by plasma and magnetic fields along the line of sight to Earth. We report radio observations of FRB 20240304B and near-infrared follow-up to identify its host galaxy. The host is a low-mass, clumpy, star-forming galaxy at redshift 2.148 ± 0.0013, corresponding to 3 billion years after the Big Bang. This FRB occurred during the peak of cosmic star formation and probes ionized gas over ~80% of cosmic history. The highly scattered burst emission implies that there is a population of FRBs that are undetected by current surveys.

articles_hidden.title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
articles_hidden.authors: Jasper Butcher, Rohith Krishna, Raktim Mitra, Seth M. Woodbury, Donghyo Kim, Rafael I. Brent, Yanjing Li, Nathaniel Corley, Andrew Favor, Anqi Chen, Paul T. Hardy, Bo Qiang, Kieran Didi, Maxwell Kazman, Lars L. Schaaf, Frank DiMaio, David Baker
articles_hidden.abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. We describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which uses free-atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges, from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active-site architecture that incorporates a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases, we obtained active catalysts in zero-shot 96 construct design campaigns.

articles_hidden.authors: April Jauhal, Bianca Cordazzo-Vargas, Daniel Sunko, Pratima Niroula, Lishi Deng, Laeticia Celine Toe, Ameer Muhammad, Aneela Pasha, Yasir Shafiq, Naveed Iqbal, Waqasuddin Khan, Andrew Mertens, Kelsey Fehr, Joann M. articles_hidden.abstract: The mammary gland produces nutrient-rich human milk (HM), yet how mammary functional state shapes HM composition and infant outcomes remains poorly understood. We used HM multiomics, including metabolomics, proteomics, micronutrients, macronutrients, and HM oligosaccharides, across 1543 samples from three cohorts, including two randomized trials, as a noninvasive readout of mammary functional state. Trajectory modeling and multiomic integration showed that maternal supplementation improved recovery from early growth faltering and revealed a shared HM compositional axis linking maternal nutrition to infant growth. Machine learning, with Human Protein Atlas–informed proteomics, identified seven HM biomarkers reflecting variation across key mammary domains, indexing milk synthesis, barrier integrity, and immune-repair activity. Elevated valerylcarnitine and low pantothenic acid emerged as metabolic signals linking mammary functional state to infant growth.

articles_hidden.title: Stereodivergent telomerization of linear functionalized dienes with amines
articles_hidden.authors: Wen-Qian Wang, Ren-En Li, Hui Xu, Han-Zhe Miao, Liang Chen, Chao Zheng, Shu-Li You, Zhi-Tao He
articles_hidden.abstract: Despite the importance of divergent synthesis to obtain different isomers for medicinal and material chemistry, divergent stereocontrol over four distinct selectivity factors remains a fundamental challenge. The telomerization reaction is limited to the transformation of simple unfunctionalized 1,3-dienes to circumvent intractable stereoisomeric mixtures. Here, we report an orthogonal telomerization platform using linear functionalized 1,3-dienes as the substrates, which simultaneously dictates geometric, regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivities. We prepared diverse types of γ-amino esters from identical, readily available unsaturated esters and amines via synergistic palladium and acid catalysis, with each precisely obtained out of hundreds of potential telomers. We developed several chiral phosphoramidite ligands to promote the transformation. This study showcases the potential of multidimensional stereomanipulation for the industrially valuable telomerization reaction.

articles.title: Misremembered social networks are predictions of the future in disguise
articles.abstract: Mistakes in how the brain processes social network information in the present can predict the network’s future state.

articles.title: Errors in social network knowledge predict how ties evolve in the future
articles.authors: Alice Xia, Yi Yang Teoh, Apoorva Bhandari, Oriel FeldmanHall
articles.abstract: A notable feature of people’s social knowledge is that it is riddled with errors. These errors, e.g., making mistakes about who are actually friends in a social network, has typically been attributed to cognitive limitations or heuristics that prioritize knowledge of general social patterns over details about specific ties. Here, we demonstrate that such errors instead reflect an adaptive link prediction process that anticipates how the network will evolve far into the future. By longitudinally following a large, real-world social network ( n  = 196) and tracking the formation and dissolution of social ties over the course of a year, we show that judgments that are wrong in the moment accurately forecast which relationships will emerge or dissolve up to 6 months later. On average, participants’ errors predicted tie formation nearly 3× and tie loss more than 1.2× above chance levels. Beyond the use of simple heuristics like triadic closure and homophily, computational modeling reveals that successful link prediction relies on mental representations of the social network that integrates information about both direct and indirect, long-range ties between individuals. Having a social network representation that is future-oriented yields distinct social advantages: Those who are better able to predict changes in the network become more centrally positioned over time, contingent on their initial position.

articles_hidden.title: Clearance of erythrocytes after subarachnoid hemorrhage: Cranial lymphatic and dural pathways
articles_hidden.authors: Tangtang Xiang, Elliot Norris, Sarmad Peymaei, Diego Ulisse Pizzagalli, Steven T. Proulx
articles_hidden.abstract: The clearance of toxic blood products from the brain after subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is critical for neurological recovery, yet the precise anatomical pathways and cellular mechanisms responsible for this process remain poorly defined. Using murine models of both arterial perforation and low-rate intracisternal injection, we have mapped a comprehensive, multifaceted network of red blood cell (RBC) distribution and clearance. We found that, while RBCs accessed peripheral lymphatic vessels via cranial nerves, an extensive distribution of extravasated erythrocytes could also be observed sequestered within nonendothelial, collagen-lined interstitial channels flanking the major dural venous sinuses. By day 2 post-SAH, regional macrophages actively cleared some trapped erythrocytes. These findings provide a detailed spatiotemporal framework of SAH blood clearance, revealing promising anatomical and cellular targets to accelerate stroke recovery.

articles_hidden.title: GDF15 impacts chronic kidney disease and associated weight loss through distinct mechanisms
articles_hidden.authors: Huajun Bai, Amritanshu Rana, Liwen Su, Ting Peng, Chenyu Li, Wenting Zhao, Aidan Bauer, Beishan Chen, Yuxiao Liang, Duanduan Lin, Joseph J. Loureiro, Nancy Finkel, Riley Sawka, Peiran Lu, Wencao Zhao, Dhanunjay Mukhi, Benjamin J. Wilkins, Randy J. Seeley, Danna M. Breen, Katalin Susztak, Liming Pei
articles_hidden.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is frequently accompanied by anorexia, cachexia, and inflammation, which collectively contribute to poor clinical outcomes. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we demonstrate a pivotal role for growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) in CKD morbidities. Deteriorating renal function and clinical disease status correlates with GDF15 levels in plasma and kidneys of CKD patients. In a mouse CKD model, GDF15 levels are elevated and Gdf15 knockout ( Gdf15 −/− ) mice are partially protected from CKD-induced anorexia and weight loss despite worsening renal function and inflammation. GDF15 receptor Gfral knockout ( Gfral −/− ) mice recapitulate these phenotypes. Metabolic cage studies reveal that the weight loss-protection effects are primarily attributed to increased food intake. Intriguingly, pair-fed Gdf15 −/− and Gfral −/− mice exhibited phenotypic and molecular divergence. Pair feeding in Gdf15 −/− mice reverses loss-of-GDF15’s effect on body weight but does not restore renal functions. In contrast, pair feeding in Gfral −/− mice reverses loss-of-GFRAL’s effect on both body weight and renal function. Transcriptome analysis suggests that GDF15 may act through both GFRAL-dependent mechanisms on food intake and GFRAL-independent mechanisms that primarily modulate inflammation and metabolic pathways. A monoclonal antibody that neutralizes circulating GDF15 markedly restores food intake and preserves body weight, demonstrating the therapeutic potential of targeting GDF15 in CKD-associated weight loss. Together, these findings demonstrate GDF15-GFRAL as a potential therapeutic target for CKD-associated weight loss and suggest GFRAL-dependent, food intake-mediated actions of GDF15 and food intake-independent effects that may contribute to renal inflammation and metabolic regulation.

articles_hidden.title: The circSRSF5 -FUS-EIF4A3 regulatory circuitry protects Ewing sarcoma cells from EWS::FLI1 small-molecule inhibition
articles_hidden.authors: Veronica Riccioni, Valentina Frezza, Claudia Fiorilli, Gianmarco Fenili, Noemie Robil, Ramona Palombo, Lidia Chellini, Pierre de la Grange, Maria Paola Paronetto
articles_hidden.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have become a key focus in cancer research due to their high stability, diversity, and ability to regulate various biological processes. This study explores the impact of small-molecule inhibition of EWS::FLI1 oncogene by YK-4-279 in Ewing sarcoma (ES). ES is a rare and highly aggressive childhood cancer driven by fusion proteins that disrupt normal gene regulation and promote tumor growth. Current treatments rely on intensive chemotherapy with serious long-term side effects, emphasizing the need for targeted therapies. A promising new approach targets the interaction between EWS::FLI1 and the RNA helicase DHX9 through the small molecule YK-4-279, which displays strong antitumor effects and has advanced to clinical trials. Transcriptome profiling revealed widespread changes in circRNA expression after YK-4-279 treatment, with a notable up-regulation of circSRSF5 . Functional and mechanistic evidence identifies a key role for circSRSF5 in tumor cell survival by stabilizing the anti-apoptotic protein eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A3 (EIF4A3) and contributing to therapy resistance. These findings uncover a previously unidentified role for circRNAs, particularly circSRSF5 , in ES pathogenesis and treatment response.

articles_hidden.title: Multimodal motion and behavior switching of multistable ciliary walkers
articles_hidden.authors: Sumit Mohanty, Paul Baconnier, Harmannus A. H. Schomaker, Alberto Comoretto, Martin van Hecke, Johannes T. B. Overvelde
articles_hidden.abstract: The collective motion of arrays of cilia—tiny, hairlike protrusions—drives the locomotion of numerous microorganisms, enabling multimodal motion and switching between gaits to navigate complex environments. Inspired by this multimodal motion, we introduce multistable soft walkers with millimeter-scale flexible cilia that buckle under the walkers weight, coupling multistability and actuation within a single physical mechanism. When placed on a vibrating surface, the propulsion direction of ciliary walkers is selected through the buckled states of their cilia, allowing multimodal motion and switching between modes in response to perturbations. We first show that bimodal walkers with left-right symmetric cilia can reverse direction upon encountering obstacles. Next, we demonstrate that walkers with isotropic cilia exhibit both translational and rotational motion and switch between them in response to environmental interactions. At increasing densities, swarms of such walkers collectively transition from predominantly spinning to translational motion. Last, we show that the shape, placement, and number of cilia controls the modes of motion of the walkers. Our results establish a rational, physically grounded strategy for designing minimalist soft robots where complex behaviors emerge from feedback between internal mechanical states and environmental interactions, laying the foundation for soft robotic collectives that operate without onboard sensing or centralized control.

articles_hidden.title: PEG-free tunable poly(2-oxazoline) lipids modulate mRNA-LNP biodistribution and expression in vivo
articles_hidden.authors: Colin Basham, Matt Haney, Yuling Zhao, Hallie Hutsell, Reb Kornahrens, Liubov Palchak, Konstantin A. Lukyanov, Kyoungtea Kim, Ayse Baysal, Michael C. Brown, Alexander V. Kabanov, Jacob D. Ramsey
articles_hidden.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have transformed drug delivery, enabling the stabilization and efficient intracellular delivery of nucleic acids. Current LNP platforms, including those used in clinical COVID-19 vaccines, rely on polyethylene glycol (PEG) to stabilize the nanoparticle. However, anti-PEG antibodies are ubiquitous in the population and are a major cause of anaphylaxis and reduced therapeutic efficacy by accelerating the blood clearance of PEGylated products. Here, we report the development of poly(2-oxazoline) (POx) lipids as alternatives. POx polymers are poorly immunogenic and mitigate accelerated blood clearance. Upon varying polymer hydrophilicity and molecular weight, we screened transfection efficiency in multiple cell lines and evaluated top candidates in vivo. Our findings demonstrate that POx-lipids incorporating short hydrophilic oxazoline chains enhance target transfection while mitigating liver expression. These POx-lipids boost expression in key extrahepatic tissues, including lymph nodes and spleen. This marks a notable advancement toward replacing PEG in LNP therapies and provides a clear path to optimizing POx-lipids for targeted vaccine and therapeutic applications.

articles_hidden.title: Psychedelics shift decision strategies and reconfigure orbitofrontal dynamics
articles_hidden.authors: C. Delgado-Sallent, S. A. Ahmed, A. Khawaja-Lopez, B. S. Lee, U. Mishra, R. A. Senne, S. Ramirez, B. B. Scott
articles_hidden.abstract: Psychedelics such as psilocybin and ketamine are attracting renewed attention as rapid-acting therapeutics, yet how they reshape cognitive computations remains poorly understood. To address this, we trained mice on a free-response perceptual decision-making task that disentangles bias-driven from sensory-guided strategies. Acute administration of psilocybin or ketamine slowed decision times while improving accuracy. Behavioral modeling combining drift diffusion and GLM-HMM approaches revealed that these effects were driven by increased decision thresholds and a shift toward sensory-engaged states. Whole-brain c-Fos mapping identified modulation of distributed task-related networks, including the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC). Calcium imaging showed that OFC population dynamics were reorganized under psychedelic conditions, with preserved task selectivity but altered temporal structure and shifted population correlations. Together, these findings indicate that psychedelics shift decision-making toward greater reliance on sensory evidence while reshaping cortical population dynamics, providing a system-level account of their effects on perceptual decisions.

articles_hidden.title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis CpsA interferes with the TBK1-p62 axis to inhibit xenophagy
articles_hidden.authors: Jully J. Sadadiwala, Sharvath Kathi, Ekansh Mittal, Keysha Patel, Thomas J. Brett, Jennifer A. Philips
articles_hidden.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) survives in macrophages by interfering with host lysosomal trafficking. Previously, we demonstrated that the Mtb protein, CpsA, is critical for bacterial survival in macrophages and infection in mice and that it can inhibit a noncanonical autophagy pathway. We also found that CpsA can interact with NDP52 and TAX1BP1, selective autophagy receptors that recognize cytosolic bacteria and target them for degradation, raising the possibility that CpsA also disrupts canonical autophagy. Here, we show that CpsA binds NDP52 and TAX1BP1 in their SKICH domains, which normally recruit the autophagy initiation machinery and TBK1. We demonstrate that CpsA prevents phagosomal recruitment of FIP200, a component of the autophagy initiation machinery, and blocks TBK1-dependent phosphorylation of p62, leading to impaired xenophagy. Our findings provide mechanistic insight into how Mtb subverts host defenses, revealing that in addition to blocking noncanonical autophagy, CpsA inhibits the TBK1-p62 axis to block xenophagy.

articles_hidden.title: A supergene converts queen-destined larvae into a novel caste in ants
articles_hidden.authors: Samuel V. Arsenault, Géraldine Bienvenu, Christina M. Daly, Waring Trible
articles_hidden.abstract: Novel morphological castes are a major source of phenotypic diversity in ants, but their genetic and developmental origins remain unresolved. Here we identify ergatoid , a 6.5-megabase dominant supergene that is necessary and sufficient to generate a novel caste in an undescribed species of moss ant, Leptothorax AF-erg . The resulting wingless (ergatoid) queens represent a distinct morphological population intermediate between workers and the ancestral winged queen caste. Morphometric and genotyping analyses show that ergatoid produces this caste by modifying queen-destined larvae rather than altering worker development or generating a new larval population. Transcriptomic and candidate gene analyses most strongly support altered ecdysone signaling and reduced insulin signaling as the developmental basis for this phenotype. These results show that a single large-effect genetic element can generate a novel caste by modifying a specific preexisting larval population, providing a molecular genetic explanation for how novel phenotypes can arise, more broadly, through modification of ancestral developmental plasticity.
