articles_hidden.title: Signals of rapid genetic change in reef coral over time and following mass mortality
articles_hidden.authors: Kate M. Quigley, Mikhail Matz
articles_hidden.abstract: Future coral reef persistence amidst accelerating climate change depends on rapid adaptive capacity. Sixteen years (2003 to 2019) of genetic data ( N  = 903) spanning mass mortality events uncovered polygenic signals of evolution and population structure in one Great Barrier Reef coral species ( Acropora tenuis ) and a similar but nonsignificant trend in another ( Acropora millepora ). Random forest revealed larger genetic shifts postbleaching compared to other time points, which was further supported by critical transitions in 34 years of remotely sensed thermal data (1985 to 2018). Concordant signals across multiple genomic ordinations confirmed significant shifts postbleaching. Specifically, three genetic variants contributed significantly to key random forest splits over time in A. tenuis . Significant genome-wide covariance in allele frequencies suggests shifts due to selection, not drift. This suggests that coral gene pools are changing, and measurable evolution can happen over subdecadal timescales, giving hope for coral resilience amid the ongoing climate crisis. However, we caution against overoptimism, and stress emissions must be urgently reduced.

articles_hidden.title: Rapid intensification of summer convective precipitation in New England
articles_hidden.authors: Jared M. Kodero, Jung-Eun Lee
articles_hidden.abstract: Anthropogenic warming is intensifying precipitation extremes, yet how subdaily convective rainfall responds in historically stratiform-dominated midlatitude regions remains poorly constrained. Using four decades of hourly station observations and reanalysis data, we show that summer convective precipitation has intensified across much of New England and surrounding regions from 1980 to 2020, with high-intensity events increasing in higher latitudes. Extreme convective rainfall scales at ∼13 to 14% per degree Celsius, nearly twice the Clausius-Clapeyron rate and significantly faster than stratiform precipitation. This intensification is accompanied by shorter event durations, increased moisture convergence, enhanced convective instability, and reduced antecedent soil moisture. Our results indicate a warming-driven shift toward convective dominance linked to changes in midlatitude circulation, reduced meridional temperature gradient, and land-atmosphere coupling, placing New England within an emerging poleward extension of the summer convective regime.

articles_hidden.title: Probabilistic neural code for subjective value and metacognition in human cortex
articles_hidden.authors: Ling Huang, Hui-Kuan Chung, Hsin-Hung Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Subjective value underlies many everyday decisions, yet the neural representations supporting these valuations are inherently noisy and subject to uncertainty. Whether humans have metacognitive access to this uncertainty and how this access is supported neurally remain unclear. Here, we provide converging behavioral and neural evidence that subjective value is represented probabilistically in the human brain. Behaviorally, participants’ uncertainty reports tracked trial-by-trial fluctuations in valuation. Neurally, we decoded probability distributions over value from functional magnetic resonance imaging activity in ventromedial prefrontal and orbitofrontal cortex, and superior parietal lobe and intraparietal sulcus. Decoded neural uncertainty predicted behaviorally reported uncertainty across trial, item, and individual levels. Moreover, predicting behavioral uncertainty required modeling the covariance structure of population noise. These findings indicate that neural populations jointly encode value and uncertainty, extending probabilistic population coding from perception, working memory to subjective value, and providing a neural basis for metacognitive access to uncertainty in value-based decisions.

articles_hidden.title: Sequential anion chemistry enables dynamic interphase regulation in high-voltage LiCoO 2
articles_hidden.authors: Lu Chen, Kai Cui, Guoqiang He, Yanxin Jiang, Chunlei Song, Nanshan Chen, Zhiqiang Yang, Junjie Chen, Chun Zeng, Tianshuai Wang, Wenjia Li, Zhouguang Lu, Tianshou Zhao, Yiju Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries using LiCoO 2 cathodes have powered portable electronics for decades, yet their operation above 4.5 volts remains severely constrained by the unstable evolution of the cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI). Under high-voltage conditions, lattice oxygen release and continuous electrolyte oxidation progressively degrade interfacial integrity. Here, we report a diluent-mediated local solvation regulation strategy to decrease dissociative solvent molecules and induce dual anion selective redistribution around Li + , forming a sequential solvation motif that drives sequential anion interfacial chemistry. DFOB − preferentially decomposes to establish a robust initial CEI framework, while BF 4 − continuously drives interfacial reactions to dynamically repair CEI defects and quench reactive oxygen species generated from lattice oxygen release. This dynamic regulation mechanism effectively stabilizes LiCoO 2 under aggressive high-voltage cycling. Consequently, the LiCoO 2 cathode delivers stable performance for 500 cycles at 4.5 volts with 73.5% capacity retention even in a low-concentration ether-based electrolyte. Furthermore, graphite||LiCoO 2 pouch cell achieves an energy density of 265.8 watt-hours per kilogram and exhibits favorable low-temperature resilience, retaining 99.1% capacity after 700 cycles at −20°C. These findings provide critical mechanistic insights into how solvation structure–driven anion chemistry can govern interfacial stability and unlock high-voltage, extreme-condition lithium-ion batteries.

articles_hidden.title: DFT-assisted natural abundance 13 C zero-field NMR via optical magnetometry
articles_hidden.authors: Blake Andrews, Xiao Liu, Raphael Zumbrunn, Calvin Lee, Sahand Adibnia, Emanuel Druga, Martin Head-Gordon, Ashok Ajoy
articles_hidden.abstract: Zero-field (ZF) nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy probes nuclear J-couplings without homogeneous magnetic fields, enabling inexpensive and geometrically flexible detection, including through metal. However, its broader use for chemical analysis has been limited by sensitivity and the difficulty of predicting the dense ZF multiplets. Here we demonstrate natural-abundance (1.1%) carbon-13 ( 13 C) ZF spectroscopy on off-the-shelf liquids using a compact commercial rubidium-87 magnetometer without hyperpolarization or special preparation. Instrumental advances yield improved sensitivity, ≤250-millihertz linewidths, and >week-long stability, enabling isotopomer-resolved fingerprint spectra across a 13-molecule library, including rare (0.0121%) doubly 13 C-labeled species. In parallel, we demonstrate vibrationally corrected density functional theory (DFT) prediction of ZF spectra with good qualitative agreement. Comparing experiment with these calculations renders residual deviations as chemically informative, reporting on hydrogen bonding and ion pairing at high ionic strength. These results contribute toward DFT-assisted ZF NMR as a general platform for field constraint–free molecular identification and for extracting transient solution-state structure from responsive J-coupling observables.

articles_hidden.title: SMAD4 loss drives cancer chromosomal instability through transcription-replication conflict–associated replication stress
articles_hidden.authors: Atmika Paul, Gargee Joshi, Philipp Jungk, Simranjeet Kaur, Shengyu Yao, Ioannis Tsirkas, Nicolas Böhly, Maren Sitte, Gabriela Salinas, Stephan Hamperl, Maik Kschischo, Holger Bastians
articles_hidden.abstract: Cancer chromosomal instability (CIN) drives tumor evolution through generating structural and numerical chromosome aberrations. However, its molecular determinants remain poorly characterized. Here, we uncover a yet unrecognized role for the tumor suppressor SMAD4 as a key regulator of chromosomal stability. Mechanistically, loss of SMAD4 causes replication stress by promoting transcription-replication conflicts (TRCs) and induces subsequent mitotic errors, leading to the concomitant emergence of structural and numerical CIN. While the tumor suppressor function of SMAD4 has been predominantly attributed to transforming growth factor–β signaling, we find that its role in genome maintenance operates via bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling and its transcriptional target gene ID3 . Consequently, inhibition of BMP signaling mimics the loss of SMAD4 , while reexpression of SMAD4 or ID3 in SMAD4 -deficient colorectal or pancreatic cancer cells suppresses TRCs, replication stress, and mitotic errors. Our findings reveal a TRC- and replication stress–driven mechanism by which loss of BMP-SMAD4 signaling causes cancer CIN.

articles_hidden.title: Platelet glycoprotein Ib shapes the immune response during lung injury
articles_hidden.authors: David Köhler, Anna Biedritzky, Philipp Burkard, Chunguang Liang, Linyan Tang, Alice Bernard, Philipp Dignus, Tim Steiner, Tiago F. Granja, Claudia Eggstein, Chao Liu, Lina M. Serna-Higuita, Diana Dudziak, Thomas Dandekar, Valbona Mirakaj, Bernhard Nieswandt, Peter Rosenberger
articles_hidden.abstract: The acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a life-threatening, inflammatory disease state of the lung. Self-propagating inflammation within the alveolar space and excessive infiltration of neutrophils into the pulmonary airspace are the main mechanisms underlying the dysfunction. A role of platelets in the pathogenesis of ARDS is suggested, but the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. We hypothesized that platelet glycoprotein (GP)Ib is an important contributor of platelet activation in this context. To highlight the contribution of the GPIb to the acute phase of experimental ALI in mice, we exposed mice genetically lacking functional GPIb ( GPIb-IL-4tg ) and wild-type (WT) mice injected with a function blocking anti-GPIb antibody to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) inhalation. GPIb-IL-4tg mice as well as anti-GPIb–treated mice displayed reduced neutrophil infiltration of the alveolar space in response to LPS. GPIb-IL-4tg mice as well as anti-GPIb–treated WT mice showed reduced interactions of platelets with neutrophils in comparison to controls, resulting in reduced platelet-neutrophil complexes and mitigated formation of neutrophil extracellular traps. Since these mechanisms are important for defense against external invasion of pathogens, we exposed GPIb-IL-4tg mice to Klebsiella pneumoniae and found reduced survival with increased bacterial load in these animals. Last, translational evaluation of biosamples of patients with ARDS showed that patients with low plasma levels of the shed GPIbα ectodomain (glycocalicin) exhibited higher mortality and worsened overall outcome. Together, our study shows that GPIb is a central mediator of neutrophil migration into the alveolar space and the defense mechanisms against the external invasion of pathogens.

articles_hidden.title: From genetic risk factor to therapeutic target: The CREB3L4-GDF15 axis drives prostate cancer immune evasion
articles_hidden.authors: Tiange Wu, Enyao Huang, Likai Mao, Pengyu Liu, Tianyi Xia, Saisai Chen, Yifei Cheng, Ruixin Zhang, Kaihua Xue, Yurui Chen, Xiangyu Zhang, Xiejunhao Zheng, Yifan Liu, Shenghong Ju, Ming Chen, Wenchao Li, Bin Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: Advanced prostate cancer (PCa) is characterized by rapid progression and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, contributing to poor clinical outcomes and limited therapeutic responses. Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants as instrumental variables to assess causal associations while minimizing confounding and reverse causation. Through integrative proteogenomic analysis, including MR and colocalization across 438,178 males, we identified CREB3L4 as associated with PCa risk. CREB3L4 overexpression promoted tumor growth in mice, accompanied by activation of cholesterol metabolism, androgen receptor (AR) signaling, and immunosuppression. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed CREB3L4 enrichment in human PCa cells. Interaction analysis identified enhanced growth and differentiation factor (GDF) signaling in CREB3L4 + tumor cells, with CD8 + T cells as the primary receivers. Ligand–receptor analysis and coculture experiments identified GDF15 as the key mediator, through which tumor cells suppressed CD8 + T cell proliferation and activation via TGFBR2 signaling. In vivo, GDF15 neutralization attenuated CREB3L4-driven tumor growth and CD8 + T cell dysfunction, whereas prostate-specific CREB3L4 knockout or adeno-associated virus-mediated knockdown suppressed tumor growth and restored CD8 + T cell function. Clinical analyses confirmed elevated CREB3L4 and GDF15 expression in PCa, inversely associated with CD8 + T cell infiltration and immunotherapy response. Collectively, these findings reveal that CREB3L4 promotes AR signaling-mediated GDF15 expression, driving CD8 + T cell dysfunction and identifying the CREB3L4–GDF15 axis as a potential therapeutic target in PCa.

articles_hidden.title: Self-assembly of bacterial volumetric patterns directed by a synthetic reaction-diffusion circuit
articles_hidden.authors: Fuqing Wu, Changhan He, Samat Bayakhmetov, Duane Harris, Xin Fang, Javier Baez, Steven Ohnmacht, Qi Zhang, Xingwen Chen, Kyle R. Allison, Yang Kuang, Xiao Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Reaction-diffusion (RD) has long been proposed as a mechanism underlying biological pattern formation. However, quantitative frameworks linking circuit design to spatial organization remain limited. Here, we engineered a synthetic gene circuit, MINPAC, that couples gene expression regulation (reaction) with bacterial colony expansion and quorum sensing (diffusion) to guide bacterial cells to self-organize into periodic volumetric patterns across multiple scales, from single cells to three-dimensional colonies. The patterns exhibit robustness against environmental variations and size-dependent complexity. Mathematical modeling supports a clock-and-wavefront mechanism, where oscillatory gene expression interacts with outward expanding diffusions to generate these periodic spatial structures. Topological analysis reveals that specific network architecture is essential for pattern formation. Guided by model predictions, we further show that pattern complexity can be systematically tuned by gene dosage, with lower expression levels favoring multiple rings through faster dynamics. This work establishes a framework uniting circuit engineering and mathematical analysis for programming multicellular self-organization through RD mechanisms, with potential applications in regenerative medicine and biomaterials.

articles_hidden.title: Enzymatic degradation of a polyester-based thermoset composite resin by an engineered cutinase from Fusarium solani
articles_hidden.authors: Mikel Dolz, Matheo Berthet, Beatrice Mongili, Nuria Velasco, Alain Garillot, Julio Vidal-Navarro, Javier Viña-Gonzalez, Miguel Alcalde
articles_hidden.abstract: Thermoset composites have become indispensable high-performance materials across key industrial sectors. However, existing recycling methods have yet to deliver sustainable end-of-life solutions for these materials. Here, we report the engineering of a highly active and stable biocatalyst capable of depolymerizing polyester-based thermoset composites. First, a second-generation polyester resin was designed to enhance susceptibility to enzymatic attack. Cutinase from Fusarium solani was selected and subsequently engineered through a combination of directed evolution and computational design using two soluble surrogate motifs representative of the redesigned resin structure. The resulting variant, which incorporated 19 mutations, exhibited a 22-fold increase in activity and an 11°C improvement in melting temperature while achieving recombinant production titers at the gram-per-liter scale in yeast cultivated in fed-batch bioreactor. This engineered enzyme depolymerized the polyester resin with a total release of 6 mM (∼1.08 grams per liter) monomethyl phthalate. Together, to our knowledge, these findings constitute the first documented example of enzymatic degradation of a complex polyester resin from thermoset composite materials.

articles_hidden.title: Aclarubicin disrupts RNA polymerase II progression at replication-coupled histone genes
articles_hidden.authors: Kevin K. Nguyen, Matthew Wooten, Kami Ahmad, Steven Henikoff
articles_hidden.abstract: Anthracyclines are effective chemotherapeutic agents that cause DNA and chromatin damage. One member of the anthracyclines, aclarubicin, has gained therapeutic interest due to its ability to kill cancer cells through chromatin-based mechanisms, thus avoiding the off-target effects associated with DNA damage. However, the molecular mechanism of action leading to aclarubicin-induced chromatin damage remains elusive. Here we performed Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag) of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) and other transcriptional regulators in human cells following aclarubicin treatment. We found that aclarubicin strongly disrupts the replication-coupled histone genes, resulting in a nonproductive accumulation of Pol II transcription machinery at levels exceeding those at other genes. We attribute this sensitivity to the dense Pol II loading and rapid transcription of the histone genes, which intensify the chromatin-disrupting effects of aclarubicin. Together, our findings shed light on the mechanism of aclarubicin as an anticancer drug and point to the replication-coupled histone genes as a target for therapeutic intervention.

articles_hidden.title: Roseburia intestinalis counteracts TBEP-exacerbated atherosclerosis
articles_hidden.authors: Liangju Liu, Tiantian Gan, Liu Yang, Zhiwei Wang, Xiaowang Lv, Xiaoyan Wang, Ka Zhang, Hao Kan, Mengru Gao, Lilong Pan, Aiqin Mao, Tingting Zhou
articles_hidden.abstract: Interactions between serum metabolites and vascular endothelial cells directly influence atherosclerotic lesions. It is essential to identify and understand the effects of the complex profile of serum metabolites on vascular pathology. In this study, we found that coronary lesion severity positively correlated with serum levels of the organophosphate ester tris (2-butoxyethyl) phosphate (TBEP), while TBEP levels inversely correlated with gut Roseburia intestinalis abundance. Western diet supplemented with TBEP substantially exacerbated atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E −/− ( ApoE −/− ) mice. We found that TBEP enhanced AMP-activated protein kinase α (AMPKα) phosphorylation, reduced nuclear translocation of active sterol regulatory element–binding protein 1c (SREBP1c) fragments, suppressed Patatin-like phospholipase domain–containing protein 3 (PNPLA3) protein expression in endothelial cells, and increased lipid deposition. Oral R. intestinalis supplementation reduced fecal and serum TBEP levels and attenuated TBEP-driven atherosclerotic lesions. We highlight that TBEP aggravates endothelial lipid accumulation and atherosclerosis, suggesting that targeting gut microbiota may serve as a promising strategy against TBEP-exacerbated atherosclerosis.

articles_hidden.title: Solubility-driven morphological decoupling enables elastic electron-deficient semiconducting polymers for fully stretchable electronics
articles_hidden.authors: Hayeong Park, Qian Liu, Wenhao Li, Minji Chung, Gunmo Koo, Chien-Chung Shih, Christopher R. McNeill, Dongsheng Yan, Yang Wang, Shanshan Zhou, Mandar M. Shirolkar, Ruicheng Li, Aung Ko Ko Kyaw, Yunqi Liu, Prashant Sonar, Joon Hak Oh
articles_hidden.abstract: The development of fully stretchable electronics is limited by the scarcity of electron-deficient polymers that combine high electron mobility with mechanical elasticity. Here, we report a solubility-driven morphological decoupling strategy that mitigates this trade-off by incorporating ∼10% planar, insoluble PyF units into a semicrystalline PySe backbone. This approach yields a hierarchical morphology characterized by suppressed long-range crystallinity alongside robust local aggregation. Driven by strong fluorine (F)-sulfur (S) interactions, highly ordered face-on domains function as robust physical anchors, providing the polymer network with exceptional elasticity to reversibly dissipate stress and preserve charge percolation pathways. Consequently, the resulting terpolymer largely relieves the long-standing trade-off between charge transport and mechanical stretchability, delivering a near-unity initial electron mobility (∼1.0 square centimeter per volt per second) and retaining 0.5 square centimeters per volt per second even under 100% applied strain, representing the highest performance reported to date. To demonstrate the practical utility of this system, we fabricated stretchable ambipolar inverters and phototransistors that maintain high performance under severe deformation. Notably, the phototransistors sustain an exceptional responsivity of 15.8 amperes per watt and an external quantum efficiency exceeding 2900% at 100% strain. These results establish a powerful blueprint for intrinsically elastic semiconductors, enabling the realization of high-performance, fully deformable optoelectronic systems.

articles_hidden.title: Evolution of MEIS transcription factor activity during metazoan neural development—born to be wild
articles_hidden.authors: Pavel Fedarenchik, Hanna Polevoy, Yael Volovik, Emil Aamar, Mohammed Mahroum, Gilad Barshad, Adi Salzberg, Dale Frank
articles_hidden.abstract: Meis TALE-class proteins pattern vertebrate neural tissue, inducing hindbrain and neural crest in Xenopus laevis embryos. Meis orthologs have two conserved regions: (i) Meis-specific domain and (ii) Meis-specific TALE homeodomain. Meis homeodomain proteins are present in “ancient” metazoans-eucaryotes like cnidarians, placozoans, and protozoans. We asked: When during metazoan evolution did Meis proteins acquire functionality to induce neural pattern? Using structure-function analysis in Xenopus , we show that the Meis-specific and Meis homeodomains suffice to induce the spinal cord but not the hindbrain. Meis proteins share a functionally conserved carboxyl-terminal transcription activation domain inducing the hindbrain. Ancient Meis proteins from Trichoplax and chlorophyte algae have a conserved Meis homeodomain, but lack the Meis-specific domain. Unexpectedly, these ancestral proteins robustly induce hindbrain and neural crest in Xenopus , unlike metazoan proteins requiring the Meis-specific domain. Thus, in early eukaryotes, Meis prototypes were “born to be wild,” having the intrinsic capacity to induce vertebrate structures like hindbrain and neural crest, despite predating them.

articles_hidden.title: SeqA-mediated sister loci cohesion regulates the efficiency and fidelity of DNA double-strand break repair across the E. coli genome
articles_hidden.authors: Deepak K. Singh, Amir Faraz, Nuha A. Khan, Jebin Babu, T. Sabari Sankar, David Bates, Mohan C. Joshi
articles_hidden.abstract: In Escherichia coli , SeqA-mediated cohesion at snap loci on the right replichore persists longer, but its role in DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair remains untested. Here, we show that site-specific DSBs at snap loci confer higher cell survival than nonsnap loci. With perturbations affecting sister cohesion [Δ seqA , topoisomerase IV overexpression (T4-OE)], this survival advantage was progressively reduced, with the combined Δ seqA T4-OE strain retaining only a transient advantage. The increased survival correlates with faster repair, reflected by rapid restoration of locus copy number and shorter-lived, thinner RecA–green fluorescent protein filaments. Consistent with more accurate repair, snap loci exhibited lower mutation accumulation under normal and antibiotic stress conditions. Comparative genome analysis of E. coli strains revealed higher GATC motif counts and higher sequence conservation. Together, these findings suggest that the chromosomal organization associated with prolonged sister cohesion at snap loci promotes efficient homologous recombination–mediated DSB repair and contributes to genome conservation.

articles_hidden.title: Surface-passivated high-entropy oxide-derived catalysts for stable dry reforming of methane
articles_hidden.authors: Qingju Wang, Xinhui Lu, Kevin M. Siniard, Hailing Yu, Guoqiang Shen, Hao Chen, Xin Wang, Caiqi Wang, Jacob Smith, Jue Liu, Yuanpeng Zhang, Alexander S. Ivanov, Michael Richard Koehler, Shuai Yuan, De-en Jiang, Miaofang Chi, Zili Wu, Zhenzhen Yang, Sheng Dai
articles_hidden.abstract: Dry reforming of methane (DRM) enables the co-valorization of CO 2 and CH 4 into syngas, yet the development of sintering- and coking-resistant catalysts that suppress CH 4 cracking while accelerating coke gasification without compromising reaction efficiency remains a major challenge. Here, we address this challenge by employing surface-passivated catalysts derived from high-entropy oxides (HEOs) for stable DRM operation. Alkaline earth metal cation (M 2+ )-doped HEOs were designed to function without pretreatment and exhibited resistance to sintering and coking. This robustness arises from the in situ exsolution of NiCuCo alloy nanoparticles encapsulated within a multifunctional BaCO 3 overlayer, enabled by HEO-stabilized Ba incorporation and Ba-mediated surface reconstruction during DRM. This adaptive architecture passivates deep CH 4 cracking, promotes CO 2 activation, accelerates coke gasification, and thereby sustains catalytic efficiency and durability. Comprehensive spectroscopic, microscopic, and diffraction analyses revealed the structural dynamics and mechanistic pathways governing catalyst evolution under DRM conditions.

articles_hidden.title: Evolution of trans-regulatory architecture and gene expression dosage compensation after genome duplication
articles_hidden.authors: Célian Diblasi, Domniki Manousi, David Hazlerigg, Jonas Paulsen, Fabiana Patalano, Tomasz Podgorniak, Lars Grønvold, Nicola Jane Barson, Simen Rød Sandve, Marie Saitou
articles_hidden.abstract: Whole-genome duplication (WGD) through polyploidization has played a major role in genome evolution across eukaryotes. While many well-studied WGDs involve allopolyploidization, autopolyploidization provides a distinct context because duplicated chromosomes initially originate from within the same species and retain high sequence similarity. A major consequence of WGD is the rewiring of gene regulatory networks, partly driven by selection on gene expression dosage. In multicellular organisms, evidence for dosage balance selection has relied largely on comparative patterns of duplicate gene retention and expression, with few studies directly examining regulatory architecture after WGD. Here, we analyzed a large-scale eQTL dataset from Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ), which experienced a salmonid-specific autopolyploid WGD approximately 80 to 100 million years ago. We found that trans-regulatory connections were preferentially retained between WGD-derived syntenic regions and that syntenic trans-eQTL pairs showed elevated three-dimensional genomic contact, suggesting partial preservation of spatial proximity between duplicated chromosomal regions. Overall, 230 duplicated gene pairs (5%) shared eQTLs, suggesting conserved regulatory control. Moreover, 16 gene pairs showed genotype-dependent compensatory expression effects mediated by a common regulator, consistent with predictions of the dosage balance hypothesis. These gene pairs were significantly enriched in late-rediploidizing regions. Our results indicate that a small subset of duplicated genes have retained dosage-balanced regulatory architecture long after WGD.

articles_hidden.title: Targeting METTL3 protects against acetaminophen-induced liver injury through HAPTOGLOBIN/CD163 macrophage axis
articles_hidden.authors: Huaxin Chen, Silin Tu, Bo Cui, Zhancheng Zeng, Xuanyong Chen, Shuai Dong, Yanli Li, Shanshan Yu, Xiao Liu, Ruiqi Xiao, Jing Guo, Xiaoqi Liang, Lijie Pan, Jiajie Chu, Yiju Huang, Chang Liu, Guo Lv, Yiwang Zhang, Wenjie Chen, Qi Zhang, Yan Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: Acetaminophen (APAP) overdose is the most common cause of drug-induced liver injury (DILI), with limited treatment options. N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) is the most abundant internal epitranscriptomic modification in eukaryotic RNAs and is involved in various physiological and pathological processes, serving as a potential therapeutic target for many diseases. However, little is known about the role of m 6 A in DILI. Here, we found that intrahepatic expression of Methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3), the core catalytic subunit of RNA m 6 A methyltransferase complex, was elevated in patients with DILI and mouse DILI models. Hepatocyte-specific knockout of METTL3, achieved via either Alb-Cre ERT2 –driven recombination or adeno-associated virus (AAV)–mediated delivery of Cre, significantly protected from APAP-induced hepatotoxicity in both male and female mice. Mechanistically, hepatic METTL3 deficiency reduced m 6 A deposition on acute-phase protein haptoglobin ( Hp ) transcripts and promoted Hp transcription and translation in hepatocytes. Increased HP secreted by hepatocytes bound to its receptor CD163, expressed explicitly on macrophages, and induced highly phagocytic and anti-inflammatory polarization of macrophages, finally reducing APAP-induced hepatic injury. Moreover, two different METTL3 inhibitors, JNJ64619178 and STM2457, effectively alleviated APAP-induced liver injury. Our study thus demonstrated that hepatic inhibition of METTL3 protected against APAP-induced liver injury by promoting the cross-talk between hepatocytes and macrophages through HP/CD163, underscoring the potential of targeting METTL3 as a promising therapy for APAP overdose.

articles_hidden.title: An all-magnonic neuron with tunable fading memory
articles_hidden.authors: David Breitbach, Moritz Bechberger, Hanadi Mortada, Björn Heinz, Roman Verba, Qi Wang, Carsten Dubs, Mario Carpentieri, Giovanni Finocchio, Davi Rodrigues, Alexandre Abbass Hamadeh, Philipp Pirro
articles_hidden.abstract: Magnonics offers nanometer-scale wave propagation and strong nonlinearities, making it attractive for neuromorphic applications such as artificial neurons. Yet, magnonic elements with interconnections solely within the magnonic system remain challenging, preventing the realization of interconnected magnonic neurons to date. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an all-magnonic neuron that reacts to magnon inputs with thresholded, amplified magnon firing and subsequent self-reset, enabling all-magnonic operation and cascading. Our approach is based on micro-antenna excitation on an ultralow damping garnet with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, where we exploit the positive magnon frequency shift to realize nonlinear activation. Using Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy, we uncover a transient neuron response with tunable fading memory: A 25% change in pump power results in a three-order-of-magnitude tuning in memory time, which we harness, demonstrating temporal integration of up to 50 magnon pulses. Last, we realize neuron triggering in a cascade of three neurons, highlighting its potential for connected magnonic circuits.

articles_hidden.title: Resolving topological obstructions to vectorial structured field control
articles_hidden.authors: An Aloysius Wang, Yuxi Cai, Yifei Ma, Patrick S. Salter, Chao He
articles_hidden.abstract: The use of structured matter, such as optical retarders, for vectorial control is a well-established and widely used technique in modern optics, and has driven continued advances in the manipulation of complex, spatially varying vectorial fields. However, achieving arbitrary field conversion typically requires the use of cascaded elements, as intrinsic physical and fabrication constraints fundamentally limit individual devices to a restricted subset of transformations. This results in an overall continuous transformation potentially failing to be continuous at the level of the parameters of the cascade, leading to detrimental engineering consequences such as the introduction of complex, discontinuous aberrations that disrupt important topological properties of the underlying light and matter fields. In this work, we establish a mathematical framework for analyzing the topological difficulties that emerge in the decomposition of an overall transformation into individual layers, and for determining the minimal depth required to overcome them. The strategy introduced provides a general pathway for optimizing designs for vectorial field control and matter field generation, with particular importance for the manipulation of topological phases in optical polarization fields, such as Stokes skyrmions, where continuity is of vital importance.

articles_hidden.title: Atomic-scale visualization and assignment of contaminant adsorption geometries at mineral surfaces
articles_hidden.authors: Bo Zhao, Ying Zhao, Chunguang Liu, Christos Christodoulatos, Yuxin Long, Meng Ji, Tsengming Chou, Qiantao Shi, Beidou Xi, Xiaoguang Meng
articles_hidden.abstract: Directly resolving coexisting adsorption geometries at mineral-water interfaces and assigning them to crystallographic sites remains challenging in environmental geochemistry. Ensemble methods provide population-averaged structural constraints but may obscure minor or similar configurations and do not directly reveal crystallographic registry. Here, we establish an experimentally constrained framework integrating controlled off-axis high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM), multislice simulations, and density functional theory (DFT) to resolve crystallographic adsorption registries and corresponding structures. For selenium(IV) adsorption on hematite (001), comparison of apparent selenium positions with multislice simulations accounting for tilt-induced registry shifts supports assignment to iron-iron bridge and oxygen-centered hollow registries. DFT favors monodentate inner-sphere structures compatible with these registries. Extension to lead(II) and uranium(VI) on multiple hematite facets demonstrates the transferability of the off-axis imaging strategy for resolving sparse high- Z interfacial species. This work enables real-space, site-resolved adsorption-structure analysis that complements ensemble-averaged structural methods and provides a basis for mechanistic models of contaminant retention and structure-guided sorbent design.

articles_hidden.title: Cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) binds talin and is anchored at the postsynaptic density by direct PDZ interactions
articles_hidden.authors: Yasumi Otani, Emily Goodall, Vignesh Srinivasan, Neil J. Ball, Samuel F. H. Barnett, Youlim Hwang, Dominic P. Byrne, Tobias Zech, Juha Saarikangas, Benjamin T. Goult
articles_hidden.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) is a serine/threonine kinase essential for brain development and function. Mutations in CDKL5 cause CDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD), a severe early-onset epileptic encephalopathy associated with impaired synapse formation and function. However, how CDKL5 mutations disrupt synaptic function remains unclear. Here, we show that the major neuronal isoform of CDKL5 contains a C-terminal PDZ domain–binding motif that mediates direct binding to PSD-95 and SHANK PDZ domains and recruits CDKL5 to the postsynaptic density. Disrupting this motif mislocalized CDKL5, reduced dendritic spine density, and impaired spine maturation. We also show that the CDKL5 kinase domain binds the R8 rod domain of the mechanosensitive scaffold talin. Mutation of the talin-binding interface or reduced cellular contractility altered CDKL5 positioning relative to focal adhesions. These findings define how CDKL5 is targeted to synapses, suggest that talin mechanoswitching may position CDKL5 kinase activity, and highlight the importance of C-terminal anchoring for interpreting pathogenic truncations.

articles_hidden.title: Tuning microswimmer motility by liposome encapsulation: A membrane clutch enables controlled swimming and cargo transport
articles_hidden.authors: Koichiro Akiyama, Sota Hamaguchi, Hiromasa Shiraiwa, Shunsuke Shiomi, Tomoyuki Kaneko, Masahito Hayashi, Daiki Matsunaga
articles_hidden.abstract: Inspired by biology’s use of vesicles for targeted transport, many studies have propelled liposomes with active matter, creating synthetic systems that can be viewed as microscale biohybrid robots. Nevertheless, the underlying motility mechanisms from a hydrodynamic perspective are often unresolved, and reliable velocity control remains challenging. In the present study, we use our previously introduced biohybrid system termed the chlamylipo, in which the motile alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii is encapsulated within a giant liposome, as a model system to investigate how liposome encapsulation regulates microswimmer motility under controlled perturbations. From a fluid mechanical perspective, we establish a deformation-velocity expression that incorporates liposome radius, beating frequency, and membrane protrusion. We further show that motility can be reversibly switched by incorporating light-responsive lipids, with the liposome acting as a “clutch” that modulates membrane protrusion. To demonstrate its transport function, we further show cargo loading, carrying, and triggered release. These results show that liposome encapsulation can convert a motile microorganism into a controllable carrier, with the membrane acting as a clutch that regulates swimming and, therefore, cargo transport.

articles_hidden.title: A flexible fiber–based artificial chemical postsynapse
articles_hidden.authors: Tran Quang Trung, Montri Meeseepong, Ok-Hyeon Kim, Guangyu Wang, Sandeep Kaushal, Rohan Machhindra Hagawane, Deepak Ganesan, Phuc Nguyen, Hyun Jung Lee, Nae-Eung Lee
articles_hidden.abstract: Most artificial synapses, which are designed to communicate with biological neural systems and exhibit neuron-like functions, rely primarily on electrical signals. Biotic-abiotic neural interfaces that use artificial synapses to communicate with biological synapses via chemical neurotransmitters while exhibiting synaptic plasticity are of great interest. Here, we present an artificial chemical postsynapse that directly interfaces with biological systems through dopamine (DA) neurotransmitters and demonstrates synaptic plasticity–like behavior. The artificial postsynapse of a flexible fiber–based organic electrochemical transistor (F-OECT) with a capacitive-like charging gate electrode, which combines volumetric charge storage and DA-sensing functionalities, can detect pulsatile DA release and transduce these sensing signals with plasticity-like behavior. The F-OECT synapse emulates key synaptic functions observed in biological synapses by responding to pulse-like DA release from dopaminergic cells. We also implanted fiber-based artificial postsynapses into a mouse brain to study their basic interaction with DA release and to evaluate biocompatibility.

articles_hidden.title: Anisotropic field suppression of charge order reveals orbital-selective Kondo hybridization in UTe 2
articles_hidden.authors: Nileema Sharma, Fangjun Cheng, Hyeok-Jun Yang, Matthew Toole, James McKenzie, Mitchell M. Bordelon, Sean M. Thomas, Priscila F. S. Rosa, Yi-Ting Hsu, Xiaolong Liu
articles_hidden.abstract: UTe 2 is a rare correlated quantum material where unconventional density-wave orders, Kondo physics, spin-triplet pairing, and reentrant superconductivity coexist. Because superconductivity emerges from a strongly correlated normal state, identifying and controlling intertwined normal-state orders are essential for understanding the electronic landscape where superconductivity arises. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy in a vector magnetic field, we uncover a staggered charge density wave (CDW) in high-quality UTe 2 crystals. This CDW exhibits a strong directional field response: It is completely quenched by a modest 1.7-tesla magnetic field along the quasi–one-dimensional uranium-chain direction while remaining robust against fields along other crystallographic axes. This anisotropy suggests an orbital-driven field-tuned quantum phase transition. Unexpectedly, the same field orientation concurrently suppresses the 5f Kondo resonance. Modeling indicates a switch in the dominant hybridization channel from Te 5 p- U 5 f to U 6 d- U 5 f coupling, suggesting an intimate interplay between CDW and the Kondo effect.

articles_hidden.title: Mantle redox states reveal contrasting styles of late Archean lithospheric subduction
articles_hidden.authors: Lei Gao, Wei Wang, Peter A. Cawood, Shuwen Liu, Kunfeng Qiu, Fangyang Hu, Guozheng Sun, Xuetang Jiang, Jincheng Hu, Tengxu Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Lithospheric recycling has operated through most of Earth’s history, likely involving subduction since the late Archean. However, the thermal structure and geometry of such subduction systems remain poorly constrained. Here, we quantify the oxygen fugacity ( f O 2 ) of mantle sources modified by recycled supracrustal materials in the North China Craton. By integrating mantle f O 2 estimation, thermodynamic simulation of lithospheric structures, and other geological constraints, we infer two styles of lithospheric subduction with contrasting slab-dip angles. The dominant style shows shallow slab-dip angles, a more reduced arc mantle and a thick overriding lithosphere. The subsidiary, localized style exhibits relatively steep slab-dip angles, a more oxidized mantle source and a thinner overriding lithosphere. In contrast to the prevalence of steep subduction on the modern Earth, flat (or shallow) subduction profoundly shaped the distinctive tectonic evolution of the early Earth, whereas the localized development of steep subduction may have enhanced mantle oxidation and strengthened coupling between Earth’s deep interior and surface environments.

articles_hidden.title: DAS reveals continuous, multicore architecture of the Alpine Fault, New Zealand
articles_hidden.authors: Voon Hui Lai, Meghan S. Miller, Yujie Wang, Xin Wang, Brian Kennett, John Townend
articles_hidden.abstract: The Alpine Fault accommodates much of the relative motion between the Australian and Pacific plates in southern New Zealand and is expected to produce large earthquakes in coming decades. How slip evolves and what ground motions are produced during the next rupture are expected to depend strongly on the continuity of principal slip zones and overall fault width. Despite extensive study, the along-strike structure of the fault and its continuity across segment boundaries remain poorly constrained. Here, we use distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) along a 30-kilometer fiber-optic array crossing the Alpine Fault to record fault-zone guided waves (FZGWs) from local earthquakes. The FZGW observations, supported by numerical modeling and passive seismic imaging, reveal up to six narrow (∼10 meters) fault cores embedded within a 200-meter-wide low-velocity zone interpreted as the fault’s inner damage zone. The principal fault core feature persists for ∼180 kilometers along strike between the Central and South Westland segments, crossing a pronounced geometric and kinematic boundary. The inferred damage zone width is consistent with empirical scaling for large-displacement faults. These results demonstrate that DAS can resolve fault-zone architecture at previously inaccessible scales and bridge geological and geophysical inferences, providing constraints on fault continuity, slip localization, and the potential for multisegment rupture in mature plate-boundary systems.

articles_hidden.title: Umbilical cord structure shapes feto-maternal heat transfer across mammals
articles_hidden.authors: Tianran Wan, Davis Laundon, Shier Nee Saw, Nicholas Cheng, Hwee Kuan Lee, Edward D. Johnstone, Oliver E. Jensen, Rohan M. Lewis, Igor L. Chernyavsky
articles_hidden.abstract: The umbilical cord varies widely across placental mammals, yet the functional consequences of this structural diversity remain unclear. We compared cord anatomy across 130 mammal species, reconstructed ancestral states, and combined multimodal imaging with physics-based modeling of oxygen and heat transfer. Reconstructions indicate that the ancestral umbilical cord was uncoiled, with three vessels and an allantoic duct; the human combination of coiling with loss of the duct is rare. Across species, vessel number, duct persistence, and cord length increase with birth weight. Modeling predicts that oxygen delivery remains near maximal across architectures but that placental heat loss depends more strongly on umbilical flow and on cord length and coiling, suggesting more efficient cooling in larger mammals. Microscopy and ultrasound imaging reveal geometric vessel layouts, including a human triple helix, consistent with configurations predicted to reduce intervessel heat shunting. As fetuses must dissipate heat through the mother, these results link cord morphology, evolution, and fetal thermal resilience.

articles_hidden.title: Skeletal muscle proteomics reveals metabolic phenotype–specific adaptations to exercise training in health, obesity, and type 2 diabetes
articles_hidden.authors: Farina L. Schlabs, Jeppe Kjærgaard, Rikke Kruse, Dimitrius Santiago P.S.F. Guimarães, Nigel Kurgan, Frederic Schrøder Wenzel Arendrup, Maria Houborg Petersen, Niels Ørtenblad, Martin Eisemann de Almeida, Anders H. Lund, Kei Sakamoto, Juleen R. Zierath, Anna Krook, Kurt Højlund, Atul S. Deshmukh
articles_hidden.abstract: Exercise training improves metabolic health, including whole-body insulin sensitivity, yet the molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We applied proteomics and phosphoproteomics to skeletal muscle biopsies from lean men, and men with obesity or type 2 diabetes (T2D), obtained before and after 8 weeks of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) under basal and insulin-stimulated conditions. Before HIIT, protein expression showed a stepwise progression from lean to obesity to T2D. HIIT induced more pronounced proteomic remodeling in obesity and T2D compared with lean men, characterized by increased mitochondrial and decreased proteasomal contents. Phosphoproteomic responses were diagnosis dependent, revealing distinct insulin signaling adaptations. Mechanistically, AMP-activated protein kinase γ2 (AMPKγ2) emerged as a prominent HIIT-regulated protein, exhibiting increased incorporation into AMPKα2β2 complexes across all phenotypes, and AMPKγ2 overexpression in human myotubes increased basal glucose oxidation. These findings elucidate molecular pathways underlying exercise-induced insulin sensitization and suggest AMPKγ2 as a candidate regulator for exercise-induced metabolic adaptation.

articles_hidden.title: LONP-1 deficiency causes dysregulated protein synthesis within mitochondria that is suppressed by mitoribosomal mutations
articles_hidden.authors: Levi D. Ali, Avijit Mallick, Yunguang Du, Rui Li, Lihua J. Zhu, Kuang Shen, Cole M. Haynes
articles_hidden.abstract: Mitochondrial homeostasis is maintained by molecular chaperones and proteases located within the organelle. The mitochondrial matrix-localized protease LONP-1 degrades oxidatively damaged or misfolded proteins. Importantly, LONP-1 also regulates mitochondrial DNA replication. Here, we show that mutations in C. elegans that impair LONP-1 function cause dysregulation of mitochondrial DNA replication, mitochondrial RNA transcription and protein synthesis within the mitochondrial matrix. LONP-1 deficient worms had reduced levels of oxidative phosphorylation proteins despite increased mtDNA-encoded protein synthesis. Via a forward genetic screen, we identified three mutations that restored mitochondrial function and the rate of development in lonp-1 mutants to levels comparable to those in wildtype worms. Interestingly, all three suppressor mutations were found in genes encoding mitochondrial ribosome proteins. A point mutation in the mitochondrial ribosome protein MRPS-38 restored oxidative phosphorylation in lonp-1 mutant worms. Combined, our results suggest that LONP-1 regulates mitochondrial translation and that suppressor mutations within mrps-38 or mrps-15 can enhance oxidative phosphorylation complex assembly when LONP-1 function is diminished.

articles_hidden.title: Denoised vibrometry reveals noncanonical filtering at the apex of the cochlea
articles_hidden.authors: George W. S. Burwood, Pierre Hakizimana, Karl Grosh, Wajiha Zaidi, Ruikang K. Wang, Alfred L. Nuttall, Anders Fridberger
articles_hidden.abstract: How do mammals distinguish sounds with different pitch? Prevailing theory states that each position along the cochlear spiral responds best to one single stimulus frequency, forming a frequency-to-place (tonotopic) map that is preserved throughout the auditory pathways. Whether this holds in the low-frequency cochlear apex, a region important for vocal communication but technically challenging to study, is unknown. Using a differential noise-canceling technique, we recorded sound-evoked motion near the lower limit of hearing. Apical locations often had two best frequencies, contradicting the assumption of one-to-one frequency-to-place mapping. Spatially distant regions responded similarly, and brief sounds evoked synchronized motion across large distances, revealing an unusual energy propagation mode. Morphology and mathematical analyses corroborate these findings, showing that tonotopy breaks down at the apex of the cochlea. These results have important implications for cochlear implants, which currently assume tonotopic organization throughout the cochlea.

articles_hidden.title: Interfacing ultrafast single-photon-level fields with an atomic ensemble
articles_hidden.authors: Kai Shinbrough, Tegan Loveridge, Benjamin D. Hunt, Sehyun Park, Kathleen Oolman, Thomas O. Reboli, J. Gary Eden, Virginia O. Lorenz
articles_hidden.abstract: Ultrafast photons—with pulse durations on the order of 100 femtoseconds—are typical of high-rate, high-purity, entangled photon-pair sources. Efficient, coherent mapping between these states and matter-based quantum systems is an important problem in quantum optics and could enable applications in quantum frequency conversion, bandwidth conversion, and local quantum information processing at gigahertz speeds. This coherent mapping is also the initial storage step in matter-based photonic quantum memory, which can enhance multiphoton rates and allow for synchronization in quantum repeaters. Here, we use a collisionally broadened neutral atomic barium ensemble to demonstrate a quantum-compatible light-matter interface with storage efficiency of 95.6 ± 0.3%, total internal efficiency of 31 ± 1%, and noise contributions of <10 −4 photons per pulse. Using the simultaneous efficiency, bandwidth, and noise performance of this interface, we perform a full amplitude and phase reconstruction via spectral interferometry of single-photon-level fields retrieved from the interface.

articles_hidden.title: A divergent bat orthopneumovirus with zoonotic potential constrained by RSV adaptive immunity and broad-spectrum treatment
articles_hidden.authors: Wendy K. Jo, Sibylle Haid, Tabea Binger, Sebastian Brünink, Dickson Dei, Christian Drosten, Arne Kühne, Janine Müller, Samuel Oppong, Valeria Penner, Anita Wadagni, Anges Yadouleton, Thomas Pietschmann, Jan Felix Drexler
articles_hidden.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; genus Orthopneumovirus ) causes severe pneumonia in young children worldwide, yet the zoonotic potential of the few known nonhuman animal orthopneumoviruses remains unknown. Here, we characterized a highly divergent bat orthopneumovirus (BPV) from West African straw-colored fruit bats and established a systematic framework for evaluating zoonotic risk posed by an emerging viral pathogen. Epidemiologic data in bats showed a low viral detection rate (24 of 1778 RT-PCR positive) and low seroprevalence (6 of 66 IgG IFA positive), suggesting BPV episodic circulation potentially sustained in immunologically naïve bats following bat birthing events. Near-complete genomes from two BPV genetic variants revealed prototypic orthopneumovirus organization, but lacked the SH viroporin-encoding gene present in RSV. Functional experiments showed that BPV NS1/NS2 antagonized human interferon β responses, and that BPV pseudoviruses entered human cells (4.5- to 53.5-fold less efficiently than RSV), while being cross-neutralized by human RSV-reactive antisera, together suggesting zoonotic traits that may be partly constrained by cross-protective immunity. BPV escaped neutralization by RSV-specific therapeutic palivizumab and inhibition by lonafarnib, but remained susceptible to MPE8, a broad-spectrum monoclonal antibody that targets the conserved pneumovirus antigenic site III. These findings identify zoonotic traits of a divergent bat pneumovirus while suggesting potential protective value of preexisting RSV immunity and broad-spectrum interventions, which has implications for pandemic preparedness. Whether cross-protection in the human population may change by the advent of RSV vaccination warrants investigation. Efforts to investigate orthopneumovirus host shifts, reservoir studies, and development of broadly reactive orthopneumovirus vaccines and antivirals are warranted.

articles_hidden.title: Geophysics-informed hydrologic modeling reveals contrasting regolith and bedrock responses of headwater catchments to warming
articles_hidden.authors: Chen Xiong, Hang Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: Predicting how warming reshapes headwater streamflow requires distinguishing shallow and deep subsurface contributions, which remain difficult to constrain in catchment-scale models. We use seismic P-wave velocity to partition the critical zone into regolith and fractured bedrock domains within a three-dimensional physically based model and develop a particle-based attribution method to quantify their streamflow contributions and source-water ages across realizations spanning diverse hydraulic configurations. Across these realizations, warming produces contrasting subsurface hydrologic responses: Regolith-sourced streamflow generally becomes slightly younger, whereas fractured bedrock-sourced streamflow generally ages. This contrast arises because warming increases evapotranspiration and alters snow accumulation and melt timing, reducing effective recharge and lowering fractured-bedrock saturation. Declining recharge slows water transit and shifts fractured-bedrock-sourced water toward longer flow paths. Our results suggest that warming may reduce fractured-bedrock water renewal, with implications for the buffering role of bedrock water storage and for prolonged retention of legacy contaminants.

articles_hidden.title: Monolithic tiered microlithography for stretchable multilayer electronics with high-density, soft, and ultrathin VIAs
articles_hidden.authors: Xinjian Xie, Guangrui Ju, Xiongwei Luo, Shengwei Feng, Hongjiao Li, Yijun Zhang, Wenqian Feng
articles_hidden.abstract: Stretchable multilayer electronics that sustain reliable electrical performance under mechanical deformation are critical for advanced skin-like devices. A remaining challenge is the development of high-density, soft, and ultrathin vertical interconnect accesses (VIAs) that enable reliable electrical interconnection in flexible and stretchable circuits, particularly at small feature sizes. Here, we present a three-dimensional (3D), tier-by-tier photolithography strategy using PEDOT-based conductors and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)–based insulators, each photocurable within 10 seconds, to directly pattern soft VIAs and planar interconnects across lithographically defined PDMS openings. Maskless, full-field exposure enables thousands of in-plane and through-plane electrical connections in a single step, bypassing conventional hole-by-hole fabrication and manual VIA-to-pad alignment. The multilayer stack ensures minimal thickness, matched mechanical compliance, and robust conduction and insulation, enabling soft VIAs to preserve cross-layer electrical performance. Integration of lithographically defined cutouts and perforations yields breathable, conformal bioelectronics with skin-friendliness and stable signal acquisition in wearable wireless ECG monitoring. This multilayer 3D electronics platform can be extended to biomolecular sensing in soft organs, where thin, integrated, and stretchable designs are essential.

articles_hidden.title: Hybrid transverse thermoelectric conversion based on off-diagonal Peltier and Ettingshausen effects in a junction-less single material
articles_hidden.authors: Atsushi Takahagi, Yosuke Goto, Masayuki Murata, Hosei Nagano, Ken-ichi Uchida
articles_hidden.abstract: Transverse thermoelectric conversion, which interconverts heat and charge currents in orthogonal directions, is gaining attention as a driving principle for next-generation thermal management devices that do not require dissimilar material junctions or complex module structures. Transverse thermoelectric conversion is driven by various principles stemming from the breaking of structural symmetry or time-reversal symmetry, and substantial performance improvements are anticipated by simultaneously utilizing multiple principles. This study demonstrates hybrid transverse thermoelectric conversion based on multiple phenomena within a junction-less single material. Using an active thermoelectric imaging technique based on lock-in thermography, the charge-to-heat current conversion characteristics in Mg 3 Bi 2 crystals showing anisotropic transport properties were visualized and evaluated. We successfully separated the contributions of the off-diagonal Peltier effect due to the electronic structural symmetry breaking and the ordinary Ettingshausen effect due to the time-reversal symmetry breaking under a magnetic field. These contributions operate additively within the same material, leading to the notable enhancement of the transverse thermoelectric conversion performance.

articles_hidden.title: Asymmetric interactions and feast-famine cycles drive chaos in microbial populations
articles_hidden.authors: William F. McLaughlin, Thomas Beardsley, Natalia L. Komarova, Megan G. Behringer
articles_hidden.abstract: Predicting the dynamics of ecological systems is a central challenge in biology. One factor that may limit predictability is ecological chaos. Theory has long suggested that even simple interactions can produce chaos, yet empirical demonstrations in living systems remain scarce. In a two-strain system of Escherichia coli , increasing the duration between resource replenishment reveals transitions from competitive exclusion to chaos, driven by asymmetric ecological interactions and periodic environmental forcing. Guided by these observations, we developed a dynamical systems framework grounded in empirical data that recapitulate the observed dynamics and predicts intermediate ecological states and transitions. Experimental validation of these predictions by implementing the corresponding conditions successfully reproduces the full range of predicted dynamical regimes. Because feast-famine cycles and asymmetric interactions are widespread in nature, our findings provide a model for uncovering the ecological and evolutionary significance of chaos, opening avenues to use resource fluctuation and interaction strength to quantify, monitor, and manipulate complex ecosystem behavior previously interpreted as stochasticity.

articles_hidden.title: Characterizing ocean flows with the scattering transform
articles_hidden.authors: Jack W. Skinner, Albion Lawrence, Jörn Callies
articles_hidden.abstract: Upper-ocean flows are a complex multiscale jigsaw puzzle of turbulence and waves. Characterizing these flows is essential for understanding their role in redistributing heat, carbon, and nutrients. While power spectral analysis offers a useful statistical descriptor of these flows, it cannot always distinguish between different types of motion. We show that the scattering transform (ST), a wavelet convolution method, can extract geometric information from flow fields, offering insights beyond the power spectrum. The ST distinguishes balanced dynamics, internal waves, and different flavors of geophysical turbulence—even when their power spectra are identical. Applied to sea surface height (SSH) fields from ocean models, the ST differentiates regions with distinct underlying dynamics. Our analysis offers a framework for interpreting SSH from satellite altimetry and for analyzing other spatial maps (e.g., from airborne and coastal radar). More generally, the ST is an appealing way to characterize complex fluid motion in a variety of contexts.

articles_hidden.title: Ubiquitination of USP5 by a bacterial effector inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome activation
articles_hidden.authors: Kelong Ma, Siyao Liu, Fan Jiang, Hongtao Liu, Rundong Shu, Jinli Ge, Zhao-qing Luo, Jiaqi Fu, Jiazhang Qiu
articles_hidden.abstract: The intracellular pathogen Legionella pneumophila employs a repertoire of effector proteins to manipulate the host ubiquitin signaling and subvert host immune responses. In this study, we reported that the L. pneumophila effector GobX (Lpg2455) functions as a ubiquitin ligase to target the host deubiquitinase USP5. Ubiquitination of USP5 by GobX inhibits its deubiquitination activity. Furthermore, this ubiquitination enhances the interaction between USP5 and the host E3 ligase MARCHF7, thereby facilitating MARCHF7-dependent ubiquitination of NLRP3. This modification targets NLRP3 for autophagic degradation, ultimately suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation in macrophages. Our findings uncover a sophisticated strategy in which a bacterial effector hijacks the host ubiquitination machinery to dampen inflammasome signaling.

articles_hidden.title: Multimodal robotic matter enabled by unified magnetic control primitives
articles_hidden.authors: Konstantinos Manos, Yifan Rao, Tuo Zhao, Minjie Chen, Glaucio H. Paulino
articles_hidden.abstract: Robotic matter seeks to achieve collective functionality through interactions among modular units governed by global control signals. A persistent challenge is identifying control frameworks that are simultaneously scalable and deterministic. Here, we introduce a unified magnetic control paradigm that enables multimodal robotic matter using a minimal set of global-field primitives. We show that combinations of rotating and pulsed uniform fields, together with controlled field gradients, are sufficient to generate diverse behaviors—including multimodal locomotion, deterministic bottom-up assembly, and rapid, reversible shape morphing in origami-inspired modular robots. Each module incorporates permanent magnets with prescribed chirality and magnetic moment, encoding mechanical and magnetic asymmetries that map global field inputs to predictable forces, torques, and deformation pathways. Using a programmable three-dimensional Helmholtz coil system, we demonstrate four locomotion modes (rolling, steering, sliding, and walking), hierarchical assembly of three-dimensional robotic architectures, and millisecond-timescale transitions among discrete stable states, with applications to origami state machines and global shape change for navigation through confined spaces. By unifying locomotion, assembly, and reconfiguration within a single control framework, this work establishes a generalizable approach to magnetic robotic matter in which multifunctional collective behaviors emerge from a minimal set of control primitives.

articles_hidden.title: Flexible megahertz low-power complementary circuits based on nanoscale organic transistors
articles_hidden.authors: Ute Zschieschang, Sabrina Steffens, Karla Cordero-Solano, Hagen Klauk
articles_hidden.abstract: The stringent low-power requirements of wearable electronics systems can be met only by combining p-channel and n-channel transistors in a complementary circuit topology. For circuits based on organic thin-film transistors (TFTs), this calls for improvements in n-channel TFT performance. We report on flexible low-voltage nanoscale n-channel organic TFTs fabricated using a recently developed high-performance small-molecule semiconductor. The TFTs have on/off current ratios greater than 10 8 and subthreshold swings below 200 millivolts per decade. Nanoscale n-channel and p-channel organic TFTs were integrated into inverters that display small-signal gains up to 175, noise margins up to 80%, static power consumption as low as 10 −12 watts, and characteristic signal-delay time constants as short as 60 nanoseconds (at 3 volts). These are the best-performing flexible organic TFT–based complementary inverters reported to date.

articles_hidden.title: Predictive model for nanoparticle incorporation into crystals reveals essential role of interfacial solution structure
articles_hidden.authors: Mingyi Zhang, Kuan-Ting Liu, Dong June Jang, Victorien J. B. Bernat, Ying Xia, Dongsheng Li, Hsin-Mei Kao, Zihua Zhu, Jaehun Chun, Ulrich B. Wiesner, Lara A. Estroff, Elias Nakouzi
articles_hidden.abstract: Control of interfacial phenomena remains limited by incomplete understanding of molecular-scale solution structure at solid-liquid interfaces. We address this challenge by developing and validating a comprehensive analytical model for nanoparticle incorporation during crystallization. Using atomic force microscopy (AFM) probes surface functionalized to be “particle proxies” combined with three-dimensional AFM and force spectroscopy, we measure nanoparticle-calcite crystal binding energies and kinetic barriers associated with interfacial hydration layers. These measurements, together with diffusivities, parameterize a predictive model that is corroborated using surface-functionalized fluorescent silica nanoparticles incorporated into calcite. We show that surface chemistry governs incorporation by reshaping the energy landscape, with amine groups particularly favoring incorporation. Applying this approach to nanoparticles with different topologies further supports our finding that kinetic barriers play a pivotal role in incorporation processes. This synthesis science framework links interfacial solution structure, particle dynamics, and crystallization kinetics, identifying kinetic barriers as a key design principle for engineering bioinspired nanocomposites beyond empirical approaches.

articles_hidden.title: Resolving the black hole sphere of influence in a hyperluminous obscured quasar at redshift 4.6
articles_hidden.authors: Mai Liao, Roberto J. Assef, Chao-Wei Tsai, Manuel Aravena, Román Fernández Aranda, Andrew W. Blain, Tanio Díaz-Santos, Peter Eisenhardt, Jorge González-López, Hyunsung D. Jun, Xiaofeng Li, Guodong Li, Lee R. Martin, Ana Posses, Devika Shobhana, Manuel Solimano, Daniel Stern, Andrey Vayner, Jingwen Wu, Dejene Zewdie
articles_hidden.abstract: Supermassive black holes (SMBHs) imprint gravitational signatures on the matter within their sphere of influence (SoI). Nuclear gas dynamics can hence be used to accurately measure the mass of an SMBH, yet these measurements remain elusive in the early universe. We report the first dynamical measurement of an SMBH mass at z  > 2, based on high–spatial resolution observations of the ionized-carbon 157.7-micrometer and carbon monoxide (12-11) 216.93-micrometer emission lines that resolve the SoI in an obscured quasar at z  = 4.6. The radial profile of the velocity dispersion reveals a clear Keplerian rise, requiring the presence of an ∼6 × 10 9 –solar mass SMBH. We propose that heavily obscured quasars allow such tracers to survive in the inner regions and may be ideal targets for increasing dynamical SMBH mass estimates in the early universe.

articles_hidden.title: Deep ultraviolet bound states in the continuum
articles_hidden.authors: Minsu Jeong, Jihae Lee, Sangwon Lee, Jaeyun Lim, Jihwan An, Junsuk Rho
articles_hidden.abstract: Light confinement is a key strategy for enhancing light-matter interaction, and photonic crystal (PhC) slabs have emerged as a promising resonant platform due to their high Q factors and design flexibility. However, realizing high- Q PhC slabs in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) regime has remained highly challenging due to the lack of suitable materials and limitations in fabrication. In this work, we propose an etchless fabrication strategy based on electron-beam lithography and atomic layer deposition. We demonstrate a shell-type PhC slab in which a low-index photoresist core is conformally encapsulated by a high-index zirconium dioxide shell. Through angle-resolved transmittance measurements, we experimentally observe symmetry-protected bound states in the continuum in the DUV regime and achieve the highest reported Q factor among resonant modes in this spectral range. Furthermore, by comparing conventional bulk-type and shell-type PhC slabs in far-field response, we show that the shell-type structure maintains comparable performance while offering fabrication advantages. These results provide a practical route for realizing high- Q PhC slabs in the DUV and open opportunities for DUV-based molecular sensing and enhanced light-matter interaction applications.

articles_hidden.title: THERM-D uncovers distinct neural mechanisms separating morning and evening body temperature rhythms in Drosophila
articles_hidden.authors: Tadahiro Goda, Olivia M. Lopez, Richard Ramolete, Nils Reinhard, Nick Ulle, Ayumi Fukuda, Yujiro Umezaki, Kazim Rizvi, Madison G. Aikawa, Roslyn Catiis, Victoria Z. Marquez, Richard Ngo, Nikita C. Raj, Cora Fisher, Gregory T. Bui, Jalen Lee, Charlotte Helfrich-Förster, Taishi Yoshii, Fumika N. Hamada
articles_hidden.abstract: Animal body temperature rises throughout the day and peaks in the evening, a pattern conserved across diurnal endotherms and ectotherms. However, the mechanisms driving the robust body temperature rhythms (BTRs) remain largely unclear. Here, we developed a machine learning–based platform, Temperature Homeostasis Evaluation of Rhythmicity in Model Drosophila (THERM-D), enabling continuous, high-throughput analyses of BTR. Using THERM-D, we identified robust BTR patterns reflecting flies’ morning and evening behaviors and revealed the function of CRYPTOCHROME (CRY)–negative clock neurons. About half of all clock neurons lack CRY, yet their functions are only partially understood. Gal4 drivers targeting CRY-negative neurons demonstrated that these neurons control the morning temperature rise. We further show that separate clock circuits regulate morning and evening BTRs. Thus, THERM-D elucidated the role of CRY-negative clock neurons in BTR and provides a powerful platform for uncovering mechanisms underlying circadian temperature homeostasis.

articles_hidden.title: Global iodine emissions remain near constant over the 21st century
articles_hidden.authors: Ryan J. Pound, Martin R. Wadley, Rosie Chance, David P. Stevens, Mat J. Evans, Lucy J. Carpenter
articles_hidden.abstract: The reaction between atmospheric ozone and ocean iodide releases gaseous iodine into the atmosphere, destroying ozone and nucleating aerosol particles. The current paradigm is that iodine emissions will substantially increase over this century, with implications for climate, air quality, and human health. Using advanced predictions of ocean iodide concentrations and the iodine emissions function, we re-evaluate this understanding. Rather than increasing through 2100, we find minimal change (−3%) in global iodine emissions compared to present day, predominantly due to a sea surface temperature driven decrease in the iodine emissions function together with relatively unchanged sea surface iodide concentrations. However, emissions increases remain in the critical Arctic region (+143%), resulting in an additional 9 ppbv of springtime surface ozone loss across the region. Our results highlight that predictions of future atmospheric iodine depend on the assumed climate-induced changes in oceanic iodide, in addition to changes in emissions driven by anthropogenic ozone and sea-surface temperature.

articles_hidden.title: A programmable cell-free biosensor device for on-demand detection of pathogens and antibiotics
articles_hidden.authors: Ziqi Gao, Ziyi Lu, Yingke Wu, Licheng Han, Yani Xu, Sheng Zhao, Zhijin Tian, Jie Gu, Shiqi Wang, Chenyi Yu, Qi Han, Xinmin Yu, Fang He, Xinyao Yu, Leihao Lu, Jicheng Yu, Yuqi Zhang, Zhen Gu
articles_hidden.abstract: Cell-free systems provide a versatile platform for engineering customizable, gene circuit-based biosensors for decentralized, low-cost molecular diagnostics. Nevertheless, their performance in complex samples is often compromised by matrix interference, necessitating laborious preprocessing that restricts field deployment. Here, we developed a programmable, on-demand, cell-free kit (POCKit) that integrates sample pretreatment with point-of-care detection. The POCKit device comprises a negative pressure storage chamber and a sampling-sensing chamber, which can be connected to a microneedle array or pipette module for sample collection, filtration and target detection via a freeze-dried cell-free molecular reaction network. The POCKit enables detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection in wound exudates, interstitial fluids and artificial sputum within one hour. It also detects tetracycline in food and environmental water, distinguishing tetracycline-spiked samples from negative controls without specialized equipment or tedious preparation. A portable fluorescence imaging box and smartphone application further support real-time signal acquisition and analysis, offering a ready-to-use platform for on-site diagnostics across biomedicine, food safety, and environmental monitoring.

articles_hidden.title: Cryo-EM reveals a transmembrane allosteric site and activation mechanism for the SERCA calcium pump
articles_hidden.authors: Vinh H. Nguyen, Carlos Cruz-Cortés, Joseph O. Primeau, Raelynn Brassard, M. Joanne Lemieux, L. Michel Espinoza-Fonseca, Howard S. Young
articles_hidden.abstract: Impaired sarco-endoplasmic reticulum Ca 2+ -ATPase (SERCA) activity contributes to defective calcium handling and cellular dysfunction in cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, yet the structural basis of small-molecule SERCA activation has remained unknown. SERCA is a ubiquitous P-type ATPase that restores cytosolic Ca 2+ to the sarco-endoplasmic reticulum and is essential for cardiac Ca 2+ cycling and cellular energy homeostasis. Here, we used cryogenic electron microscopy to define how two chemically distinct activators, CDN1163 and UM-52, enhance SERCA function. Structures at 2.6 Å and 3.1 Å resolution show that both compounds bind the same previously unrecognized activation hotspot in the transmembrane domain, a shallow groove formed by helices M3 and M4 and capped by M1. Despite limited chemical similarity, both activators share conserved interactions with Ser265 and Trp272 and stimulate Ca 2+ -dependent ATPase activity. Activator binding promotes a catalytically competent, calcium-bound E1-like conformation of SERCA that may involve altered protein-lipid interactions. These findings establish a structural framework for rational design of potent next-generation SERCA activators.

articles_hidden.title: Subclonal evolution can shape the transition toward a sarcomatoid phenotype in pleural mesothelioma
articles_hidden.authors: Maya Arnould, Jean-Baptiste Assie, Clément Meiller, Ruth Sequeiros, Sandrine Imbeaud, Amélie Roehrig, Camille Boano, Delphine Le Corre, Sophie Mouillet-Richard, Lucie Poupel, Julien Lavergne, Véronique Hofman, Paul Hofman, Sarah Humez, Arnaud Scherpereel, Françoise Le Pimpec-Barthes, Jessica Zucman-Rossi, Christophe Blanquart, Marie-Claude Jaurand, Sylvie Lantuejoul, Theo Z. Hirsch, Diane Damotte, Didier Jean
articles_hidden.abstract: A better understanding of intratumor heterogeneity in pleural mesothelioma (PM) is crucial to implementing precision medicine for this deadly cancer. Using single-cell RNA sequencing approaches on tumor samples and derived primary cell lines, we defined four phenotypic cell types, related to overall survival in larger bulk cohorts: epithelioid, sarcomatoid, intermediate, and nondifferentiated. Some tumor samples showed intratumor phenotypic heterogeneity, associated with subclonal evolution, in which sarcomatoid cells can emerge from parental cells with an intermediate phenotype following the acquisition of copy number variations. Subclones were conserved in cell lines and retained their specific phenotypes, suggesting high phenotypic heritability. Spatial transcriptomics illustrated the link between phenotypic and subclonal evolution, showing that subclonal cells were colocalized and exhibited specific morphologies within the tumor tissue. Our study provides a comprehensive single-cell profiling of PM tumor cells and reveals a link between phenotypic evolution, clonal architecture, and tumor spatial organization.

articles_hidden.title: Spaceflight reshapes Alzheimer’s disease–associated molecular programs in human brain organoids
articles_hidden.authors: Natalia C. S. Moreira, Luisa B. V. Coelho, Luiz P. Petroski, Stephanie S. Almeida, Luiza P. M. Gaudio, Livia L. Nascimento, Jeong-Hee Lee, Stevens Rehen, Blake Tsu, Juliana de S. da G. Fischer, Paulo C. Carvalho, Aline M. A. Martins, Roberto H. Herai, Alysson R. Muotri
articles_hidden.abstract: Spaceflight provides a unique environment to study neural responses relevant to neurodegenerative diseases. Here, human cortical organoids derived from induced pluripotent stem cells that carry familial Alzheimer’s disease (AD) mutations in APP, PSEN1 , and PSEN2 were cultivated at the International Space Station alongside Controls for 40 days. Multiomic profiling, integrating transcriptomics and proteomics, revealed a coordinated shift in neuronal and cellular states during spaceflight. Spaceflight was associated with changes in amyloid-β processing and tau phosphorylation, although the magnitude of these responses varied across genetic backgrounds. Pathway analysis identified increased synaptic and neurotransmission-related signatures, particularly those associated with GABA-releasing and glutamatergic signaling. Integrative analysis further revealed convergent programs involving RNA processing, chromatin organization, cytoskeletal dynamics, and cellular stress responses. Proteomic and multiomic analyses also identified changes in RNA binding proteins, including CIRBP, consistent with altered posttranscriptional regulatory networks under spaceflight conditions. These exploratory findings indicate that spaceflight reshapes neuronal regulation in human brain organoids, revealing coordinated molecular responses relevant to AD biology.

articles_hidden.title: How far are we from a critical salinity in the North Atlantic Subpolar Gyre?
articles_hidden.authors: Lucas Almeida, Didier Swingedouw
articles_hidden.abstract: The North Atlantic Subpolar Gyre (SPG) can undergo abrupt cooling associated with a loss of deep convection, yet the hydrographic conditions that drive this transition remain uncertain.
