While some CMIP6 models simulate an abrupt SPG cooling, others do not. Here, we identify a critical sea surface salinity (SSS) that separates these contrasting behaviors. Models without abrupt cooling either remain above this threshold because they project weak freshening or already lie below it under present-day conditions, inconsistent with observations. Observed SSS exceeds the critical threshold by 0.3 to 0.8 g kg −1 , depending on the exact threshold definition. Although no declining trend is currently detected, observations remain consistent with models that simulate abrupt cooling. In these models, SSS begins to decline rapidly and crosses the critical threshold about 20 years after the onset of freshening. These results highlight the importance of sustained salinity observations for detecting the approach to this critical threshold, providing a physically based early warning of an abrupt SPG cooling.

articles_hidden.title: Selenium isotopes uncover the mechanism of the deep plate tectonic cycle in the MORB mantle
articles_hidden.authors: Stephan König, María I. Varas-Reus, Romain Tilhac, Carlos J. Garrido
articles_hidden.abstract: Subduction has recycled oceanic crust into Earth’s interior for billions of years, yet how deeply subducted material evolves and contributes to mantle-derived melts, such as mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORBs), remains poorly resolved. Because subducting slab-derived dehydration fluids typically produce isotopically light selenium (Se) in residual eclogites, which is transferred to mantle melts without further fractionation, Se serves as a powerful isotope-based tracer of recycled components into the mantle. Here, we present high-precision Se isotope data for recycled crust–derived garnet pyroxenites that bridge the gap between the primitive mantle and isotopically lighter MORB. Through two-stage thermodynamic modeling, we trace the reactive infiltration of eclogite-derived melts within the convective mantle, leading to the concurrent formation of subduction-derived garnet pyroxenites that preserve residual eclogite cores, both of which contribute to the mantle source of MORBs during adiabatic decompression. Our results establish a petrologically consistent and isotope-validated framework to trace the fate of subducted crust and its long-term imprint on the MORB mantle throughout the deep plate tectonic cycle.

articles_hidden.title: Hardware-encoded modality separation for multimodal sensing and artificial perception
articles_hidden.authors: Wooseok Kim, Bosung Kim, Dae Han Kim, Pei Liu, Doyoung Kim, Hee Kyu Lee, Sang Uk Park, Janghoon Joo, Byeong Woon Lee, Se Gi Lee, Bogeun Kim, Jaejun Lim, Changsoon Choi, Jong-Woong Kim, Geumbee Lee, Jae-Young Yoo, Sejin Kim, Joohoon Kang, Raudel Avila, Jong Uk Kim, Sang Min Won
articles_hidden.abstract: Human skin achieves robust perception by distributing modality-specialized receptors that preferentially encode mechanical and thermal cues. Yet, soft and flexible tactile sensors often suffer from cross-sensitivity, where stretching, bending, and temperature variations generate overlapping electrical readouts that undermine reliable multimodal measurement and downstream artificial intelligence–based interpretation. Here, we present a multimodal piezoresistive platform based on doped silicon nanomembranes that leverages their crystallographic anisotropy and a bilayer differential architecture for front-end modality separation. By integrating [110] longitudinal/transverse gauges with [100] reference gauges that exhibit reduced piezoresistive sensitivity but comparable temperature coefficient of resistance, together with a bilayer differential layout, the platform compensates thermal drift and decouples stretching from bending at the hardware level. Experimental and theoretical analyses establish a quantitative framework for separating modality-specific responses under combined stretching, bending, and temperature stimuli. Integrated into a flexible, wireless platform, the decoupled signals enable real-time transmission and deep learning–based interpretation, allowing accurate identification of geometrically similar objects with distinct thermal or mechanical properties. These results highlight the feasibility and need to co-design front-end sensing architectures and learning models to achieve robust, high-accuracy multimodal decoupling in real-world conditions.

articles_hidden.title: Light-guided photophosphorylation nanorobot rescues injured cardiomyocytes via in situ bioenergetic restoration
articles_hidden.authors: Tingting Yue, Meng Mao, Xiankun Lin, Yang Huang, Qiang He
articles_hidden.abstract: Myocardial injury is a leading cause of death worldwide and is accompanied by profound mitochondrial bioenergetic dysfunction in impaired cardiomyocytes. Restoring cellular bioenergetic homeostasis could be a promising strategy to promote cardiac repair; however, current clinical adenosine triphosphate (ATP) injection therapies yield limited efficacy due to the inability to achieve in situ, targeted delivery. Here, we develop a photoactivated phosphorylation nanorobot engineered to rescue impaired metabolism via targeted, in situ ATP synthesis within cardiomyocytes. These Janus photophosphorylation nanorobots are fabricated through mechanical extrusion–assisted phase separation, enabling the asymmetric integration of chromatophore-coupled F o F l -ATPases. Under structured near-infrared irradiation, the nanorobots exhibit synergistic F o F l -ATPase rotation, which simultaneously drives active propulsion and high-yield ATP catalysis. Following targeted internalization and efficient lysosomal escape, the nanorobots achieve deep penetration into injured myocardial tissue. Intracellularly, the localized elevation of ATP rebalances the NAD + /NADH ratio, suppresses pathological mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) opening, and mitigates calcium ion overload—collectively restoring mitochondrial integrity and promoting functional myocardial recovery. This self-propelled, bioenergy-restoring nanoplatform represents a rationally designed strategy for targeted therapy of energy-deficient cardiomyopathies.

articles_hidden.title: Stress unmasks disconnected endocrine coordination of glucose metabolism in Duchenne muscular dystrophy
articles_hidden.authors: Gretel S. Major, Cara A. Timpani, Hannah Lalunio, Jiayi Chen, Lauren Boatner, Nicholas Giourmas, Stephanie Kourakis, Eva van den Berg, Ekaterina Salimova, Joel Eliades, Gang Zheng, Rong Xu, Sukhvir Kaur Bhangu, Thirimadura V. H. Mendis, Joel R. Steele, Ralf B. Schittenhelm, Deirdre L. Merry, Louise Lantier, Christoph E. Hagemeyer, Francesca Cavalieri, Karen Caeyenberghs, Aaron P. Russell, Michael de Veer, Craig A. Goodman, Alan Hayes, Emma Rybalka, Charles P. Najt, Angus Lindsay
articles_hidden.abstract: Skeletal muscle orchestrates systemic metabolism, dynamically coordinating glucose uptake and fuel use to match energy demand. In Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), loss of dystrophin is associated with altered metabolic regulation. Using physiological stress to unmask metabolic deficits in the mdx mouse model of DMD, we show that stress hormone signaling rises without an appropriate poststress rise in insulin secretion, maintaining hyperglycemia despite elevated basal glucose uptake in skeletal muscle. Rather than reflecting increased gluconeogenesis, this hyperglycemia appears to stem from impaired glucose oxidative disposal; skeletal muscle stores glucose as glycogen instead of oxidizing it, while the heart and brain show persistent, tissue-specific uptake differences. Restoring insulin availability transiently corrects glucose control and reverses stress-induced deficits. Instead of correcting glucose handling, removing excess glucose directly using empagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor) prevents stress-induced increases in blood glucose. These findings identify a breakdown in endocrine-metabolic coordination underlying metabolic vulnerability in DMD and demonstrate two mechanistically distinct routes, restoring insulin secretion or bypassing it entirely, to restore metabolic resilience under stress.

articles_hidden.title: A precipitation threshold delineates contrasting controls on global soil pH under nitrogen fertilization
articles_hidden.authors: Wenqi Jiao, Tao Hu, Chongchong Qi, Liyuan Chai
articles_hidden.abstract: Nitrogen fertilization is a major driver of soil acidification globally, yet its independent effects on soil pH and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly resolved. Here we isolate the contribution of nitrogen fertilization by compiling the largest paired experimental dataset to date, consisting of 3564 paired soil pH observations under control and nitrogen fertilization treatments across seven major ecosystem types worldwide. By constructing robust machine-learning models, we predict global soil pH under nitrogen fertilization (pH_T) and quantify fertilization-associated pH change under a standardized hypothetical fertilization scenario. Under this scenario, we estimate that 96.27% of global soils undergo acidification, with a mean pH decline of 0.34 units. Critically, we identify a precipitation threshold at ∼900 mm year −1 that separates two distinct regimes in the relationship between precipitation and pH_T: climate-driven leaching and buffering in drier regions versus soil-mediated internal regulation in humid regions. This threshold demonstrates that the association between precipitation and pH_T is not uniform across the global precipitation gradient but varies markedly among hydroclimatic regions. Our results provide a global outlook on soil pH responses to nitrogen fertilization, supporting acidification risk early warning, precision fertilizer management, and sustainable agricultural development.

articles_hidden.title: Visual learning through auditory reactivation during wakefulness and sleep
articles_hidden.authors: Musi Xie, Zhuoqun Li, Yuxin Fan, Yifan Li, Xingbei Wan, Sirui Yang, Shiman Huang, Chengsi Zhao, Ning Ma, Fang Fang, Xilin Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: Visual learning, like other kinds of learning, has classically been attributed to intensive, active training; however, whether it can be achieved via effortless, passive reactivation remains unresolved. Here, we triggered targeted reactivation using auditory tones that had acquired contextual meaning through preceding visual–auditory associative learning. Re-exposure to learned tones improved subsequent visual performance during both wakefulness and slow-wave sleep. Wake reactivation matched training in both improvement and improvement per trial, whereas sleep reactivation surpassed both wake reactivation and training. By contrast, re-exposure to unlearned tones impaired performance only during slow-wave sleep. Reactivation-induced improvement and impairment were strictly orientation- and location-specific and were associated with a convergent auditory–visual coupling pathway. Beyond this shared pathway, auditory reactivation during wakefulness and sleep unfolded through distinct coupling architectures linking sensory and higher-order cortical regions. Collectively, our findings establish auditory reactivation as a highly efficient route to visual learning, identify sleep as its most potent state, and reveal a double-edged, state-dependent neuroplastic architecture.

articles_hidden.title: Historical evidence that wildfire frequency modulates debris-flow hazards through sediment-supply limitation
articles_hidden.authors: Emily C. Geyman, Michael P. Lamb
articles_hidden.abstract: Southern California is an epicenter of postwildfire debris flows. In this region, steep topography, frequent fire, heavy rainstorms, and large populations along the wildland-urban interface conspire to produce costly debris flows. Wildfire frequency in the region has tripled in recent decades, causing concern about escalating debris-flow hazards. Here, we investigate how wildfire frequency affects the magnitude of postfire erosion by analyzing long-term debris basin records. We identify two contrasting erosional styles. In steep catchments, erosion exhibits a binge-purge behavior: Erosion for 3 years following fire exceeds background rates by ∼17×. In contrast, in low-sloping, soil-mantled catchments, sediment export following fire only exceeds background rates by ∼1.5×. Critically, in the steep catchments, debris-flow volumes decline when wildfires recur more frequently than the ∼30-year interval characteristic of the past century. This observation suggests a sediment-supply limitation in which more frequent wildfire may reduce, rather than amplify, some of Southern California’s most severe debris-flow hazards.

articles_hidden.title: Bioinspired mucolytic microrods for active mucus penetration and enhanced antibiotic delivery against H. pylori
articles_hidden.authors: Wenhuang Ban, Min Sun, Jingjing Qu, Yuening Zhong, Weixi Wu, Yijun Lin, Yu Liu, Runqin Tan, Xiumei Ni, Song Zhou, Shan Guan, Dan Shao, Yan He, Kaiyun Liu, Chengzhong Yu, Jie Tang
articles_hidden.abstract: Helicobacter pylori infects half of the global population and is a major driver of gastric cancer. Clinical eradication remains challenging because antibiotics must survive the acidic gastric lumen, penetrate the viscoelastic mucus barrier, and reach bacteria residing near the gastric epithelium. Here, we report a biomimetic oral delivery system that integrates rod-shaped morphology, acid protection, active mucolysis, and localized antibiotic delivery. The platform consists of clarithromycin-loaded Santa Barbara Amorphous-15 silica microrods coated with a pH-responsive alginate-pronase conjugate. The coating protects clarithromycin and pronase under acidic gastric conditions, while the less acidic inner mucus microenvironment promotes coating detachment and pronase-mediated mucolysis, enabling active mucus penetration. In vitro and in vivo studies show that these bacteria-mimicking microrods significantly enhance mucus penetration and increase gastric residence time twofold. In a murine infection model, the platform achieved 100% eradication at 15 milligrams per kilogram and maintained 90% clearance at 7.5 milligrams per kilogram, producing a ∼2000-fold bacterial burden reduction compared to free clarithromycin. This bioinspired, shape-guided strategy offers a promising paradigm for localized gastrointestinal therapy.

articles_hidden.title: Complex IV maturation coordinates postnatal mitochondrial and metabolic development
articles_hidden.authors: Milica Popovic, Alfredo Cabrera-Orefice, Lea Isermann, Marijana Croon, Aleksandra Zecic, Jana Meisterknecht, Yasmin Alameldin, Vidyarashmi Hanehalli, Triinu Siibak, Christian Frezza, Ilka Wittig, Aleksandra Trifunovic
articles_hidden.abstract: The perinatal heart undergoes a rapid metabolic transition from glycolysis to fatty acid oxidation that requires extensive mitochondrial remodeling, yet the molecular checkpoints that coordinate this process remain poorly defined. Using temporally resolved proteomics and complexome profiling of developing mouse hearts from late gestation through early postnatal life (E18.5 to P10), we identify a discrete developmental window in which respiratory chain architecture is remodeled to enable metabolic commitment. Complex IV (CIV) emerges as a central structural determinant of this transition, undergoing isoform-specific reassembly and transient suppression at birth before incorporation into mature respiratory supercomplexes. We identify the CIV subunit COX7C as a developmentally regulated determinant of CIV maturation, with its abundance increasing during maximal respirasome assembly and the switch to fatty acid oxidation. Loss of COX7C impairs terminal CIV maturation, prevents incorporation of heart-specific isoforms, and destabilizes the respirasome organization. Notably, this defect causes a selective secondary failure of complex I completion, demonstrating that respirasome formation is required for catalytic CI maturation in vivo. Consequently, cardiac-specific COX7C deficiency fails to complete the perinatal metabolic transition, leading to the collapse of fatty acid oxidation, activation of nucleotide and serine–glycine–one-carbon metabolism, attenuated activation of the mitochondrial integrated stress response, and a metabolically and structurally compromised state unlikely to support the increasing energetic demands of the postnatal heart. Together, these findings define a developmentally timed, CIV-dependent assembly step that couples respiratory chain assembly to postnatal cardiac metabolic fate and provide a temporal framework for mitochondrial maturation in the developing heart.

articles_hidden.title: Neuromorphic self-aware wings for embodied-intelligent bionic flying microrobotics
articles_hidden.authors: Hao Zheng, Xu Zeng, Yao Tan, Changliu He, Cheng Tu, Haitao Deng, Yu Song, Yan Wang, Beomjoon Kim, Yuan Lin, Xiaosheng Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: Flying insects achieve robust proprioception and agile flight control using distributed mechanoreceptors on their wings, but current bionic flying microrobots rely heavily on external sensors for state monitoring. Typical sensing solutions including offboard vision or surface-mounted devices inevitably sacrifice either flight autonomy or payload capacity. Inspired by insect wing mechanoreception, we introduce an embodied neuromorphic self-sensing paradigm that eliminates this tradeoff by enabling intrinsic, aerodynamics-maintenance proprioception in flapping-wing systems. Instead of treating the wing solely as a propulsive structure, we reengineer it into a self-contained sensory organ capable of autonomous motion monitoring and health state awareness. We develop an interface charge field mapping model that decouples complex local wing motions, enabling dynamic three-dimensional reconstruction of wing deformation. Building on this theoretical foundation, a conformal bionic mechanoreceptor is directly grown on the wing surface via layered sensitive units. By synergistically combining physics-driven kinematic feature extraction with machine learning, the system achieves real-time fault diagnosis and closed-loop aerodynamic-loss compensation. We do not add sensors to the wing, we make the wing itself the sensory organ. This embodied self-sensing paradigm establishes a new principle for structural intelligence in bionic robotics, offering a promising path toward autonomous, self-aware, and robust miniature flying systems.

articles_hidden.title: Dual-modality photoacoustic and optical coherence tomography imaging simultaneously tracks transplanted stem cells and their viability
articles_hidden.authors: Sumin Park, Wei Qian, Jeff Folz, Van Phuc Nguyen, N. Dayanthi Perera, Wei Zhang, Abigail T. Fahim, Yannis M. Paulus, Xueding Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Monitoring transplanted cell viability in vivo, noninvasively remains a considerable challenge. By using multiwavelength photoacoustic microscopy powered by a reactive oxygen species (ROS)–responsive contrast agent, we can relatively and semiquantitatively assess and longitudinally monitor the viability of human-induced pluripotent stem cell–derived retinal pigment epithelium (hiPSC-RPE) cells in vivo. The contrast agent comprises colloidal chain-like gold nanoparticle (CGNP) clusters conjugated with IR775c, a heptamethine cyanine dye that undergoes selective oxidative quenching under elevated ROS conditions associated with cellular death (CGNP-IR775c). Dual-wavelength photoacoustic microscopy at 620 and 775 nanometers provides self-calibrated ratiometric measurements that enable relative viability assessment, distinguishing healthy from nonviable cell populations. In vitro studies demonstrated that CGNP-IR775c exhibited biocompatibility and showed dose-dependent ROS sensitivity across physiologically relevant H 2 O 2 concentrations. hiPSC-RPE cells labeled by CGNP-IR775c were subretinally transplanted into living rabbit eyes and longitudinally monitored for 2 weeks, showing that laser-induced oxidative stress produced measurable photoacoustic signal changes that were consistent with the viability status of the transplanted cells. The imaging technology developed here provides a practical solution for noninvasive, longitudinal, and semiquantitative assessment of the transplanted cell viability in vivo, and may contribute to ophthalmology cell-based therapy in both preclinical and clinical settings.

articles_hidden.title: Dynamic nuclear pores dictate the emergence of lamina-associated domains and UV protection during embryogenesis
articles_hidden.authors: Fei Xu, Adrián Fragoso-Luna, Itai Sharon, Angelo L. Angonezi, Dania Camila Pulido Barrera, Kamaludeen Mariyath Nibrasul Haque, Cristina Tocchini, Can Eser, Hiroshi Kimura, Ohad Medalia, Peter Askjaer, Susan E. Mango
articles_hidden.abstract: Lamina-associated domains (LADs) are large heterochromatin domains tethered to the nuclear periphery. LADs organize genome architecture, replication, repair, and transcription, but their formation during development is not well understood. Here, we use DamID and single-cell imaging to analyze embryonic LAD biogenesis in Caenorhabditis elegans . In early embryos, abundant nuclear pore components prevent heterochromatin formation at the lamina, and DNA positioned there is transcriptionally active. Over time, pore components decline, enabling LADs to form; auxin-mediated pore depletion induces precocious LADs. Nuclear basket component npp-21 /Translocated Promoter Region is not required, distinguishing embryonic LAD biogenesis from LADs in differentiated cells. Functionally, LADs confer protection against UVB radiation: Older embryos concentrate DNA damage at the nuclear periphery and survive UVB, whereas early embryos accumulate damage throughout nuclei and die, unless shielded by their mothers in utero. Within the embryo, damage is concentrated in upper, ultraviolet-facing cells, while underlying cells are shielded, suggesting that the Bodyguard effect operates at the organismal level. These findings identify embryonic dissipation of nuclear pores as a key step in embryonic LAD biogenesis, enabling older embryos to withstand environmental challenges.

articles_hidden.title: The importance of organics in hydrothermal environments: A synchrotron laboratory study
articles_hidden.authors: Laura E. Jenkins, Stephen P. Thompson, Eamonn T. Connolly, Celine Beck, Sarah J. Day, Lucy K. Saunders
articles_hidden.abstract: The icy moon Enceladus has hydrothermal plumes that are of astrobiologic interest as they could provide conditions to sustain life or allow for its origin. To understand the geology of hydrothermal environments on icy moons, a carbonaceous asteroid simulant similar to the material Enceladus may have accreted from was subjected to conditions analogous to that of its seafloor. The sample environment used allowed high-resolution in situ synchrotron x-ray diffraction data to be collected during the experiment. Mineral reactions were observed as they occurred. Multiple mineral reactions had a large dependence on organic matter. Organics catalyzed the breakdown of aluminosilicates and dissolved pyrite. Melanophlogite and pyrrhotite were also formed as a result of organics being present. This study reveals that organics can have a large impact on mineral reactions and likely play an important role in the geology of hydrothermal vents on icy moons, which have an abundance of organics.

articles_hidden.title: Immune infiltrate predicts response to αPD1/αCTLA4 but not αPD1 and distinguishes programs of primary resistance in metastatic melanoma
articles_hidden.authors: Amy Y. Huang, Kelly P. Burke, Marc C. Glettig, Ryan Porter, Peter Fatouros, Jonathan M. Li, Lynn Meiger, Valeria Rosado, Shuyun Xu, Jiekun Yang, Emily Robitschek, Natalie Vokes, Cora Ricker, Giuseppe Tarantino, Jiajia Chen, Tyler J. Aprati, Yiwen He, Cassia Wang, Doris Fu, Li-Lun Ho, Kyriakitsa Galani, Gordon J. Freeman, Elizabeth I. Buchbinder, F. Stephen Hodi, Christine G. Lian, Manolis Kellis, Genevieve M. Boland, Arlene H. Sharpe, David Liu
articles_hidden.abstract: While immune-checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized treatment of metastatic melanoma, the identification of robust biomarkers to predict the relative efficacy of single versus combination ICB has been challenging. We performed a meta-analysis of eight cohorts of patients treated with anti–PD-1 ( n  = 290), anti–CTLA-4 ( n  = 175), and combination anti–PD-1/anti–CTLA-4 ( n  = 51) with pretreatment tumor sequencing and clinical annotations. Surprisingly, the increased response rate to combination anti–PD-1/anti–CTLA-4 compared to anti–PD-1 monotherapy was observed only in highly immune infiltrated tumors, and not in immune-low tumors. Stratifying tumors by high or low frequency of immune cells also distinguished context-dependent programs of primary resistance to single and combination ICB. Notably, hypoxia-related pathways were enriched in nonresponders to anti–PD-1 ICB in immune-high, but not immune-low, tumors. Using an independent cohort of patients with scRNA-seq data, we observed that correlates of hypoxia were associated with increased stromal tumor receptor-ligand interactions. As proof of concept, selective inhibition of HIF-2α, a component of the hypoxia pathway and highly expressed in endothelial cells and fibroblasts, in combination with anti–PD-1, controlled tumor growth in mouse models of highly immune-infiltrated tumors but not poorly immune-infiltrated tumors. Our work demonstrates how stratification by tumor immune characteristics and clinical features can lead to the rational discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

articles_hidden.title: Arctic forcing of European spring productivity and agricultural yields linked to Barents Sea ice loss
articles_hidden.authors: Zhi Huang, Jun Wang, Philippe Ciais, Xichen Li, William K. M. Lau, Ning Zeng, Wenping Yuan, Haijin Dai, Hao Zhou, Jinfeng Ding, Meirong Wang, Ran Yan, Duwei Zhong, Anmin Duan, Yimin Liu, Jing M. Chen, Fei Jiang, Weimin Ju
articles_hidden.abstract: Arctic sea ice loss reshapes midlatitude climate, yet its cascading impacts on terrestrial carbon cycling and food security remain unclear. Barents Sea ice area (BSIA) has experienced the Arctic’s fastest decline. Using four decades of satellite observations, agricultural statistics, and Earth system model (ESM) simulations, we identify late-winter BSIA as a key driver of European spring productivity. Interannual BSIA reductions substantially enhance gross primary productivity (GPP) and raise national wheat yields by up to 16.5% in Eastern Europe, a global breadbasket. Reanalysis and model experiments reveal that reduced BSIA alters large-scale circulation through stratosphere-troposphere coupling, wave–mean flow interactions, and Rossby wave propagation. Anomalous subsidence drives adiabatic and radiative warming; cyclonic flow strengthens warm-air advection, together alleviating thermal constraints on photosynthesis. Although most ESMs capture atmospheric teleconnections, they systematically underestimate productivity responses due to underrepresented GPP-temperature sensitivity. BSIA decline accounts for approximately half of the four-decade increase in Eastern European productivity, highlighting an overlooked Arctic forcing of midlatitude carbon dynamics.

articles_hidden.title: Continuously aligned biomimetic sites in MXene membranes for rapid lithium extraction
articles_hidden.authors: Zihan Liu, Longfeng Hu, Sijin Li, Shirong Li, Tianhuai Kang, Hongzhi Liu, Gaoxin Dai, Langming Bai, Heng Liang
articles_hidden.abstract: Efficient separation of lithium ions (Li + ) from magnesium ions (Mg 2+ ) remains a central challenge for direct lithium extraction from salt lake brines due to their similar physicochemical properties. Inspired by biological ion channels, biomimetic membranes have been explored to improve Li + /Mg 2+ separation. However, most biomimetic membranes focus primarily on introducing recognition sites while overlooking the structural features of biological channels, particularly the continuous arrangement of coordination sites that facilitates efficient ion transport. Here, inspired by the continuous carbonyl coordination structure of the KcsA ion channel, 4-formylbenzo-15-crown-5 ether was periodically grafted onto poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) chains and integrated with MXene nanosheets to construct two-dimensional interlayer channels with continuously aligned crown ether recognition sites. This architecture shifts Li + transport from random diffusion to successive site-to-site hopping, reducing the effective transport energy barrier. The resulting biomimetic MXene membrane achieves a Li + flux of 0.12 mol·m −2 ·h −1 with Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of 109 and performs effectively across various salt lake brines.

articles_hidden.title: Unseen but not unheard: Animal-borne audio recorders reveal missing interactions between seabirds and untracked vessels
articles_hidden.authors: Jonathan D. Rutter, Sarah Bond, Ana P.B. Carneiro, Aline da Silva Cerqueira, Igor Debski, Johannes H. Fischer, Robin Freeman, Dave Goad, Louise Maurice, Jason Moss, Oliver Padget, Olivia Rowley, Kate Simister, Graeme Taylor, Stephen C. Votier, Katrina J. Davis, Tim Guilford
articles_hidden.abstract: Quantifying interactions between marine megafauna and vessels is key to assessing the ecological impacts of commercial fishing and shipping. Automatic identification systems (AIS), by publicly tracking global vessel activities, have enabled animal-vessel interactions to be identified at scale. However, the extent of these interactions is inevitably underestimated due to “unseen” vessels that lack AIS or have gaps in coverage from technical issues or intentional disabling. Using animal-borne audio recorders on three seabird species (northern gannet, Balearic shearwater, and Westland petrel), we investigated whether acoustic detection of vessel sounds could reveal a more complete picture of interactions. We found that a striking proportion of vessel audio detections (gannets, >32%, estimated 57%; shearwaters, >12%, estimated 20%) could not be matched with AIS-tracked vessels, suggesting substantial potential for bycatch risk from unseen fishing. Our approach is computationally lightweight, applicable to pre-existing datasets, and transferrable to non-seabird taxa. Acoustic detection could improve future assessments of animal-vessel interactions and unseen vessel activities to support marine conservation.

articles_hidden.title: Ultra-generalized hologram synthesis via domain-adaptive wavefront learning
articles_hidden.authors: Runze Zhu, Jiasheng Xiao, Hao Zhang, Hong-Bo Sun
articles_hidden.abstract: Deep learning–based computer-generated holography is essential for creating lifelike three-dimensional (3D) visuals in extended reality and immersive human-digital interaction. However, current data-driven approaches predominantly rely on a 3D-solution search strategy that couples scene representation with physical parameters. This paradigm leads to physical overfitting, restricting models to fixed wavelengths and depths and preventing generalization across diverse 3D data formats. Here, we report a 2D-solution search technique, wavefront-aware neural encoding (WNE). This method is a universal framework that overcomes these limitations via domain-adaptive wavefront learning. By compensating for feature distribution shifts induced by varying data formats and physical parameters, WNE maps various wavefronts into a unified feature domain compatible with a frozen, pretrained encoder. This mechanism enables ultra-generalized hologram synthesis: A single pretrained network can encode high-fidelity phase-only holograms for diverse 3D representations, from conventional layer-based data to emerging Gaussian splatting. Outperforming previous analytical and neural encoding methods in image quality, WNE establishes a robust, plug-and-play engine for diverse holographic applications.

articles_hidden.title: TREX1 and TREX2 3′ → 5′ DNA exonucleases enhance the fidelity of translesion synthesis by DNA polymerase θ
articles_hidden.authors: Jung-Hoon Yoon, Karthi Sellamuthu, Louise Prakash, Satya Prakash
articles_hidden.abstract: A multiplicity of translesion synthesis (TLS) DNA polymerases (Pols) promote replication through DNA lesions in an error-free or error-prone manner. Among these Pols, Polθ operates in an error-prone manner. However, Polθ conducts TLS in human cells in a much more error-free manner than implicated from the high error-proneness of the purified Pol. To resolve this incongruity, here we show that the TREX1/TREX2 3′ → 5′ exonucleases are integral components of TLS mediated by Polθ. In TREX1- or TREX2-deficient cells, Polθ-dependent TLS becomes nonoperational and chromosomal instability rises similar to that in Polθ-deficient cells. Consequently, similar to that in Polθ −/− mice, trex2 −/− mice exhibit increased susceptibility to ultraviolet-induced skin cancers. Furthermore, our findings that in the absence of TREX1/TREX2 3′ → 5′ exonuclease activities, Polθ-mediated TLS manifests high mutagenicity, and an increase in the diversity of misincorporated nucleotides demarcate a crucial role of these exonucleases in the removal of Polθ misinsertions and, thereby, in enhancing Polθ TLS fidelity and the consequent genome stability.

articles_hidden.title: Structural basis of Anopheles mosquito salivary protein complexes implicated in malaria transmission
articles_hidden.authors: Tiantian Su, Shiheng Liu, Adeline E. Williams, Eric Calvo, Z. Hong Zhou
articles_hidden.abstract: Successful malaria transmission by Anopheles mosquitoes depends on Plasmodium development within the mosquito midgut and subsequent sporozoite invasion of its salivary glands. Salivary proteins, notably Saglin and likely salivary gland surface proteins (SGS4 and SGS5), were suggested to play roles in these processes, but the lack of their structures has hindered our understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms. In this study, we carried out biochemical and mass spectrometry analyses of salivary gland extracts and demonstrate that Anopheles gambiae SGS4 and SGS5 bind Saglin and other SG1 (salivary gland 1) proteins. Cryo-EM structure of the Saglin-SGS4 complex reveals that Saglin homodimerizes through coiled-coil interactions and disulfide bonds and engages longitudinally with SGS4. Comparisons among SG1-SGS complexes show that SG1 proteins share a conserved architecture, and SGS proteins adapt conformationally to bind different SG1 partners of varying lengths. To our knowledge, our findings uncover the first native mosquito salivary protein complexes that likely facilitate malaria transmission and highlight potential vector targets for blocking malaria transmission.

articles_hidden.title: Dissecting the molecular triggers of early and late long-term potentiation
articles_hidden.authors: Rui Wang, Michaela Schweizer, Kristina Ponimaskine, Christian Schulze, Christine E. Gee, Thomas G. Oertner
articles_hidden.abstract: The brain stores information by changing the strength of its synapses, a process that has at least two phases: Late long-term potentiation (L-LTP) is thought to result from the consolidation of early LTP (E-LTP), just as long-term memory requires the prior establishment of short-term memory. Recently, inhibitory avoidance experiments under CaMKII inhibition have challenged this notion, demonstrating long-term fear memory without measurable short-term memory. Here we use optogenetic activation and inhibition of CaMKII during induction of spike-timing-dependent potentiation (tLTP) to dissect the signaling pathways. While CaMKII activation in CA1 neurons was sufficient to induce E-LTP, growth of the postsynaptic density and spine neck expansion, we found that CaMKII-induced LTP does not give rise to L-LTP. Conversely, inhibition of CaMKII during tLTP induction prevented E-LTP, but FOS and L-LTP were still expressed, driven by CaMKK and PKMζ. Thus, both long-term memory and L-LTP form in the absence of CaMKII activation.

articles_hidden.title: Disulfiram inhibits pyroptosis and apoptosis through multiple complementary mechanisms
articles_hidden.authors: Han Yu, Elliott M. Bernard, Stefania A. Mari, Tetiana Serdiuk, Kristyna Pluhackova, Michele M. Nava, Upnishad Sharma, Matilde Lucioli, Wenhui Cheng, Jack Kuipers, Martin Fussenegger, Paola Picotti, Sebastian Hiller, Petr Broz, Daniel J. Müller
articles_hidden.abstract: Gasdermins (GSDMs) execute pyroptosis by forming lytic pores in the plasma membrane that release IL-1 cytokines and promote cell swelling and membrane rupture. Their key roles in infection, inflammation and cancer make GSDMs attractive therapeutic targets. Here we systematically investigate how disulfiram, an approved drug for treating alcoholism, inhibits pyroptosis and identify multiple complementary mechanisms. First, disulfiram inhibits processing of procaspase-1 to caspase-1. Second, disulfiram inhibits caspases from processing human GSDMD to release the lytic N-terminal domain (GSDMD Nterm ). Third, disulfiram structurally modifies GSDMD Nterm . Fourth, disulfiram partitions into membranes, where it remains embedded, changes membrane properties and prevents GSDMD Nterm insertion. Similarly, disulfiram blocks intrinsic apoptosis by inhibiting procaspase-3 activation, caspase-3 cleavage of human GSDME, and GSDME Nterm pore formation. Furthermore, we show that two other GSDMD inhibitors, necrosulfonamide and dimethyl fumarate also inhibit GSDM-induced cell death through multiple complementary mechanisms. These multilevel inhibitory mechanisms deepen our understanding of strategies to target GSDM-mediated cell death pathways.

articles_hidden.title: A membrane-guided strategy for optimizing proton exchange membrane fuel cells via spatially controlled acid distribution
articles_hidden.authors: Jingjing Lin, Yilin Chen, Jisong Hu, Muzi Xu, Dong Liu, Jinwu Peng, Lei Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Efficient regulation of phosphoric acid (PA) distribution is vital for advancing high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells. PA migration from the membrane into the catalyst layer (CL) enhances proton accessibility but compromises membrane conductivity, highlighting the need to balance acid distribution within the membrane electrode assembly. Here, we propose a membrane-guided strategy enabling systematic evaluation of PA distribution effects and identification of a favorable acid content range. By designing side chain–grafted polybenzimidazole (PBI) membranes with abundant acid-binding sites, we achieve tunable acid doping levels and regulate PA partitioning through acid-polymer interactions. To compare PA accumulation, we introduce the mass ratio of phosphorus to platinum in the CL (PA CL /Pt CL ) as a semiquantitative descriptor of CL acid content and use distribution of relaxation times analysis to decouple its influence on ohmic resistance, oxygen reduction kinetics, and oxygen transport. We identify a favorable PA CL /Pt CL range of approximately two to three under the present conditions, while the nearly twofold enhancement over OPBI highlights coordinated control of membrane transport and the CL acid state.

articles_hidden.title: Uterine-derived anisotropic compressive force specifies the anterior-posterior axis orientation in the mouse embryo
articles_hidden.authors: Seiya Mikoshiba, Hiroshi Koyama, Sanae Oka, Takaya Abe, Hiroshi Kiyonari, Masahiko Hibi, Toshihiko Fujimori
articles_hidden.abstract: The establishment of the anterior-posterior (A-P) axis is a fundamental process in embryonic patterning. In mice, directional migration of the anterior visceral endoderm (AVE) determines the A-P axis, yet the cues directing migration remain elusive. Here, we show that anisotropic compression directs AVE migration toward the minor-axis end of the deformed embryo, using ex utero culture with controlled compression and in utero pharmacological manipulations of uterine mechanics. This compression induces localized accumulation of basement membrane (BM) components, including COLLAGEN IV, which directs the AVE toward the minor-axis end. Mathematical modeling demonstrates that BM density-dependent AVE-BM adhesion accounts for the observed AVE dynamics. Our findings reveal that the maternal mechanical environment provides directional cues for cell migration, bridging tissue-scale mechanics and biochemical patterning during body axis specification.

articles_hidden.title: Oligodendrocyte ER-phagy restricts excessive myelination by degrading sphingolipid synthases
articles_hidden.authors: Tingxin Zhang, Daniela Barbosa, Aksheev Bhambri, Lu O. Sun
articles_hidden.abstract: Myelination is critical for nervous system function. Numerous signaling pathways have been identified that promote myelin sheath growth, disruption of which can lead to hypomyelination. However, the negative regulators of myelin sheath expansion remain poorly defined. Here, we identify endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–phagy as a cellular brake on central nervous system myelination that restricts myelin sheath thickness during brain development. ER-phagy is active in oligodendrocytes during myelin membrane expansion and limits the abundance of ER-resident sphingolipid synthases, including ceramide synthase 2 (Cers2). Impairment of ER-phagy accumulates ER, elevates sphingolipid production, drives excessive myelin thickening, and alters social behavior after prolonged juvenile social isolation. Genetic deletion of Cers2, which synthesizes long-chain ceramides essential for sphingolipid biogenesis, rescues the hypermyelination phenotype caused by ER-phagy disruption. Together, our findings establish that ER-phagy–sphingolipid axis represses myelin growth and reveal a mechanistic link between ER homeostasis and myelin production by oligodendrocytes, providing insight into the cellular mechanisms underlying pathological hypermyelination.

articles_hidden.title: Ribosome-associated vesicles promote activity-dependent local translation in neurons
articles_hidden.authors: Eva Martin-Solana, Stephen D. Carter, Karthik Krishnamurthy, Giovanni de Nola, Jiying Ning, Jill R. Glausier, Matias A. Preisegger, Laura Harris, Lauren Meyer, Leanna Eisenman, Paul N. Joseph, Cedric Bouchet-Marquis, Ken Wu, Catherina L. Mobini, Amber N. Frantz, Stephanie Puig, Cheri M. Hampton, Nadine Kabbani, David Mankus, Eric K. F. Donahue, Kristopher Burkewitz, Grant J. Jensen, Simon C. Watkins, Karl Deisseroth, Lief E. Fenno, Michael S. Gold, Zachary P. Wills, Abigail K. R. Lytton-Jean, Sulagna Das, Zachary Freyberg
articles_hidden.abstract: Local protein synthesis in axons and dendrites underpins synaptic plasticity. However, the composition of the protein synthesis machinery in distal neuronal processes and the mechanisms for its deployment to local translation sites remain unclear. Here, we employed multi-scale imaging that combines cryo-electron tomography, volume electron microscopy, and live-cell imaging to identify endoplasmic reticulum-derived KDEL-positive vesicles, a subset of which are decorated with ribosomes (Ribosome-Associated Vesicles, RAVs) in neurites. We demonstrate that neuronal stimulation triggers compartment-specific responses: dendrites accumulate stationary KDEL-positive vesicles at sites of enhanced translation, while axons accelerate vesicle transport. cLTP stimulation additionally increases the proportion of KDEL-positive vesicles that carry ribosomes, expanding the local RAV pool. Real-time imaging of translation at single mRNA resolution reveals that RAV-associated translation sites exhibit ∼30% greater nascent-peptide signal amplitude compared to periods without RAV association, indicating that RAVs boost local translation output. These findings establish RAVs as specialized platforms that integrate activity-dependent signals with local protein synthesis, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding how neurons achieve precise spatiotemporal control of translation.

articles_hidden.title: Recovery and resurrection of chiral homogeneous catalysts for closed-loop recycling
articles_hidden.authors: Shiqi Liu, Najwa Arafah, Jingjun Huang, Etienne A. LaPierre, Darby E. H. Curtis, Jiajing Li, Jolene P. Reid, Thibaud Bregent, Stellios Arseniyadis, David C. Leitch
articles_hidden.abstract: Homogeneous catalysis by transition metal complexes is essential for chemical synthesis; however, these processes remain unsustainable because the catalysts are generally not recovered. We address this problem with a framework for closed-loop catalyst recycling. This approach centers on two chemical processes: stasis, where catalytic activity is selectively halted while retaining molecular integrity; and anastasis, where full catalytic function is restored. We apply this framework to recycle chiral palladium catalysts used for asymmetric allylic alkylation. ortho -Quinone oxidants drive the catalyst to converge on a discrete Pd II complex that is readily recovered, while mild reductants regenerate active Pd 0 precatalysts in a subsequent step. By rendering catalyst deactivation, isolation, and reactivation chemically addressable, this work is an important step toward circular, resource-efficient synthesis.

articles_hidden.title: TRIM28-mediated SUMOylation of ERG at K389 conveys PARP inhibitor resistance by inhibiting 53BP1 expression in CRPC
articles_hidden.authors: Shiwei Liu, Zhe Hong, Zhongyuan Wang, Yongqing Zhang, Chenye Jiang, Yuchen Jiang, Runkai Zhang, Zheng Liu, Zhi Shang, Guowen Lin, Zongyuan Hong, Bo Dai
articles_hidden.abstract: Both intrinsic and acquired resistance to poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPis) have emerged as a formidable challenge in clinical practice. Here, we report that the transcription factor E-twenty-six (Ets)-related gene ( ERG ) was highly expressed in PARPi-resistant prostate cancer and was correlated with PARPi resistance in castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) cells. ERG was posttranslationally modified by tripartite motif-containing 28 (TRIM28) as SUMOylation at lysine 389 (K389), which promotes DNA homologous recombination repair (HRR), thereby weakening the efficacy of PARPis. Mechanistically, the SUMOylation of ERG (K389) inhibited protein degradation mediated by the SPOP-mediated ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, thereby stabilizing the protein. Concurrently, this posttranslational modification increased HRR capacity by inhibiting 53BP1 expression, which in turn reduced PARPi sensitivity. Blockade of ERG K389 SUMOylation can effectively impair DNA repair efficacy and overcome PARPi resistance. These findings suggest that TRIM28-mediated ERG SUMOylation conveys resistance to PARPis by inhibiting 53BP1 expression; combined TRIM28/ERG targeting and PARPi therapy may improve outcomes for ERG-positive CRPC patients.

articles_hidden.title: In vivo screening reveals new regulators of natural killer cell development and functional response to acute cytomegalovirus infection
articles_hidden.authors: Eleanor J. Pring, Simon Clare, Roseanna Hare, Sam Sheppard, Morgan Marsden, INTREPID consortium, Mathew Clement, Lucy Chapman, Katherine Harcourt, Carmen Ballesteros Reviriego, Cordelia Brandt, Agnieszka Andres, Bushra Abu-Helil, Vivek Iyer, Louise van der Weyden, Maria A. Oliver, Paul A. Lyons, Eddie C. Y. Wang, David J. Adams, Matthew C. Cook, Daniel M. Davis, Ian R. Humphreys, Anneliese O. Speak
articles_hidden.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are critical innate immune effectors in antiviral and antitumor responses. However, the factors governing NK cell development and function remain incompletely understood. To address this, we adopted an in vivo screening approach, generating a panel of mice deficient in genes differentially expressed across NK cell maturation stages or following viral infection. We performed a combinational screen comprising baseline immunophenotyping and mouse cytomegalovirus (MCMV) challenge. We identified regulators of NK cell development, including transcriptional regulators and proteins with putative trafficking functions. MCMV challenge studies additionally identified proteins that affected antiviral immunity independently of NK cell phenotypes, including a previously undescribed regulator of NK cell degranulation, synaptotagmin-like protein 3. Identified genes exhibited a trend toward reduced tolerance to loss of function in large-scale human sequencing studies and evidence for reduced NK cell numbers in a cohort of patients with immunodeficiency. Together, these findings provide a resource of NK-expressed genes important for NK cell maturation and function, with relevance to human health.

articles_hidden.title: Intestinal BMP SMADs impart the mid-villus pattern through a transcription factor cascade mechanism
articles_hidden.authors: Alexandra Logerfo, Jahangir Iqbal, Rachel Ofer, Sneha Kandalgaonkar, Rahma Rizly, Ping He, Merilyn Anusha Gnanapragasam, Marielle Rodney, Kiranmayi Vemuri, Lei Chen, Martin Matzuk, Michael P. Verzi
articles_hidden.abstract: Differentiated cells of the intestinal villus are not a monolith of equivalent cell types, but an exquisitely patterned continuum of transdifferentiated cells with evolving functions. Villus patterning requires BMP signaling; however, the transcriptional regulators downstream of BMP are unclear. We find that SMAD1 and SMAD5 are necessary for middle villus pattern. Spatial transcriptomics reveal a homeotic-like shift in the villus pattern of SMAD1/SMAD5 mutants, with the villus bottom and tip domains expanding at the expense of the middle. Disruption of mid-villus patterning corresponds to decreases in lipid uptake and runted pups in SMAD1/5 mutants. Unexpectedly, SMAD1/5 is not required for regulation of villus tip identity, which is dependent on SMAD4. Epigenomics approaches reveal a mechanism in which SMAD1/5 directly activate some mid-villus genes and control others via a transcription factor hierarchy, including TBX3. An intestine-specific TBX3 mutant phenocopied the SMAD1/5 mutant. These findings contribute mechanistic details to intestinal villus patterning.

articles_hidden.title: Small and large earthquakes driven by inelastic deformation in weak fault zones
articles_hidden.authors: Peng Zhai, Yihe Huang, Jean-Paul Ampuero
articles_hidden.abstract: Earthquakes manifest across a wide range of magnitudes, corresponding to a diversity of rupture sizes and amounts of slip. Classical earthquake models consider rupture processes solely on the fault plane, but the surrounding fault zone rocks can host inelastic deformation. Here, we show, via a dynamic seismic cycle model incorporating spontaneous fault zone evolution through damage and healing, that both small and large earthquakes on a single fault emerge naturally from the interplay of fault slip and fault zone inelastic deformation. Our simulations reproduce key observations: frequency-magnitude distribution consistent with the Gutenberg-Richter law, magnitude-invariant static stress drop, and the dual-regime scaling of fracture energy density with earthquake magnitude. The results underscore the coevolution of earthquakes and fault zone damage as a fundamental mechanism governing earthquake behavior in nature. Fault zone deformation causing multiscale seismicity indicates that continuous monitoring of fault zone material properties may reveal fault stress states and earthquake potential.

articles_hidden.title: Machine-learning-driven identification of cooperative descriptors for polysulfide conversion on spinel oxides
articles_hidden.authors: Wen Xie, Wen Cui, Kai Tang, Shibo Xi, Zihan Shen, Longcheng Zhang, Dongshuang Wu, Zhichuan J. Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: Spinel oxides have emerged as promising catalysts for polysulfide conversion, yet a comprehensive design strategy that elucidates the underlying structure–property relationship across diverse spinel oxides remains elusive. The complex multistep conversion processes make single descriptors insufficient to capture the full catalytic behavior, whereas identifying cooperative descriptors introduces additional complexity that challenges manual analysis. Here, we employ a machine-learning–assisted approach to uncover universal cooperative descriptors and accelerate the discovery of high-performance spinel catalysts. We reveal that the intrinsic polysulfide conversion efficiency of spinel oxides is cooperatively governed by two structural features. Further screening of promising catalysts is conducted using the extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) algorithm, achieving rapid and accurate prediction of these features on spinel oxides. The model identifies Fe 2 CoO 4 and Fe 2 NiO 4 as superior catalysts, which are experimentally validated to exhibit excellent performance. This work provides deep mechanistic insights and a powerful data-driven framework for the rational design of spinel catalysts, with potential extension to other applications.

articles_hidden.title: Interband connectivity and climate shaped Neanderthal extinction and Homo sapiens ’ dispersal
articles_hidden.authors: Marco Vidal-Cordasco, Guillermo Rodríguez-Gómez, Ana B. Marín-Arroyo
articles_hidden.abstract: To what extent Neanderthal extinction was triggered by climate change or the arrival of Homo sapiens , and by which mechanisms, remains unresolved. Here, on the basis of climate-driven changes in habitat favorability for primary and secondary consumers and in net primary productivity, we estimate carrying capacity, herbivore biomass, and intraguild predation pressure during the time Neanderthals and H. sapiens lived in Europe. These spatially explicit estimates were incorporated into an agent-based model simulating human demographic dynamics under various scenarios. Results indicate that carrying capacity changes cannot explain Neanderthal extinction at a continental scale, though they are essential to understanding spatiotemporal distribution patterns of both human species. Conversely, the arrival of H. sapiens remarkably increased Neanderthal extinction likelihood. Because of the successive demographic expansions and contractions, group connectivity emerges as the key factor shaping population stability in both species. These findings support that Neanderthal disappearance and H. sapiens dispersals were interconnected demographic processes.

articles_hidden.title: Postimpact evolution of the South Pole–Aitken basin revealed by Chang’e-4 and Chang’e-6
articles_hidden.authors: Yuqi Qian, Wenlei Song, James Head, Mingyu Tian, Zhuang Guo, Harald Hiesinger, Carolyn H. van der Bogert, Le Zhang, Jingyou Chen, Wanfeng Zhang, Ziqing Li, Lingzhi Sun, Xiangsong Wang, Wei-Ran Li, Jiacheng Liu, Nicolas Dauphas, Yi-Gang Xu, Guochun Zhao
articles_hidden.abstract: South Pole–Aitken (SPA) basin has recorded complex geological histories of the Moon. It is a critical region for solving lunar fundamental questions but remained unexplored until the Chang’e-4 and Chang’e-6 missions of China. Their in situ measurements and the Chang’e-6 samples provided the first ground truth for the SPA evolution. On the basis of these constraints, we found that the SPA impact occurred ∼4.34 billion years ago, generating a thick melt sheet that differentiated to form moderately magnesium (Mg)–rich norites. They are exposed at the SPA central peaks and currently investigated by the Chang’e-4 mission in Von Kármán crater, transported by the Finsen impact to the site. Highly Mg-rich materials were found within SPA, likely products of Mg-suite magmatism, including those exposed at the Apollo western peak ring. They were initially excavated by the Apollo impact at ∼4.2 billion years ago and delivered to the Chang’e-6 site by the Chaffee S impact. A series of other events occurred in the SPA basin subsequently (e.g., the Orientale impact ∼3.87 billion years ago); all of them shaped the architecture of the Moon’s largest impact basin.

articles_hidden.title: Environment-adaptive molecular neural networks enabled by heterogeneous threshold DNA neuron
articles_hidden.authors: Xiewei Xiong, Wanhui Xu, Na Li, Sichen Xing, Ziyi Huang, Jiayi Chen, Li Li, Tong Zhu, Hao Pei
articles_hidden.abstract: Molecular neural networks enable autonomous information processing in biochemical environments, yet most existing DNA-based implementations operate with fixed connectivity after assembly, limiting their ability to adapt network topology to changing environments. Here, we report an environment-adaptive molecular neural network enabled by DNA neurons with sequence-programmed, heterogeneous activation thresholds. These neurons incorporate triplex-based proton-gated DNA switches with tunable pH-response windows, which regulate the accessibility of toehold and recognition domains to switch pre-encoded weighted connections between inactive and signal-propagating states, thereby reconfiguring network connectivity without changing molecular composition. We demonstrate this principle in a DNA neural network that processes 64-bit inputs, where environmental acidification activates dormant neurons and reconfigures the computational topology from a sparse convolutional neural network for coarse two-class categorization into a fully connected neural network for fine-grained discrimination among four distinct patterns. Our results establish DNA-based neural circuits capable of adapting their computational architecture to environmental cues, offering a framework for molecular information processing in fluctuating biochemical environments.

articles_hidden.title: TLR5 drives metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis through lipid- and flagellin-induced hepatocyte injury signaling
articles_hidden.authors: Wenhao Li, Niannian Wang, Dania El Abyad, Seray Anak, Raju Kumar, Iris Ginés, Upkar Gill, Gillian Hood, James Brindley, Charles Mein, James Boot, Una Rose Wilcox, Neil Dufton, Robert Goldin, Tania Roskams, John Loy, Kalpana Devalia, Humza Malik, Adam Goralcyzk, Maria Jimenez-Ramos, Timothy J. Kendall, Jonathan A. Fallowfield, Maria Ines Castanho Martins, Krista Rombouts, Michele Vacca, Olivier Govaere, William Alazawi
articles_hidden.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a strong predictor of clinical outcomes in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Fibrosis is a consequence of persistent liver cell injury and inflammation in which Toll-like receptors (TLRs) play a key initiating role. Here, we test the hypothesis that TLR5 is involved in the development of MASH and fibrosis using a combination of clinical data from multiple independent patient cohorts, single-cell liver transcriptomics, and human in vitro and ex vivo models. Hepatic TLR5 expression, but not TLR2 or TLR4, is associated with liver fibrosis and mortality. Plasma levels of TLR5’s cognate ligand flagellin are increased in MASH with advanced fibrosis and fall with liver disease improvement. Mechanistically, we identify two parallel TLR5-mediated routes to hepatocyte injury: one elicited by flagellin and the other indirectly by lipid injury. Furthermore, hepatocyte TLR5 inhibition abrogates paracrine activation of hepatic stellate cells to suppress collagen production. This is also seen ex vivo in patient-derived precision-cut liver slices where TLR5 inhibition significantly reduces lipid-induced collagen deposition. These findings reveal a new role for TLR5 signaling, specifically in the development of advanced MASH fibrosis and may offer a novel disease-specific therapeutic approach.

articles_hidden.title: Beyond metabolites: A wearable biointerface integrating antibody and aptamer probes for the real-time tracking of proteins in vivo
articles_hidden.authors: Hanjia Zheng, Fatima Shafique, Alexander S. Qian, Mayank Garg, Florian Gessler, Jonathan L’Heureux Hache, Quan M. Quach, Bernardo L. Trigatti, Mahla Poudineh, Leyla Soleymani
articles_hidden.abstract: Continuous monitoring of protein biomarkers could transform the management of acute and chronic diseases. Despite tremendous potential, wearable health monitors have remained largely limited to metabolites and small molecules. A key challenge is the limited availability of biointerfaces that reversibly track low-abundance proteins in vivo without user intervention. Here, we present the Differential Aptalyzer, a minimally invasive hydrogel microneedle platform for continuous monitoring of proteins in skin interstitial fluid. The platform combines high-affinity antibodies for selective target capture with aptamers for reversible electrochemical signal transduction. When integrated into a differential electrochemical chip and pulse-assisted sensor regeneration, this approach enables continuous monitoring of proteins in a wearable format. Using cardiac troponin I (cTnI) as a clinically relevant model analyte, Differential Aptalyzer offers a broad dynamic range (0.003 to 0.640 nanograms per milliliter) and strong specificity against interfering proteins. This platform reliably tracks both rising and falling exogenous cTnI levels injected into healthy mice, as well as endogenously elevated cTnI in a double-knockout mouse model of coronary artery disease, demonstrating its capability in continuous protein monitoring and identifying coronary artery disease cohorts.

articles_hidden.title: Posttranscriptional regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 controls the transcriptional program enforcing T cell quiescence
articles_hidden.authors: Ines C. Osma-Garcia, Trang-My M. Nguyen, Orlane Maloudi, Mailys Mouysset, Dunja Capitan-Sobrino, Yann Aubert, Manuel D. Diaz-Muñoz
articles_hidden.abstract: Immune protection against infections relies on long-term maintenance of a highly diversified naïve T cell repertoire. Transcription factors cooperate to enforce T cell metabolic quiescence and maintenance. However, less is known about the posttranscriptional networks that preserve naïve T cells. Here, we describe the RNA binding proteins T cell antigen 1 (TIA1) and TIA-like 1 (TIAL1) as key promoters of CD4 and CD8 T cell quiescence. T cells deficient in TIA1 and TIAL1 undergo premature T cell activation, exhaustion, and death in the absence of cognate antigens. Mechanistically, TIA1 and TIAL1 promote the messenger RNA translation of quiescence-associated transcription factors such as forkhead box P1, lymphoid enhancer factor 1, and T cell factor 1 to restrain homeostatic T cell proliferation and activation. In summary, our study highlights a previously unrecognized dependency on posttranscriptional gene regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 for implementing the quiescent transcriptional programs for long survival of T cells.

articles_hidden.title: Membrane-confined self-assembly enables localized bioorthogonal prodrug activation and selective cancer therapy
articles_hidden.authors: Wenjie Wang, Jiaxin Guo, Hong Han, Dan Yuan, Junfeng Shi
articles_hidden.abstract: Bioorthogonal prodrug activation offers a promising approach for site-specific drug release, significantly reducing the systemic toxicity associated with conventional chemotherapy. However, challenges remain in precisely controlling prodrug activation at the target site while maintaining optimal selectivity, reactivity, and potency. Here, we report a dual-targeting peptide, TzFFY p HH, that integrates on-membrane enzyme-instructed self-assembly (EISA) with bioorthogonal chemistry to enable selective chemotherapy. Exploiting the overexpression of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) on cancer cells, TzFFY p HH selectively anchors and self-assembles on the cancer cell membrane, enriching tetrazine (Tz) handles that act as bioorthogonal reactors to activate a trans -cyclooctene (TCO)-caged prodrug (TCO-Dox) for precise drug release. Upon topical administration, TzFFY p HH forms a hydrogel at subcutaneous tumor sites, enabling in situ prodrug activation for effective tumor inhibition. Notably, this localized chemotherapy elicits a potent antitumor immune response, which, when combined with anti-programmed death-1 antibody (αPD-1), synergistically potentiates therapeutic outcomes. By coupling supramolecular self-assembly with bioorthogonal reactivity on the cell membrane, this work establishes a chemically programmable platform for spatiotemporally controlled prodrug activation and provides a general strategy for integrating localized chemotherapy with immunotherapy.

articles_hidden.title: Bionic skin with hair follicle regeneration capability from acoustic fluids-mediated 3D printing
articles_hidden.authors: Xinyue Cao, Ruisi He, Zhuhao Wu, Yuanjin Zhao
articles_hidden.abstract: Tissue engineering holds substantial potential for constructing normal skin with appendages such as hair follicles, directly restoring skin’s complete physiological functions. The current challenge lies in recreating biomimetic hair follicle organs with high-level cell density and architecture. Here, we developed an acoustofluidic-assisted 3D bioprinting platform to fabricate bionic skins with efficient hair follicle regeneration capability. Pre-formed hair follicle germs, derived from co-cultured epidermal and dermal mesenchymal stem cells, were encapsulated within a hydrogel bioink. Controlled acoustic fields generated flow vortices that directed cell migration and promoted organized cellular assembly from initially disordered states. Guided cell aggregates were then patterned through bioprinting to construct a grid-structured bionic skin. This architecture provided stable 3D support while maintaining high porosity, enabling efficient gas exchange. The printed bionic skin exhibited well-organized spatial cell distribution, high cellular viability, and promising differentiation potential. Further in vivo experiments demonstrated the efficiency of the bionic skin in accelerating mature hair regeneration, showing promise for clinical alopecia treatment.

articles_hidden.title: Phonon-assisted endothermic triplet sensitization enables record NIR-II-to-visible-light photon upconversion
articles_hidden.authors: Kin Ting Chang, Pui Ying Wong, Shaokuan Gong, Aleksandr A. Sergeev, Kai Kin Li, Kam Sing Wong, Xihan Chen, Haipeng Lu
articles_hidden.abstract: Near-infrared-to-visible triplet−triplet annihilation photon upconversion (TTA-UC) enables harvesting low-energy photons; however, extending nanocrystal-sensitized TTA-UC into the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) remains challenging because triplet sensitization is thermodynamically disfavored under sub-triplet excitation. Here, we demonstrate that lead-free AgBiS 2 nanocrystals facilitate phonon-assisted endothermic triplet sensitization, enabling efficient NIR-II-to-visible upconversion. Under the sub-bandgap single-photon excitation, AgBiS 2 nanocrystals exhibit anti-Stokes photoluminescence, suggesting strong exciton−phonon coupling mediated by surface states. When coupled with 5-tetracene carboxylic acid transmitters and rubrene annihilators, AgBiS 2 achieves 980 nm-to-visible upconversion with a record quantum yield of 6.22% (normalized to 100%) and an anti-Stokes shift of 0.95 eV. Time-resolved photoluminescence and ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy support a surface-state-mediated uphill energy-transfer pathway coupled to low-frequency vibrational modes. Our work establishes phonon-assisted triplet sensitization as a strategy to overcome the NIR-II red wall for lead-free photon upconversion.

articles_hidden.title: An integrative single-cell long noncoding RNA atlas reveals regulatory programs in the pan-cancer tumor microenvironment
articles_hidden.authors: Shiting Wang, Qiheng Qian, Yuting Liu, Yang Ding, Dechang Yang, Xing Zheng, Sijin Cheng, Guoquan Huang, Ge Gao, Jingfa Xiao, Zhang Zhang, Shuai Jiang
articles_hidden.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown as critical components in cancer genomics, yet their functionality and regulation remain elusive. Here, we present an integrative lncRNA atlas covering more than 370,000 cells from 18 cancer types. In addition to multiple lineage- and cellular state transition–associated lncRNAs, we identify a set of lncRNAs that are embedded within cell type–specific regulons, suggesting associations between lncRNA expression and cell type–enriched transcriptional programs. By integrating CRISPR-based functional genomic screens and clinical data, we further prioritize not only CRISPR-supported candidate lncRNAs linked to tumor cell fitness and immune cell state features but also specific lncRNA signatures correlated with patient survival and immunotherapy response.

articles_hidden.title: Non-invasive, high-precision, and independently controllable neuromodulation via optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation
articles_hidden.authors: Kyunghyun Jo, Yeji Kim, Yeonzu Son, Joonhee Won, Woojin Jeon, Joonhyung Kwon, Hyung Jin Choi, Young-Gyun Park, Jong-Seok Kim, Seongjun Park
articles_hidden.abstract: Non-invasive neuromodulation is an important approach in clinical and translational neuroscience, yet existing techniques remain limited in precisely and flexibly targeting spatially distributed brain regions. Temporal interference stimulation (TIS) enabled non-invasive selective targeting; however, conventional implementations lack sufficient spatial focality, steerability, and scalability for network-level modulation. Here, we introduce optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation (omTIS), a computationally optimized framework that achieves high spatial focality, flexible steerability, and scalable control for distributed neuromodulation. Using a multi-electrode architecture, finite element analysis (FEA)–based optimization, and carefully selected multiple carrier frequencies, omTIS generates focal interference envelopes that can be positioned across multiple brain targets, enabling simultaneous and independently controllable multi-focal stimulation with minimal mutual interference. Across simulations, tissue-mimicking phantom experiments, and in vivo mouse studies, omTIS outperformed conventional TIS in spatial selectivity, steering flexibility, and cross-talk-free multi-focal modulation. These results establish omTIS as a scalable platform for precise, non-invasive control of distributed brain networks.

articles_hidden.title: Auditory cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulations is sufficient to support perceptual categorization of speech and music
articles_hidden.authors: Jérémie Ginzburg, Clarisse Gotti, Émilie Cloutier Debaque, Arthur Borderie, Benjamin Morillon, Laurence Martineau, Paule Lessard Bonaventure, Robert J Zatorre, Philippe Albouy
articles_hidden.abstract: Auditory processing is typically described as hierarchical, culminating in neural representation of abstract categories. However, it remains unclear whether category-selective responses in auditory cortex require representational mechanisms beyond the coding of acoustic features or whether the acoustic representations already available in the auditory cortex are sufficient to account for categorization. Here, we test whether cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulation (STM) features is sufficient to support speech-music categorization by combining human intracranial recordings with continuous behavioral judgments of a naturalistic soundtrack in which speech and music occur both separately and simultaneously. We show that temporal and spectral modulation patterns largely characterize speech and music, respectively, and that cortical auditory regions robustly track these features over time, with distinct oscillatory frequency bands preferentially encoding temporal and spectral modulations. Critically, cortical representations of STMs predicted perceptual categorical judgments gathered in an independent sample. Last, speech- and music-related STM representations showed stronger tracking of category-specific acoustical features in left versus right cortical auditory regions, respectively. These findings indicate that the efficient neural coding of acoustical features provides a sufficient basis for the categorical distinction between speech and music and that the temporal and spectral components of this representation are implemented through distinct oscillatory mechanisms.

articles_hidden.title: Nanoparticle-enabled gene delivery for pediatric brain tumors
articles_hidden.authors: Jiayuan Zhu, Helen Forgham, Yu Qin, Xiaodi Li, Xueguang Lu, Sui Wang, David S. Ziegler, Maria Kavallaris, Thomas P. Davis, Ruirui Qiao
articles_hidden.abstract: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of disease-related death in children, yet effective treatment remains a major clinical challenge. These aggressive tumors have limited therapeutic options capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and frequently recur due to genetic or epigenetic alterations and treatment resistance. Gene therapy offers a promising strategy to address these limitations by modifying gene expression, correcting mutations, or introducing functional genes. Nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems facilitate this approach by protecting genetic cargo and enabling BBB penetration and tumor-specific uptake. This review summarizes current genetic engineering strategies and NP-based delivery systems for pediatric brain tumors, including their design principles and delivery mechanisms, highlights key therapeutic approaches under preclinical and clinical investigations, and discusses the major challenges and future directions in NP-mediated gene therapy for pediatric neuro-oncology. By critically evaluating these developments, we aim to underscore the transformative potential of NP-mediated gene therapies in reshaping treatment paradigms and improving outcomes and quality of life for children.

articles_hidden.title: USP8 inhibition suppresses prostate tumorigenesis via promoting RICTOR degradation to inhibit mTORC2 signaling
articles_hidden.authors: Jingchao Wang, Daoyuan Huang, Bo Liu, Weiwei Jiang, Fabin Dang, Li Chen, Tao Hou, Peiqiang Yan, Yihang Qi, Hiroyuki Inuzuka, Lei Li, Wenyi Wei
articles_hidden.abstract: RICTOR plays an essential role in regulating mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) kinase activity, but it remains largely elusive how RICTOR is aberrantly activated in human prostate cancer (PrCa). Here, we identify RICTOR as a substrate of Cullin 3–based ubiquitin ligase adaptor SPOP, an important tumor suppressor in PrCa. SPOP deficiency or cancer-derived SPOP mutations disrupt SPOP-mediated degradation of RICTOR, thereby promoting PrCa progression. Furthermore, we identify USP8 as its upstream deubiquitinase, and inhibition of USP8 specifically suppresses RICTOR/mTORC2 activity without affecting mTORC1. As such, the USP8 inhibitor induces RICTOR degradation concomitant with marked tumor suppression in vivo. Hence, these findings reveal an SPOP-USP8-RICTOR regulatory circuit that underlies PrCa tumorigenesis and provides a rationale for targeting RICTOR via USP8 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for patients with PrCa.

articles_hidden.title: Reconciling the medical relevance of mitochondrial transplantation in vivo
articles_hidden.authors: Eaman Abay, Joan Sanchez-Gurmaches, Jeffery D. Molkentin
articles_hidden.abstract: Mitochondria transplantation is a proposed therapeutic approach to improve the function of diseased or injured tissue. It has garnered attention and sparked debate.

articles_hidden.title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
articles_hidden.authors: Jiaxin Wu, Hongzhuo Wu, Zuhong Zhang, Xiaoyu Guan, Jinbo Zhao, Yuting Guo, Zhihao Li, Zirui Li, Tengyu Ma, Ying Tang, Zhe Li, Weiwei Zuo, Jorge Pascual, Bo Hou, Feng Yang, Xiaoli Pan, Yu Wang, Luyao Wang, Lin-Long Deng, Guixiang Li, Luca Sapienza, Antonio Abate, Meng Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl − induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between −40 and 85°C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

articles_hidden.title: Structure and dynamics of the cellular belt driving bacterial gliding motility
articles_hidden.authors: Hanxiong Liu, Yaëlle Aouizerate, Xiangan Liu, Zihe Zhang, Caterina Comas Hervada, Yongtao Zhu, Maxence S. Vincent, Eric Cascales, Bo Hu, Thierry Doan
articles_hidden.abstract: Various bacteria move on solid surfaces through a process known as gliding motility. Gliding bacteria of the phylum Bacteroidota are major ecological players in a wide variety of niches, as commensals or as pathogens. They use the type IX secretion system (T9SS) to transport adhesins to the cell surface, which then travel in a helical pattern to propel the cell. Here, we purified the filament that drives adhesin helical movement and uncovered its structure by cryo–electron microscopy. Live imaging showed that this outer membrane–associated periplasmic belt, built from T9SS core components, is powered by T9SS molecular motors. This structure functions as a moving walkway that conveys outer membrane β barrel protein–adhesin complexes, therefore coupling motor activity to directional surface translation. This study reveals a unique machinery coupling protein secretion with rapid directed movement of membrane-embedded protein complexes.

articles_hidden.title: A state-dependent neural circuit resolves approach-avoidance conflict
articles_hidden.authors: Devika Bodas, Şevval Demirci, Olga Procenko, Marine Balcou, Lennart Baumeister, Darryl Segal, Lisa Scheunemann, Carolina Rezaval
articles_hidden.abstract: To survive, animals must balance opportunity and risk, yet how internal motivational state biases this trade-off remains poorly understood. Here, we show that hunger gates avoidance of a noxious stimulus in Drosophila to enable food approach under conflict. Using a behavioral assay in which flies must cross an electric shock barrier to reach food, we find that starvation promotes shock tolerance only when food-related olfactory cues are present. This state- and context-dependent behavioral shift is mediated by a defined neuromodulatory circuit. Leucokinin neurons encode hunger and convey this information to PV5K1 lateral horn output neurons, which integrate internal state signals with food odor cues and suppress shock-responsive FB2B neurons in the ventral fan-shaped body.
